  `control.lua` has `install_limits`; on an older world `fh deploy` refuses a larger bundle before sending anything and
  says to restart the world with the current mod.
- The deployed code is stored in the save and takes priority over the mod's `runtime.lua`. For an existing save, edits only take effect after a deploy.
- A runtime error quarantines the runtime. Read-only calls still work until a fixed deploy succeeds.
- Module top-level code must not touch the game. Persistent state goes in `storage.agent_harness`.
- Changing prototypes or `control.lua` still needs a game reload.

- `preflight {position, items, from}` also reads one source chest position or up to 16 in sight/remote view.
  `from` lists each distinct chest and its stock of each requested item/quality. The existing `order` rows add
  `kg`, `slots`, `from_held`, `from_short` (what the chests lack after cargo already aboard) and `short` (also less
  what you hold). `manifest` reports the requested list's kg/slots, the silo's lift/cargo slots, and `after_kg`,
  `after_slots`, `fits` for the whole list after topping up existing cargo, including unrelated cargo already aboard.
  These combined limits differ from the individual `order[].fits` checks. No cargo moves. Discovery without a silo
  position includes the same manifest and source checks for each visible silo.
- `supply {item}` and `science` count stock on our platforms stopped over the planet (d15 trajectory analysis: Grok's
  102 calcite sat on Starling over Nauvis while the artillery ran out of shells): `supply` adds `in_orbit: in orbit on
  Starling 102 (platform hubs stopped over nauvis; a drop brings it down)` and the same words at the end of `where`;
  each `science` pack line ends with `; in orbit on Starling 40`. It reads the hub's main inventory; a platform in
  flight or over another planet is left out.
- `supply {item}` adds `belt_lines` (Muse, Grok, d15 07:50: supply said coal 1001 on belts and the backed-up line took
  128-wide scans to find): the belt tiles holding the item joined into lines (tiles side by side that hold it; an empty
  tile or an underground's two ends split a line), the 5 holding the most first: `412 on 52 belt tiles
  (12.5,30.5)-(63.5,30.5); most 8 at (40.5,30.5); out end (63.5,30.5) 8, in end (12.5,30.5) 6` (out: its items move on
  to no belt of the line; in: nothing of the line feeds it; up to 4 ends, the fullest first), then `N more belt lines
  hold M`. Up to 4096 belt tiles are listed; the `belts` total counts every one.
  `belt_positions: true` (d26 batch221) adds those lines' tiles from the same scan, and `belt_tiles` reads fixed
  tiles later (the d26 batch221 section).
- `supply {item}` adds `surplus_chest`: the largest unreserved stock among plain, storage and provider chests,
  excluding requesters and buffers. It includes position, kind, held, reserved for robot pickups, and free; this
  does not reserve the stock or assert that no inserter uses it. It is independent of the largest-five chest list.
- Full `status` warnings recheck up to three recorded egg sites within 64 tiles of your character: enemies visible
  within 16 tiles now, the recorded first-hatch timer (future or elapsed), and visible gun turrets within 64 tiles
  whose range covers the site, with ammo and inactive state. An elapsed timer is not evidence of a hatch. Old timer
  sites are retained for ten minutes; enemies can have moved, and eggs can have been consumed or carried away.
  The bounded reads show their check tick and report caps (33 enemies, 65 guns); brief status does not run them.


### 04:50 build, transfer and fuel facts

- A queue `transfer` step accepts `min_moved: 1` **on the step**, alongside `action` and `args`:
  `{"action":"transfer","args":{"position":{"x":14.5,"y":140.5},"direction":"to_entity","item":"iron-plate","count":100},"min_moved":1}`.
  The integer range is 1..10000 and `wait` must be true (the default). The scheduler checks reported `moved` or
  `transferred` after completion, including walks and craft waits. A lower count or an unknown count fails the
  step with the observed count and uses its existing `on_fail` policy (abort, skip, goto). This requirement also
  applies with `up_to:true` or `on_short:"skip"`. Without it, existing short-transfer behavior is unchanged.
  Counts are the action's reported total, across targets and courier legs, not a guarantee that items remain in
  the destination. A failed minimum does not roll back items already moved.
- `inspect` (full and compact) and `trace` feeder/taker reads add `held_blocked` or a corresponding line when an
  inserter holds an item that its current drop target cannot accept even one of now. The fact names the inserter,
  item, quality, target and current recipe when present. It reports current refusal, which can be full inventory
  or incompatibility; it does not claim the blockage is permanent. Belt targets and unavailable reads are omitted;
  an out-of-sight target is not queried for acceptance. No additional entity scan is made.
- Full `status` adds one `boilers` line from the completed network cache: boilers under 20 minutes of their own
  fuel at their equal share of sampled generator draw, up to six positions with their already-read feeder chest
  and fuel contents (or feeder description), the count unlisted and sample age. Boilers with fuel at their feeders
  still appear when their own fuel is below the threshold. Missing samples/draw estimates are explicit. The line
  performs no new scan; brief status omits it. Existing `boilers`, `game_alerts kind=boiler_fuel`, `networks` and
  `team.science` retain their fuller reads and alert conditions.
- `feed`, `refuel` and walking transfers already use `move_to`'s enemy corridor planner and per-leg path checks.
  They now retain up to eight `last.route_failures` before skipping unreachable stops: the stop position, avoidance
  reason and `smaller_margins` with the largest verified smaller margin or the diagnostic's budget/failure fact.
  `first_unreached` also includes that line, and compact `--wait` keeps these facts. No smaller margin is chosen
  automatically, and there is no promise that a route exists. A stop inside enemy reach remains subject to the
  existing goal check; `unsafe_goal` and `avoid_enemies` keep their existing meanings.
- Platform `build` / `place_ghosts` dry runs add `pump_circuits` for pumps in the plan with an enable condition but
  no currently connected circuit network. Conditions declared in the entry and existing built pump conditions
  count. Red/green wires declared from either endpoint are named as planned, not yet connected; copper wires and
  disconnect declarations do not count as new circuit connections. This reads at most 64 planned pump
  positions (further pumps counted as unchecked), not a full-platform circuit audit or a proof that a declared wire will connect. Existing `circuit`
  and `circuit_set` reads already report `enable_ignored` for an enabled condition without a circuit connection.

## d15 batch3 (operator 18:30, shifts 18-19)

- Full chests (Astra, Luna: Gleba's nutrient, yumako and bioflux providers had 48/48 slots used, mostly spoilage,
  and the machines feeding them stopped): `supply {item}` adds `full_chests`, the chests with every slot used that
  the item's makers' output inserters wait on or that hold the item: `passive-provider-chest (10.5,4.5): 48/48 slots
  used (spoilage 4000 in 40 slots, nutrients 240 in 8 slots); output waits on it: biochamber (7.5,4.5) full_output
  (1 inserter waiting)`. Its `chests` rows add each non-requester chest's free slots (`, 0/48 slots free`).
  `bottleneck {item}` adds the chest to a not-working maker stopped by its output (`; output into ... 48/48 slots
  used (...)`) and lists those chests in `full_chests`. `open for you` counts full chests in your fresh claims that
  a full_output machine's output waits on. `inspect` of such a chest adds `slots_used`, `output_waits` and
  `free_chests_near` (the nearest 3 chests of ours within 32 tiles with a free slot).
- Heat (Sol: reclaiming "spare" heat pipes twice froze an ammonia underground pipe and the only steam turbine on
  Aquilo): `mine {position, dry_run: true}` on an entity mines nothing and reads `heat_loss`; `deconstruct` (dry run
  and live) reads it for the heat-network parts it marks; a live `mine` of a heat part carries it when it is not
  `none`. `heat_loss.cut_off`: the heat-network parts (by the engine's heat links) whose part of the network keeps no
  nuclear reactor or heating tower without the removed ones (`1 heat-network part cut off from every nuclear reactor
  and heating tower (1 heat-pipe; first at (5.5,1.5)); they keep their heat and cool`). `heat_loss.freeze` (a surface
  whose entities need heating): freezable entities beside a removed heater, or beside a cut-off one, that keep no
  heater at 30 C or more (`pipe-to-ground (4.5,2.5): loses its last heater at 30 C or more (heat-pipe (4.5,1.5) 270
  C)`, or `keeps only heaters cut off from every reactor and heating tower, which cool`). Up to 64 freezable
  entities are read; a heat network is followed up to 2000 parts.
- Gun and ammo slots (Grok: a pistol in gun slot 1 and 75 piercing rounds in ammo slot 2; gun slot N fires only from
  ammo slot N): `inventory` (and `status {inventory: true}`) gives `guns` and `ammo` per slot (`1 pistol, 2 empty, 3
  empty (selected: 1)`, `1 empty, 2 piercing-rounds-magazine*75, 3 empty`) and `ammo_idle` for ammo whose gun slot
  does not fire it (`ammo slot 2 piercing-rounds-magazine*75: gun slot 2 is empty; it fits gun slot 1 pistol, which
  fires only from its own ammo slot`). `shoot`'s `no_compatible_ammo` names compatible ammo in other ammo slots and
  the gun slot beside each. `equip {slot: ammo, item}` moves ammo held only in the ammo slots: to `index`, or beside
  the selected gun when it fits it, else beside the first gun it fits (`moved_from`, `swapped`, `fired_by`). `equip`
  without `slot` takes it from the item's kind.
- `blueprint_save` and `blueprint_capture` take `platform=NAME` (Astra, cloning platform Starling into a new platform
  Swift): they capture on that space platform by remote view, in platform coordinates (hub at 0,0), as `paste` and
  `blueprint_place` already place there. Aboard a platform they act on it as before.
- Route preview (Haiku died on a 500-tile move_to with `avoid_enemies {distance: 12}` past big worms of range 38;
  Luna walked into an enclosed core twice): `move_to {..., dry_run: true}` walks nothing (a read). It reads the
  route now, without the engine's pathfinder: `route` and `length` (straight lines through the via points, round the
  worms and spawners the map shows as a walk plans its legs), `enemies` (each worm, spawner and area under attack
  within reach: `big-worm-turret (250,0) range 38: closest pass 14 tiles at (251,14) (24 inside it)`, nearest its
  range first, up to 8), `reachable`, `closed_in_start` / `closed_in_goal` (no way out within 24 tiles) with
  `mine_for_a_way_in` (the fewest of our entities, trees or rocks to mine, the first met first), and `unsafe_goal`
  (said instead of refused). `feed`, `collect`, `transfer`, `rearm` and `refuel` take `dry_run: true` with positions:
  the same read through the stops, nearest first from you (radius and area tours choose their stops when they run).
  With `avoid_enemies {distance: N}`, `under_range` names the worms on the route whose range is more than N, on the
  dry run and on a live move_to's reply.
- Collect and output inserters (Sol: twice `collect {positions, item, count, wait_ticks}` waited while inserters moved
  every lithium plate into an output chest): a wait at a machine says `taken_by_inserters` (`1 inserter takes
  lithium-plate from its output as it is made: fast-inserter (5.5,-3.5) into steel-chest (6.5,-3.5) (holds 340
  lithium-plate)`; an inserter whose filter keeps the item out is left out) and `follow_chests`. `follow: true` with
  `wait_ticks` or `keep_taking` takes from the chests those inserters fill when they hold the item, instead of
  waiting (`followed` says so; none holding it: the wait at the machine). `collect {positions, dry_run: true}` adds
  `outputs_taken` for each machine among the positions.
- Build dry runs (Astra: a Fulgora roboport's dry run named the accumulators and a pole in its way; after mining them
  the build met shallow oil): an entry blocked by entities also says the tiles it needs (`tiles: stands on 4
  oil-ocean-shallow tiles: needs 4 foundation first`). On a platform, a ghost or build refused over empty space says
  whether foundation tile ghosts stand under it not built yet (`placement blocked by tiles: empty-space under it, with
  tile ghosts of space-platform-foundation at (15,-2) not built yet: the game's ghost check refuses this entity's
  ghost while they are ghosts, and takes it once the foundation under it is built ...`) or that no foundation or
  foundation ghost is there. The shore hint is only given for water tiles.
- Route preview limits (measured on a copy of world n): a dry run reads at most 128 map chunks for worms and
  spawners a call (`unread_chunks` names the rest, the farthest; the chunks read are kept a minute, so the same dry
  run again reads the next ones), plans each leg round the nests near it only, and plans at most 72 discs a leg and a
  call (`not_planned_round` names the legs read as straight lines). A goal with no spot to stand within a tile (deep
  water, a building) reads `reachable: no: no spot to stand at the goal`.
- Queues (Muse, Luna):
  - Each history entry keeps the arguments its step ran with, and a finished loop keeps its steps.
    `queue_status {args: true}` shows them, so a finished plan or a 40-round loop can be submitted again. Without
    `args` the replies are as small as before.
  - While a timed transfer, collect, feed, rearm or refuel tour, or a courier (`pick` with `to`), walks, status
    `active.progress` reads `stop 2 of 3 (steel-chest (6,8)), 10 tiles to it, 22 tiles left in all; moved 40
    iron-plate so far` (a courier: `leg N of M ...; took 50, delivered 0`).
  - A queued transfer or feed tour interrupted by a direct action is requeued with the stops it had not finished.
    A courier whose take is done is requeued as the give at its destination with what it still carries. The history
    entry says `resumed_from`. Before, such a step failed whole.
- Small ones (item 8):
  - `deconstruct {area, cancel: true}` cancels the deconstruction marks there, as `cancel_deconstruction` does
    (`cancelled`). A plain deconstruct says `already_marked` when some were marked before (Grok).
  - A build or place_ghosts dry run gives each pump's `ports`, blocked or not: each tile it joins, one past its body,
    and what stands there, with whether it connects back (`output north at (130.5,40.5), one tile past the body: pipe
    (130.5,40.5) (connects back); input south at (130.5,43.5), one tile past the body: nothing`) (Grok).
  - A build on lava says the tile first: `lava-hot (unbuildable: lava; only foundation laid on it makes it buildable,
    and that is not researched)` (Sonnet).
  - A fast replace of an inserter keeps the stack its hand holds in the new inserter's hand. A hand stack that would
    need inventory room is named in the refusal with the rest that does not fit (Sonnet).
  - supply's `chests` rows add what robots have reserved for pickup in each provider, storage or plain chest. When
    all of it is reserved, `surplus_chest` names the largest such chest as `all reserved for robot pickups` instead
    of leaving it out (Haiku).
- Artillery (Grok lost a turret to biters that came after the artillery woke a nest): each row of `artillery` adds
  `units_near`. These are the enemy units within 64 tiles of the piece that our force sees now: the count by name,
  and for the 5 nearest the distance, its attack range and how far outside it the piece stands, and how many of our
  turrets reach it (`big-spitter (20,0) 20 tiles away, its range 13 (7 outside it); 1 turret of ours reaches it`).
  The row's line says the same.
- platform_endurance (leftovers from d15 blockers):
  - Flying on a leg under 10 minutes old, the rates come from the largest window that fits inside the leg (5 or 1
    minute, `rate_from: last 1 min, within this leg (3m00s so far)`), so the stop it left no longer dilutes them.
    Ammunition comes from the leg's own counts (`this leg so far, 3m00s`).
  - The ingredient cap goes two levels down: an ingredient the machines aboard make is counted with what they can
    still make of it from their own ingredients aboard (`explosives 10 aboard and at most 8 more from its own
    ingredients aboard (sulfuric-acid 80)`). A fluid ingredient is counted in the storage tanks and in the makers'
    fluid boxes (`ingredient_limited.fluid`, `ingredient_limited.below`).
  - `tools/read_cost.py` has `platform_endurance` (`--platform NAME`, default Aegis) and `artillery`.

## d15 batch4 (operator 21:25; shifts 19-20)

- `trace {position, upstream: true}` (Sol, Luna, Astra, Grok: Starling drifted backwards ~8 min while an arm at
  (9.5,2.5) sent all its ore onto a furnace belt; Swift's ammo starved behind a jammed mixed return; Grok walked a coal
  tour while coal sat on the copper ore lane): from the target back along what feeds it. Per ingredient it lacks
  (`all: true`: every one; `item`: that one), `ingredients[] {item, has, needs, line, feeders, lanes, makers}`:
  - a feeder whose filter does not let it through, or that is off by its circuit condition (the condition and the
    signal on its wires, as thrust reads it);
  - each lane a feeder picks, walked back tile by tile through undergrounds, splitters and side-loads
    (`lanes[] {from, at_feeder, jammed, path_back, line}`). The line says, in the order items move: an inserter
    taking it elsewhere first (onto another belt, into a chest, into a machine with another recipe; its status,
    filter and what it holds; inserters feeding machines like the target are counted), the first tile back where it
    is on the lane, where it comes onto the lane (an inserter and what it reads, a drill, a side-loading belt), the
    first tile where another item joins and from what (`which it burns as fuel` when the target does), a splitter
    filter sending it to the other output, and where the walk ended (the lane's start, out of sight, the cap);
  - `jammed`: the lane at the feeder full with none of it (`the left lane at transport-belt (15.5,2.5) is full and
    holds no iron-ore (left lane 4 coal, right lane empty), front item coal`);
  - a chest a feeder reads with none: what fills it; a machine making it that is not working: traced the same way one
    level down (`makers`).
  - A thruster: each fluid by pipe and pump (thrust.lua's walk) to the machines making it, each traced as above, so
    oxidizer goes back through its iron ore belt to the crushers and their chunk belt to the collectors. A machine's
    fluid ingredient it lacks goes the same way (water to the ice melting plant).
  - A hub, chest or belt tile with no `item`: every lane feeding it, with the items coming onto it, first first.
  - Bounds: 800 belt tiles, 500 a lane, 16 lane walks, two machine levels. `cost` says what it walked. Measured on a
    copy of world n in a private 2.0.77 container: 184 tiles back along the south copper line 21 ms there (about 4 ms
    on n), Swift's oxidizer plant with every ingredient (6 lanes, the ice melter one level down) 18 ms.
  - `line` gives each ingredient's first problem per lane (a jam, a taker elsewhere, a splitter filter, no source
    found); `lanes[].line` has every finding.
  - A requester or buffer chest a feeder reads names its request (`a requester chest requesting 40 (robots fill
    it)`). An inserter that would take it elsewhere but is off by its circuit condition is named as off.
- `power {position, fragile: true, radius?}` (Opus: one small pole at (-72.5,-114.5) cut 142 poles of oil and drills;
  NW oil lost its one link pole twice): the network of the pole nearest `position` (within 12 tiles), its poles within
  `radius` (8..512, default 96) and their copper wires.
  - Sources: a pole covering a generator of the network (steam engine or turbine, solar panel, fusion or burner
    generator), and the network beyond the radius when a wire leaves it (`wires_out`). Centre an outpost read on the
    outpost and its link to the base counts as power.
  - `fragile` (the 8 cutting most; `fragile_total` all): each pole whose loss leaves a group of poles with no source,
    and the machines only that group and the pole cover: `small-electric-pole (20,0): its loss cuts 3 poles and 3
    machines (2 electric-mining-drill, 1 pumpjack) around (30.5,6.5), from (20,1) to (41,12), off from all
    generation`. The one pole covering the only generator is listed too.
  - A pole whose loss cuts only machines in its own supply area is not a cut of the network and is not listed.
  - `unreached`: poles of it in the area with no wire path to a source now. Bounded: 200 supply-area
    searches (`cost`). Machines are counted for the 16 cuts with the most poles; the 1000 poles nearest are read and
    wires to the rest count as power (`capped`). Measured on the copy of world n in the container: 297 poles 20-27 ms
    there (about 5 ms on n), 1000 poles (radius 512 round Opus's oil pole) 78-82 ms (about 16 ms on n).
- Personal requests (Haiku: 10 repair packs at south copper (-10,562) never came; Muse): `requests` for the character
  adds `unfilled`, one line per request whose held plus on-the-way count is under its min, with the first reason
  that holds:
  - personal logistics switched off;
  - no slot of the character takes the item (main inventory full, its free slots filtered to other items; d20 batch59
    U1);
  - no logistic network where the character stands;
  - the network has no logistic robots;
  - the network holds none of the item robots can take;
  - all its logistic robots are busy;
  - robots are bringing some;
  - the network holds it and has free robots, and none has taken it yet.
  - Example: `repair-pack: hold 0 of 10; logistic network 120 where you stand has no logistic robots (its roboports
    hold none)`, read on a copy of world n as Haiku.
  - Alert (team.alerts): a personal request unfilled for 60 s or more in a network with 0 logistic robots. Checked
    every 5 s an agent replies; told once per network and item, and again after 10 minutes.
  - What a request counts (d20 batch59 U1, Astra #1480: firearm-magazine and rocket read `hold 0 of 100; network 348
    holds 4039 and has 176 of 190 logistic robots free; none has taken it yet` for 25 minutes, 04:13-04:38 in
    shift49, while her ammo slots held 100 of each; the game had nothing to send). Checked on 2.0.77 on the private
    copy:
    - ammo slots count: sol with 10 firearm-magazine in them got nothing for min 10 and 6 for min 15;
    - gun slots count: 1 pistol held, nothing for min 1, 1 for min 2;
    - worn armor counts: gemini wearing modular-armor got 1 for min 2.
    - So the line counts the main inventory, gun, ammo and armor slots, and says where:
      `firearm-magazine: hold 19 of 30 (19 in ammo slots) (1 on the way); ...`.
    - With every free slot filtered to wood, sol got no pipe for min 5; with one slot cleared, 6 were on the way
      within 6 s. The line says `no slot of yours takes pipe`.
    - With personal logistics off, the requester point's `logistic_network` reads as an invalid object; so does
      grok's on Gleba on the copy. Both read as no network now; before, every call on it failed and the line said
      "has no logistic robots".
- `character_settings {personal_logistics?, personal_roboport?, movement_bonus?, filters?}` (d20 batch59 U1, Astra
  #1480 for viewer Foobator17928). The character GUI's switches and the main inventory's slot filters, read and
  written as a player sets them.
  - The 2.0.77 fields, read and written on the private copy:
    - personal logistics: the character requester point's `enabled` (the master switch of the requests; the
      sections' own switches stay `requests {section, active}`);
    - the personal roboport: the character's `allow_dispatching_robots`;
    - the equipment movement bonus: the armor grid's `inhibit_movement_bonus` (on = not inhibited);
    - slot filters: the main inventory's `set_filter`/`get_filter`. The API also sets a filter for another item on
      a slot that holds one, which a player's middle-click does not do, so that is refused (`slot 2 holds radar*1: a
      slot that holds an item takes a filter for that item only`). An empty slot takes any item's filter.
  - `filters: [{slot, item, quality?}]`, 1..200 entries; `item: false` clears the slot's filter.
  - Every argument is checked before anything changes, and an edit changes only what it names.
  - `changed` lists each change, e.g. `personal roboport on -> off`, `slot 1 filter none -> stone-brick`. When
    nothing named differed, `unchanged` says so.
  - Every reply is the read after the edit: `personal_logistics`, `personal_roboport`, `movement_bonus` (on/off,
    noting no roboport or no exoskeleton in the armor), `filters` (each filtered slot with what it holds; 40 at most,
    `filters_more` counts the rest) and `filters_line`. Runs of empty slots with one filter read as one, e.g. `90
    slots filtered: 1-90 wood (empty); 0 of 90 slots free (empty and unfiltered)`.
  - `networks` gives:
    - `logistic`: the network the requests go to, or the one whose area covers the character while personal logistics
      are off;
    - `construction`: the roboport networks whose construction area covers the character;
    - `personal_roboport`: count, switch, construction radius, construction robots in the main inventory and out
      now, energy;
    - `not_dispatched`: what the game shows stops robots now (roboport off, no robot to send, no energy, personal
      logistics off, no free slot);
    - `unfilled`, as `requests` gives it.
  - Passive: it leaves the character's action and queue alone, as `requests` does.
  - Real engine (private copy, bot gemini, with a personal roboport): all three switches off with slots 1 and 100
    filtered, then all back on, each read back; a filter for iron-plate on slot 2, which holds a radar, was refused,
    with nothing changed.
  - Tests: tests/d20_batch59.lua U1.
- Burner fuel alert (Opus: 30 stone furnaces ran out of coal and copper fell from 1000 to 560 a minute). team.alerts
  names a group of burner machines that no inserter brings fuel to (fed by hand or by order) when they will run dry
  within 10 minutes: `stone-furnace near (108,-168), fed by hand or by order (no inserter brings them fuel): 21 run dry
  within 10 min at full use (coal; the first in about 3 min)` (on a copy of world n).
  - A background pass goes over the census's fuel users: furnaces, burner drills, burner assemblers, heating towers and
    burner generators. Boilers have their own alert in the networks view, and burner inserters are left out. It reads
    24 machines a second.
  - Minutes left: the fuel slots' fuel value plus the rest of the item burning, over the burn at full use (energy use
    with the consumption bonus, over the burner's effectivity).
  - Fed by an inserter: one dropping into it holds a fuel item, reads a belt, chest or output holding one, or is
    filtered to one. This is read again every 5 minutes.
  - Groups are by name and 64-tile cell. A group is told once, and again after 10 minutes if still so. `out of fuel
    now` counts only machines the pass saw working with fuel before.
  - Cost on the copy: 49 ms in 60 s in the container, at most 1.8 ms a step (about 0.4 ms on n).
- Requester and buffer chests (Sonnet: hours of starvation twice).
  - A hand `transfer` or `feed` into one adds to `delivery_note` what the game does with that item now.
  - Over the request's max: `iron-plate: the chest holds 100, over its request max 20: the game moves the 80 over it to
    the chest's trash slots, and robots carry them to storage`.
  - With trash unrequested on: an item with no max, over its min, goes the same way, and so does an item the chest
    does not request at all.
  - An item it does not request, with trash unrequested off, stays in its slots.
  - Seen on a 2.0.77 copy of world n: a chest asking 10..20 iron plate given 100 kept 20 and moved 80 to its trash, and
    robots took 78 within seconds. With trash unrequested on, copper plate with no max fell to its min of 10, and the
    coal went to the trash.
  - One item in every slot while the chest requests others it lacks: `one item fills every slot: stone 2400 in all 48
    slots (it does not request it), so iron-plate, copper-plate cannot come in; put in by ...`. This appears in that
    delivery note, in `inspect` (`one_item`), and in the `requester_full` alert line in place of the slot list.
- Platform arrival before departure (Sonnet, every shift: "no estimate" until the ship left). A `wait_until
  {until: platform_arrived, platform, location}` estimate for a platform stopped at a location now reads its
  schedule:
  - the current stop's wait conditions, with the seconds left on a time condition (counted from when the stop began);
  - each leg to `location` at the platform's last flying speed (freight.lua keeps it once a second while it flies);
  - the time conditions of the stops between.
  - Example: `ETA 175s before departure: leaves gleba when time 60s; gleba->nauvis 15000 km at 120 km/s (its last
    speed): 125s`.
  - A wait that is not a time condition (all requests satisfied, a circuit condition, ...) is named, not timed: `ETA
    175s after gleba: all_requests_satisfied: ...`, with no `eta_s`. Conditions joined by `or` give `at most` the
    shortest time condition.
  - Without `location`: the next stop.
  - No estimate: a paused platform, a schedule that does not go there, or no flying speed seen yet.
- Silo automatic launch (Muse, twice: Starling asked 50 low-density-structure and no rocket went up). With automatic
  requests on, the silo read adds `auto_waits`; the harness does not change the rule.
  - What was seen on a 2.0.77 copy of world n: the silo's own logistic request asked its network for a full rocket by
    weight (200 low-density-structure at 5 kg each). It did so both for a platform asking 50 with no max and for one
    asking 400..400 holding 350, and the rocket went up once it held about 200. With 16-30 low-density-structure in
    its network the silo took up no platform; with 320 it filled a rocket and launched.
  - Filling: `filling a rocket for Starling: low-density-structure 14 of 200 aboard (a full rocket by weight, 5 kg
    each); its network holds 30 more, under the 186 it still waits for; ...`.
  - No platform taken up: `no platform taken up now; above nauvis: Starling asks low-density-structure 50 (holds 0);
    the silo's network holds 30, a full rocket of it is 200 by weight`.
- `equip {slot: "ammo", unequip: true, index?, item?}` (Grok: a rocket ride refused ammo in the ammo slots, and equip
  could only put ammo in) moves that slot's stacks back to the main inventory (`unequipped`). What does not fit stays
  and is named in `left`. `slot: "gun"` does the same for guns.
- A ride refused for items it carries names them and, for the ammo slots, how to clear them: `only armor and guns
  travel with the rider: character_ammo holds firearm-magazine*10; equip {slot: "ammo", unequip: true} moves them to
  your main inventory; a transfer {position, direction: "to_entity", item} into a chest takes from the ammo slots too`.
- `fh ... --wait` that ends with exit 3 (a tell, a mention or the wait timeout while the action still runs) also writes
  to stderr: `still running (exit 3): transfer goes on after this wait ended (a walk keeps walking); fh wait resumes
  waiting for it`.
- `train {stops: true, surface?}` (Gemini, 21:40: no call listed the train stops) lists every train stop of ours on the
  surface, by name: position, the rail beside it, limit, `trains_count`, and the trains heading there or stopped at it
  (`train 13 at it (front (-43,96))`). It gives at most 200, and reads `game.train_manager.get_train_stops` and
  `get_trains` once each.
- Transfer and feed dry runs (Luna: timed walks to a machine that did not take the item). `transfer {positions,
  direction: "to_entity", item, dry_run: true}` and `feed {..., dry_run: true}` add `accepts`, one line per stop (at
  most 16). It is read now, with the inventory a hand move would pick:
  - `yes: stone-furnace (-26,-45) takes coal into fuel`;
  - `no: assembling-machine-2 (x,y) recipe iron-gear-wheel takes iron-plate, not copper-plate`;
  - `no: stone-furnace (-26,-45) makes nothing from iron-gear-wheel (no recipe of its crafting categories takes it)`;
  - `no: electric-furnace (-52.5,-73.5) furnace_source is full: all 1 slots taken (iron-ore 3 in 1 slot)`;
  - a furnace holding another ore: `refuses ... now (its recipe copper-plate; a furnace switches recipe only once its
    source is empty)`;
  - a filter or an inventory that does not take it, and an assembler with no recipe.
- `from: "nearest"` names a requester or buffer chest with its request for the item (`a requester chest requesting 200
  nutrients: robots bring it there for that request`). Such chests stay left out unless `feeding: true`, and come
  after the others then. supply's chest rows already give a requester's request and a provider's robot reservations.
- `move_to` through `via` points that ends short (Opus: the NE uranium route, 4 times) names the leg: `failed_leg`
  `leg 4 of 6 (to (20,150))`. The why line, which the error line shows, starts with it and ends with the smaller-margin
  result.
  - `smaller_margins` on a via chain verifies every leg left (the failed leg's goal, the via points after it and the
    final position) at each smaller margin. The line gives `largest smaller integer margin with a verified route: 3
    (avoid_enemies 3); the 3 legs left in the via chain ...`, with `legs`.
  - With `avoid_enemies {distance: N}` it tries smaller distances down to 4 (`largest_verified_distance`; before, it
    verified nothing for a distance).
- Repeating loops walk into reach (Muse, twice: a hand haul left the character elsewhere and the loop's collect failed
  out of reach, past the 32 tiles a call walks by default). In a `queue_repeat` loop, a transfer, collect, feed, rearm
  or refuel step that names `position` or `positions` and gives no `walk` runs with `walk: true`, as a transfer with
  `walk: true` does. `walk: false` on the step keeps it from walking. `from: "nearest"` steps and `queue_submit` plans
  are unchanged.
- A remote recipe change on a platform machine holding items (Astra, twice: a deconstruct and rebuild instead, and
  during the gap an unfiltered feeder grabbed magazines and stayed jammed). `configure {platform, position, recipe}`
  now moves its input and output stacks, then what the recipe change returns (the ingredients of a craft under way),
  into the platform hub, and reports them as `to_hub`.
  - On a copy of world n, a crusher on Swift changed from metallic to oxide crushing: `to_hub {iron-ore: 48,
    metallic-asteroid-chunk: 2}`.
  - The hub must have an empty slot for each stack (and one per ingredient of a craft under way). Otherwise the
    refusal names the hub's empty slots, and nothing changes.
  - Fluids still need `force: true`, as before.
- `cargo {items: [...], one_rocket: true}` (Sol: 375 explosives and 50 low-density-structure make 1000 kg, hard to find
  from separate reads) loads one rocket from the list in its order: each item as many as still fit by weight and
  slots. It returns `items` with kg, `kg`, `slots`, `room_kg`, `room_slots`, `left_over` and a line: `one rocket:
  explosives 375 (750 kg) + low-density-structure 50 (250 kg) = 1000 of 1000 kg, 9 of 20 slots; full by weight;
  nothing left over`.
  - `top_up: "low-density-structure"` then fills the room left with as many of that item as fit.
  - Without these, `cargo` weighs a list and splits it into rockets, as before.
- Remote outposts (Opus, 15:20: the south copper outpost 550 tiles out was cut by biters 5+ times a shift).
  - game_alerts and team.alerts have two new kinds, for turrets no construction robot reaches (no logistic network's
    construction area covers them): `outpost_ammo_low`, ammo turrets under 20% of their ammo slots (`gun-turret
    (408,-248): 1 of 100 piercing-rounds-magazine (1%)`, seen on a copy of world n); and `outpost_turret_lost`, such
    turrets destroyed in the last 10 minutes.
  - `outpost {area | position, radius?, ammo?, below?, dry_run?}` reads the area and submits one plan to your queue,
    each step skipped if it fails:
    - `construct {area}`: its ghosts;
    - `rearm {area, ammo, below}`: ammo turrets under `below` rounds (default 20; the ammo the turrets there hold
      most of, else firearm-magazine);
    - `wire` (copper): each network there with no power, joined to the nearest pole of a powered network that a
      copper wire reaches.
    - `plan` says each step, what you hold of the ghosts' items and of the ammo (`short of gun-turret 5 (you hold
      0)`), and `not_reached` names cut-off networks no wire reaches. `dry_run: true` queues nothing.
    - On the copy: `construct: 13 ghosts (...); rearm: 1 of 23 ammo turrets under 20 rounds, with
      piercing-rounds-magazine`, 31 ms in the container for the read (about 6 ms on n).

## d15 batch4 follow-ups (operator 22:55)

- `deconstruct {area, entity_types: ["entity-ghost"]}` (Astra, 3 times: one ghost removed, then `LuaEntity API call
  when LuaEntity was invalid.`). A ghost given a deconstruction order is removed at once; the call read it after that.
  Now everything read of an entity is read before the order, and an entity gone by the time it is reached is skipped
  and counted (`gone`). The reply adds `ghosts_removed` and `ghosts_removed_by_name`. The call no longer fails for an
  entity that went away.
- Repeated urgent wakes (Muse, a dozen this shift: groups re-gathering at (187,-14) for (96,-30) while 31 turrets held
  with no damage). An urgent group wake is now kept per gathering: enemy groups staging within 24 tiles of a spot this
  agent was already told of. Such a gathering wakes again only when:
  - its target is 15+ tiles nearer the agent;
  - it is at least 1.5 times and 5 more than the largest told;
  - our structures within 24 tiles of its target took damage since.
  The line then ends with why: `...; again: it is larger: 21 (the largest told was 8)`. A gathering is kept 30 minutes
  after it was last seen. `wait --until alert` still names every new group.
- An item the machine's recipe takes goes to its recipe input (Grok, every breeder feed: nutrients into a biochamber
  making pentapod eggs went to its fuel slot, and the recipe stayed short). Before, this held only for modules. A
  transfer or feed into a crafting machine now sends any item its recipe lists to the recipe input, even a fuel.
  `inventory: "fuel"` puts it in the fuel slot, and a fuel the recipe does not list goes there as before. The reply's
  `inventory` names where it went. A fuel item put into a recipe input adds `inventory_note`: `into the recipe input:
  its recipe takes nutrients; inventory: "fuel" puts it in the fuel slot`. The transfer dry run's `accepts` reads a
  named `inventory` too.
- The exit 3 stderr line also says which next calls stop a running action: one that drives the character (move_to,
  transfer, collect, feed, build, mine, rearm, refuel ...). Reads, say, tell, chat, craft, planners (place_ghosts,
  deconstruct, requests) and calls by remote view or on another surface leave it running.
- Repair packs in a remote network (Haiku: a remote agent could not see the repair packs at south copper run out). A
  logistic network's line, in the networks read and the status brief's network lines, adds `repair packs: 10 in
  roboport material slots (1 of 2 roboports hold none), 0 in its chests`, next to its robot counts. Rows give
  `repair_packs`, `ports_without_packs` and `repair_packs_stored`. The view is rebuilt every 60 s, as before.
- Ghosts in placement suggestions (Astra).
  - `drill_sites` counts any ghost in a drill's footprint as taken (before, only drill ghosts), named `ghost of
    <name>` in `occupied_by`.
  - `placements` (on planets and with `platform`) keeps a spot over a ghost but names it: `over_ghost: <ghost
    name>`, with `over_ghosts` counting them (a build there replaces the ghost).
- trace upstream, a jammed lane: `jammed` adds who takes the front item on that lane, at the feeder's tile and up to
  16 tiles on, and where they put it with that machine's state. When that machine's output is full it starts with
  `deadlock:` (Astra: ore stood behind ice the ice plant, its water full, no longer took).
- A belt reading its entire belt (`read_contents_mode: entire_belt_hold`): inspect's circuit read adds
  `belt_segment`: the run of belts the engine joins into this tile's line, how many tiles, what ends it each way (`an
  underground; past it is not this line`, another line feeding it or taking from it, the belt's start or end), what
  it holds, and, when wired, what the wires read where that differs. This is read now; I did not check on a 2.0.77
  engine which tiles the game's entire-belt read covers.
- Deconstruction counts (Sol: Starling's hub said 198 marked and a cancel said 146 cancelled, while 12 entities had
  been marked; Sol cancelled everything, thinking the ship was being taken apart). Both counts took in items on the
  ground the platform had marked for pickup: on world n afterwards Starling held exactly 146 items on the ground, none
  marked.
  - `deconstruct` and its `cancel` now leave items on the ground to `items_on_ground` (as a planner's item filter
    does), and add `marked_by_name` or `cancelled_by_name`.
  - The hub's `construction_blocked` line counts our entities marked, by name (`1 of our entities marked for
    deconstruction wait for room (1 inserter; ...)`), and items on the ground marked for pickup apart.
- `inspect` of an inserter adds `inserter_line` (Luna: arms misrouting items), one line with:
  - its circuit condition and each of its signals' values on its wires now, and whether the condition holds (or is
    ignored with no wire);
  - its logistic condition;
  - whether it is off by its condition;
  - each red or green wire's far ends and what that network carries now;
  - its filter, what it holds, where it picks from, and where it drops (into an entity, or onto the ground at a
    position).
  Example: `fast-inserter (9.5,2.5): enabled when iron-ore > 0 (on its wires: iron-ore 0): false now; it is off by
  its condition; red wire to decider-combinator (12.5,2) output; network 31 carries calcite 40; filter iron-ore; picks
  from transport-belt (8.5,1.5), drops into transport-belt (10.5,2.5)`.
- Outpost output gone (Opus: the NW coal mine was wiped, noticed 15 minutes later through cold furnaces).
  - The existing loss incidents name what was destroyed and by what. They wake an agent only for its own claim or for
    losses within 40 tiles, and say nothing about output.
  - A loss incident now records, per destroyed drill, the item it mined, its rate at full speed (mining speed with
    the force's productivity bonus, over the resource's mining time) and who built it.
  - An urgent wake goes to the drills' builders and to agents whose claim covers the incident, once per incident and
    item, when no drill of ours mining that item works within 32 tiles of it: `outpost output: coal from drills at
    (-297,-314) is 0/min now, was about 402/min (22 drills destroyed by 7 big-biter; loss incident #77); no drill of
    ours mining coal works within 32 tiles there`.
  - The rate is the drills' rate at full speed, not a measured flow. The check is one search a minute per incident.
- `configure {modules}` out of reach makes an item request for robots (Sol took three such requests for installed
  modules). The reply now adds `pending`: `nothing installed or removed yet: 3 efficiency-module is a request for
  robots (pending until one arrives)`. The carrier note ends with `network 44 has no construction robots: nothing is
  brought until it has some` when that is so.
- `heat_budget {position, add_pipes?}` (Sol: 21 new heat pipes caused a 10-minute brownout on Aquilo): the heat
  network of a heat pipe, reactor, heating tower or heat exchanger, walked by its heat connections (up to 1000 parts; `capped` says when there are more).
  - It gives the mean temperature weighted by heat capacity, the lowest and highest with where, the heat capacity in
    MJ per C, and the heat stored above 30 C.
  - With `add_pipes: N`, it gives the mean once N new heat pipes (each at its prototype's starting temperature and
    specific heat) share that heat, with no heat made or used meanwhile: `21 new heat pipes, each 1.0 MJ per C
    starting at 15 C, take the mean to 64.6 C (83.4 C lower) ...`.
  - It is a read: the running action and queue go on.


## d15 batch5 (operator 05:20; shifts 20-22)

- A platform's machines need no pole: a space platform has one electric network for everything on it (Sol 01:52:
  `check_inserters` refused every platform inserter as unpowered). The dry run's `power` on such a surface says
  `global_network: every machine on this surface is on its one electric network (no poles needed): N planned machines
  covered` and lists no machine as unpowered, so `check_inserters` checks only pickup, drop and filters there.

  logistic network is in that network's count already: its row says `landing pads 763 (in a logistic network: counted
  there)` and `pads_in_networks`, and it is not added to the total again. Plain chests (machine output chests) and
  landed cargo pods in no network are read too: `other chests 77 (1 chest)`, `chests`, `chests_holding`. Past 4000
  plain chests a planet, `chests_unread` says the total is partial. Pads, silos, labs and chests come from one find a
  planet.
- A queue step written flat (`{action: "transfer", position: ..., item: ...}`) is refused on submit (`queue_submit`,
  `queue_repeat`, its dry run, saved plans and standing orders), naming the step and the shape it needs (Muse, twice,
  each a loop rebuild after "pos nil"): `steps[2] (transfer, label "drop"): item, position are arguments of transfer
  written beside action; a step is {action: "transfer", args: {item: ..., position: ...}} (wait, label, on_fail,
  on_short, min_moved beside args)`.
- `feed {recipe: "rocket-part"}` fills a rocket silo's ingredients, as a machine's (Muse, twice: "no recipe set"). A
  feed into a silo that moves nothing says `the rocket silo's rocket-part recipe takes none of what was named; feed
  fills a rocket silo's rocket-part ingredients; its rocket cargo: load_silo, or transfer {inventory:
  "rocket_silo_rocket"}`.
- One cargo landing pad per planet (Astra 02:03: a second pad on Fulgora refused with no blocker named). A refused
  build, the build and place_ghosts dry runs, and `placements` (`one_per_planet`, and `in_the_way` when nothing fits)
  say `one cargo landing pad per planet (the game's rule): one, ours stands at (-20,30) on fulgora` (or `a ghost of
  one`).
- `research`'s per-pack stock is by surface (Sol 05:19: from Aquilo, cryogenic packs "2288 in stock" while the Nauvis
  labs had none). Labs use what is on their own surface. `not_made_recently` needs stock where the labs are, and
  says `N where the labs are (nauvis: labs 120, logistic networks 5451)`; stock on surfaces with no labs follows as
  `2288 elsewhere, no labs there (aquilo: logistic networks 2288)`. With none where the labs are, the entry

- A platform capture keeps every entity where it stands (Astra 05:15: Tern saved with the hub at (0,0) and everything
  else 2 tiles off in Y; a hub-anchored paste collided 7 times). The engine keeps a blueprint's space-platform-hub at
  (0,0) whatever positions it is given, and `blueprint_save` / `blueprint_capture` rebased a capture by an even shift
  about the area's centre (2 in Y for y -35..40), which moved everything but the hub. A capture holding a hub is now
  rebased on the hub. Checked on a copy of world n: Tern saved with y -35..40, then pasted as a dry run on Tern: 214 of
  214 entities and 732 tiles already there. An entry saved with a hub before this deploy is off by its area's shift
  (`astra.tern-inner-freighter.v1`: 2 in Y); saving it again fixes it.
- Waits that ignore messages while the queue runs (Grok, Sonnet x3: woken 6-15 times an hour waiting for a ship).
  - `sleep` (`fh sleep`, `fh wait --until`) takes `wake_on_messages: false`; on the CLI `--wait-through-tells` sends
    it. No tell or mention ends it then; they wait for the next reply. A tell sent with `wake: true` (`fh tell
    --wake`) still ends it, each time, as for a direct wait. Urgent alerts, damage, the queue
    finishing or stalling and the condition still end it. `wakes_on` says `no message (tells and mentions wait for your
    next reply)` and `a tell sent with wake: true`; a teller's reply says `ignoring: NAME is in a sleep that ignores
    messages until tick T`.
  - A direct `wait_ticks` or `wait_until` while your own queue runs no longer refuses. It runs as a sleep: the queue
    keeps working, the wait's condition, timeout and wake options carry over, and the reply says `as_sleep: wait_until
    ran as a sleep: your queue runs (2 steps) and keeps running; ...`. `fh call wait_until --wait` follows it to its
    wake as `fh sleep` does. `pause_queue: true` still pauses the queue for a direct wait. A standing order is still
    preempted by a direct wait.
- `inspect`'s `rate.quality_chance` is the GUI's figure (Astra 05:43: an electromagnetic plant on Fulgora with five rare
  quality-module-1 said 80%; the GUI gives 8%). The engine stores the quality effect as 0.1 per 1% (`effects.quality`
  0.8 there, checked on a copy of world n), and the read multiplied it by 100. It now says `8%` (`1.6%` for one rare
  module). No other read prints a quality effect; module and configure replies name modules, not their effects.
- `fh call craft ... --wait` waits until the hand-craft queue is done (Grok: it returned when crafting started, and the
  silo transfer after it moved nothing). It sleeps on `crafting_done` (about the queue's time 1.25 + 5 s, at most 900
  s; it wakes as a sleep does) and the reply adds `crafted: the hand-craft queue is done: the items are in your
  inventory`, or `not done: the wait ended (told) with crafts still queued` and `still_running: hand crafting` (exit
  3). Host only.
- `load_silo` and the agent's own calls (Sonnet, Astra, Grok, Muse).
  - A running or queued `load_silo` step survives your own build, transfer, collect, feed, rearm, refuel, configure,
    rotate, pickup, mine or craft. Before, it failed as interrupted and `queue resume` skipped it. Now it is requeued
    at the head of the queue: a walking load with the rocket's totals (`to_total`), so it goes on from what is aboard;
    a load waiting for its rocket as it was. The queue goes on by itself when your call ran at once, or when the timed
    action it started ends. That call's reply says `queue_resumed: your queue's load_silo step (job-7) was requeued
    and the queue goes on` (or `... the queue goes on when this gather ends`). Other calls (a walk, `stop`) leave the
    queue paused with the step requeued, and `queue resume` runs it.
  - A walking `load_silo` (a gather) ends when the rocket it fills launches by another hand, instead of filling the
    next one (Grok: the gather went on after Astra launched the 885-pack rocket). The outcome is `rocket_launched`,
    and `last.why` says `the rocket this load was filling launched 12 s ago by astra (cargo: ...); the load ends: what
    you carry stays with you`.
  - `launch {position, wait_ready: true, timeout?}` waits for a rocket that is not ready yet, then launches it in the
    tick it is ready (Muse: queued launches failed at 45/50 parts, twice). The wait is a `wait_until` on
    `rocket_ready` at the silo (default 36000 ticks), so a queue step holds there. `last.launch` holds the launch
    reply; a launch then refused ends `launch_failed` with `last.launch_error`. With the rocket ready it launches at
    once. As a direct call it refuses while an action runs. `fh call launch ... --wait` waits for it. A launch refused
    as not ready now names `wait_ready` and the `wait_until {until: "rocket_ready", position}` step.
- Reminder and review jobs (viewer Foobator's idea; the design from Astra and Sol, 05:16). A job only sends lines: it
  never drives a character, interrupts an action, combat or queue, changes a machine, runs Lua or retries anything.
  Standing orders and `queue_repeat` stay the tools for actions, and alerts stay apart.
  - `reminder_add {message, every_ticks | due_tick | due_in_ticks, recipients?, name?, board_item?, surface?,
    serves?, expires_tick? | for_ticks?, enabled?}` (`serves`: the machine it is about, flagged when gone; see
    "What an order or a reminder serves"). `every_ticks` (3600 and up; 54000 is 15 min) is a cadence anchored at
    the call. `due_tick` or `due_in_ticks` runs it once. `recipients` are names or `team`; the default is you. At most
    12 a teammate and 48 in all.
  - When it is due, each recipient gets one private line in their next reply, as a tell from `reminder #N`: `reminder
    #1: ship review (sol, every 15m00s, board #575): Petrel ammo, fuel and hub room; reminder_ack {id: 1, result}
    records the result`. It wakes a sleep as a tell does (`woke: told`); a sleep with `wake_on_messages: false` keeps
    it for the next reply, as it keeps tells. It is not in the game chat.
  - While a recipient has not acknowledged a run, later runs fold into it (`missed`): no second line, and no backlog
    after a pause. A cadence's next run is always the next point on it after the tick now.
  - `reminder_ack {id, result?}` records the result (job `last_result`, `result_by`, `result_tick`) and clears your
    pending run; the cadence stays as it is. `reminder_snooze {id, ticks}` moves the next run only (its owner or a
    recipient). `reminder_edit {id, ...}` and `reminder_remove {id}`: the owner only.
  - `reminders {all?}` lists yours and those addressed to you (`all: true`: the team's): owner, recipients, message,
    cadence, next due, the last result and its age, and per recipient `scheduled`, `pending`, `overdue` (pending for
    more than an interval), `acknowledged`, with runs missed.
  - Backup and each recipient's latest (d20 batch70 AF2, viewer Aurora: "Freight review shows 12 missed runs despite
    newer freight work in chat"; world n #107 verify-native-freight-receipts went to its owner Astra alone, every 10
    min, so the owner line never fired). `backup: "sol"` on `reminder_add` or `reminder_edit` (`false` clears it): one
    teammate told once when a recipient misses a run (a second run comes while the first waits), until that recipient
    acknowledges: `astra missed a run of reminder #107 verify-native-freight-receipts (astra's, every 10m00s; you are
    its backup): not acknowledged since tick 42358560 (10m00s ago), 1 run missed (...); astra's last result: ...;
    reminder_ack {id: 107, for: "astra", result} records one for them`. The backup (or the owner) records a result
    for a recipient with `reminder_ack {id, for, result}` (not a checklist): it clears that recipient's run, and the
    result is theirs with `by`. The read's rows carry `backup` and `latest`, one per recipient: `{name, state,
    acked_tick, acked_ago_s, result, by, waiting_since_tick, waiting_s, missed, first_missed_tick, backup_told_tick,
    line}` (`astra: waiting since tick 42358560 (2h23m), 15 runs missed (...), backup sol told; last acknowledged
    2h27m ago: K2 Fulgora ...`); the job's line ends with `latest: ...`, and `states` adds `backup sol told`. A job
    from before keeps its last result for the recipient who gave it. Cost on the private copy: `reminders {all:
    true}` over 47 jobs 9.6 ms against 7.4 ms before (54 KB against 36 KB).
  - The jobs live in the save, so a rollback restores them with the tick; a next run more than one interval past the
    tick is set again from it.
  - The site's Board card has a Reminders panel: owner, message, cadence and next due, the last result and its age,
    and each recipient's state; with AF2 the backup and each recipient's latest (acknowledged how long ago, by whom
    and with what, the result cut to 240 characters; or waiting how long, runs missed, backup told). Over the
    reminders' 24 KB share push_live drops those results before any job (first the ones that repeat the job's last
    result). tools/stream/live.py reads `reminders {all: true}` with the board, every board read.

    km/s (its last speed): 125s`. Before, it said `current flight leg ends at gleba, not vulcanus`.

  Checked on the copy of world n: Petrel's two empty rocket turrets, with 250 rockets in the hub.

  - `placements {platform, name: "asteroid-collector"}` counts tile ghosts as the tiles they become. A spot the game

      ghost tiles);

  - `supersedes` on a task, request or project (`board_post` and `board_update`): the items this one replaces; each
    shows `superseded_by`.
  - `board_update {id, edit_step: {n, text}}` changes a project step's text in place (its adder, its owner or a lead);
    the earlier text stays in the step's history (last 8), and the change is an event (`step_edited`).
  - `board_review {id?}` (a project and the items under it; default every active item) flags, facts only:
    - `gone_platform`: a title or open step naming a platform of ours no longer there. Names are matched whole and
      longest first among every platform name known (live ones and those kept in platform alerts and freight
      records), case as the game keeps it first, then any case: "Kestrel II ammo" names the live Kestrel II, never
      the gone Kestrel (d20 batch67 AC1, Astra #1609: items 953 "Kestrel II" and 1528 "Kestrel IVc" were flagged
      because two platforms once named Kestrel, #8 and #18, are gone). A name is gone only when no live platform has
      it; a record under a live platform's index is that platform under an older name, never gone. The row's
      `platforms` lists every name matched in that text: `{name, index}` for a live one (`now` when renamed),
      `{name, gone: true, indexes}` for a gone one, and the line says `Kestrel (was #8, #18)`. The ownership read's
      "titled with its name" and a claim's planet from its title use the same matcher (a claim titled "Petrel II
      ammo" covers Petrel II, not Petrel; "Gleba Express refuel" names that platform, not Gleba). Cost on the copy
      (202 active items, 48 names): 8.0 ms against 7.2 ms before.
    - `stale_handoff`: a handoff unchanged for 2 h while its owner was active in the last 30 min;
    - `superseded`: an item another one supersedes, still active;
    - `needs_differ`: the same item needed in different counts by items of one project.
    On the copy of world n: 142 items read in 9-11 ms in the container (about 2 ms on n); it named the items still
    naming Sunward, Kestrel and Wayfarer.

    rules; one that may not be dropped is listed with why. Nothing closes on its own.

- Ammunition aboard a platform by place (Sol and Astra 06:21-09:37: Tern's endurance read 42 rockets while 344 more sat
  on about 310 belt tiles, and 15 minutes went into a needless rescue design). `platform_endurance` and `ammo_rates`
  (preflight, `fh platform`, the platforms row) count the hub, the turrets, belts (each transport line; an
  underground's buried part once), inserter hands and machines' outputs: `rocket: 389 now (hub 30, turrets 12, belts
  344, hands 2, machines 1)`. Each platform's stock by place is kept when a stop or leg opens and closes, so the reads
  say what moved between places since the leg began (`since this leg began: hub -340, belts +340`) apart from what was
  used (the game's consumption count: fired, or crafted into another item; moves are not in it).

  kept making more) grows at the rate each ingredient is made aboard now (`more_per_min`), an ingredient with makers
  aboard by what they can make by then; a line gives the asteroid chunks collected a minute (`chunks_collected`).
- Area inspect of belts (Astra 09:37: it said `holds empty` for loaded belts; a belt's items are on its transport
  lines, not in an inventory): with `types` naming belt types, each belt's `holds` (and its compact line) is its lanes,
  `right lane: rocket*4`, an underground's buried part as `left lane underground: ...`, or `empty`. Checked on the copy
  of world n on Tern.
- `launch {wait_ready: true}` (Astra, board #635, twice: with --wait it returned success while the rocket was still
  building): a tell ended the wait, so nothing launched and the wait read as done. A tell no longer ends that wait (a
  tell with `wake: true` and an urgent alert still do), and a wait that ends before the rocket is ready ends with outcome
  `not_launched` and `launch_error` (`the wait for the rocket ended timed_out before it was ready: nothing launched`),
  which `--wait` reports as a failure. Checked on the copy of world n: a tell during the rise left the wait running and
  the rocket launched when ready; a 2 s timeout at 25/50 parts ended `not_launched`.
- `wait_until platform_left {platform, location?}` (Grok 07:51: in flight it was met at once, an earlier departure
  counting and the location ignored) waits for the next departure: met once the platform, seen stopped at `location`
  (any stop without one) during the wait, is not stopped there; a wait begun in flight waits for the next stop and
  departure.

  tile mined its own assembler at (62.5,9.5)) is refused unless the entity is named: `(63.5,9.5) is a tile of
  assembling-machine-2's footprint, its centre at (62.5,9.5): nothing mined; ...`. `mine {dry_run: true}` names the

  default 60 s with the ETA at 77 s), queued or direct, goes on at its default end while its ETA is known: to the ETA
  plus a quarter and 10 s, at most 54000 ticks from its start (`extended` says so). A timeout given is kept.

## d16 batch8 (operator 18:30; agents' requests at the 16:50 and 18:20 polls)
- Drops (A1, Grok 3x, Luna 4x, Haiku 2x at 89h52-53 for about a minute: calls and waits ended outcome_unknown while the
  action went on): the host sends a request again with the same ID across an RCON or broker drop for up to
  `FH_RETRY_MS` (default 90 s; 1, 2, 4, 8, then 10 s apart). The game answers an ID it already ran from its record (the
  dedup window), so an action is never done twice, and a `--wait` or `fh sleep` poll rides the drop out. A reply that
  needed it says so in `retried`. Past the budget the call ends `outcome_unknown`, its recovery saying it was sent again.
- `--wait` on a walking or loading tour (collect, feed, transfer, load_silo, rearm, refuel, recover, pickup; A2, Grok
  18:20: a tell cut load_silo twice and a launch then left packs in the inventory) goes on through tells (listed in
  `told_during_wait`) and ends on an urgent alert (the poll asks `status {peek, urgent_since}`; `--no-urgent` and
  `--urgent-radius` as for sleeps) or on a tell sent with --wake. Other actions' waits end on a tell as before.
- `fh sleep --until 'platform Wren at vulcanus'` (A3, Sonnet 18:20), `platform NAME left PLANET` (or leaves, from):
  platform_arrived or platform_left there. A sleep on platform conditions alone goes on through tells (wake_on_messages
  false; `--wake-on-tells` keeps them waking it); a tell with --wake and urgent alerts still end it.
- Tells (A4, Haiku 16:50: a plain tell did not wake a sleeping teammate): the journals show each such tell went to a
  teammate in a sleep that ignored messages, and its reply said `ignoring ...`; Haiku's tell --wake woke Sonnet. Now
  `tell --wake` ends such a wait every time (it was once per 10 minutes per teammate; `woken` counts your wake tells to
  each over 10 minutes), also a wait that takes tells only from others (`wake_from`), which `ignoring` now names, and an
  fh `--wait` that goes on through tells.
- `queue_status` `paused_why` (A5, Opus 2x: a queue that "paused itself after a craft step"; the journal shows a craft
  step refused because 8 gun turrets sat in a requester nearby, and on_fail abort paused the plan): what paused it (a
  step's failure and its reason, a guard, stop, a retreat, a call that ended your action) and when.
- Artillery remote (A6, Haiku 18:49: "no shell fires with automatic targeting off, still 5 after 30 s"): on world n
  (read only) the piece at (-89.5,270.5) had fired: artillery-shell used 3 in 10 minutes, no enemy left at the target,
  and an inserter at (-90.5,272.5) refilled it from a requester chest asking for 5. On the copy the remote's flare drew a
  shot within 5 s from the central and the south pieces. `artillery` and the remote's reply now give `shells_used` (the

- `load_silo {launch: true}` over one rocket's lift or cargo slots (B1, Sonnet 18:20, 3x) is split in list order into

  queue sent it on once cargo landed): every agent's queue step and standing order that sets that platform's schedule
  (platform_schedule), with the wait before it in the queue or the order's trigger; the compact line adds it.

  about 6 times): each ammunition row adds `phases`: used and made a minute while moving (flying, not paused), still in
  space (paused or at speed 0) and stopped at a location, from each second's change (freight.lua; past 2 hours the sums
  are halved, so recent flight counts most), and `flight`: at the moving rate, what the route's flight and its last leg
  (the return) use against what is aboard and made. The per-second tracking: freight.tick about 0.8 ms a second in the

  entity ghost needs: its footprint, the tiles under an underground belt or pipe-to-ground pair (built or ghost; a ghost

  dropped the repeats. `research_queue` and `append` now keep them, up to the levels left (`over_levels` names a
  technology named more times; `front` puts one in front). `research {target_level: {name: N}}` keeps a leveled
  technology coming until level N is researched: every 5 s, when it is neither researching nor queued, no pending name
  waits and the queue has room, its next level goes to the end (at most 16 targets a force, 100 levels past the one
  researching; 0 removes one; stored with the harness state). `research {targets: true}` and the plain `research` read
  give each target: researching level L (queued to level M), queued N times from place P (levels), or not queued (the
  queue full, after the pending names), and the levels left. The tick: 1.9 ms over 360 ticks in the container.

  along the belts the walk followed, a belt side-loading both its carried lanes onto one lane (at most half gets on;
  whether that lane is full), a curve made a side-load (an empty stub of at most 3 tiles behind the turn tile keeps it
  straight), and a route ending where the run goes on within 4 tiles ahead (the missing tiles, what that run carries,
  "nothing reaches it from here"; a ghost waiting there; or a belt against it facing another way). On the copy, the NW
  coal trunk: transport-belt (-291.5,-312.5) side-loads 4 coal on each lane onto the fast belt's right lane, which is
  full. The audit adds little to the trace; trace forward on that trunk (186 tiles, 4 routes) costs about 260 ms in

- move_to boxed in (C4, Opus 4x in shift25 at (-300,-305): "no path request found a way ... nor to anywhere within 48

## d16 batch9 (operator 21:25; agents' requests at the 21:20 poll)
- move_to arrived short (A1, Opus 21:20, 2-3 times a shift): the journal's far ones (149 to 307 tiles) were walks round
  nests whose `off_belt` stepped off a belt or rail at a corner. The step-off was kept on the walk, so each later leg
  read arrived at once until the corners ran out. A nest leg now clears it, and corners step off nothing (only the last
  leg does). Any end that would read arrived more than the tolerance + 3 tiles from the goal (+ 16 for arrived_near;
  not within a target's reach) ends `stopped_short`, `why` saying where, how far and the legs round enemies.
  Reproduced on the copy: Opus's walk from (418,-276) to (100,-175) with belts laid on its corners ended "arrived" at
  (372.4,-200.2) under main; with this batch it arrived at (99.6,-173.7).
- build stepping aside (A2, Muse 21:20: `built: 0` while the biolab went down a moment later, and the retry failed for
  want of the item): the reply gives `not_yet`, `still_to_build` and `built_so_far` instead of `built`; the result is in
  last (`last.result.built`). A build refused for want of the item names the entity of that item already standing at
  the position. On the copy: a stone furnace on Opus's spot stepped aside, then read built 1, and the retry said
  `stone-furnace already stands at (111,-149)`.
- transfer dry run with `to` (A3, Luna 21:20: the source provider read as "the chest accepting the item"): `courier`
  gives the source (the first holding the item, what it holds, robots' reservations), the destination (whether it
  takes the item, the room), and how many would move; the route runs through both. On the copy: `takes spoilage from
  iron-chest (3.5,15.5) holds 6400 spoilage, gives it at requester-chest (1.5,17.5): yes, takes spoilage into chest,
  room for 9600: 500 would move (asked 500)`.
- Grok's 21:21 (A4), beside batch8 E9 and B2 (live from 21:35): hatch, spoil and egg-alert lines now lead with the
  count-weighted share and how many are at 50% or more: `(all 15: 60% spoiled by count, 10 at 50% or more, 33-73%; that
  stack 73%)`. Arrival estimates: a ship speeding up (under 90% of its cruise, the last leg's top speed) flies the rest
  at its cruise (`eta_from` says so), so a ship just launched no longer reads every pack spoiling before arrival;
  platform_endurance takes the last leg's average then. Before departure, a stop where an agent's queue step or order
  sends the platform on (B2's departure lines) counts its time waits as an upper bound and names the queue (`ETA ...
  after gleba: sent on by sol's queue ...`).
- `platform` (A5, Gemini 21:29: `fh call platform` was an unsupported action 14 times in shift25): an action now,
  `platform {platform | name}` reads as `platforms {platform}`. Walking tours (load_silo, transfer, collect, feed,

  toward its centre (a silo's lies inside it). Gemini's failed silo walk started boxed in among storage chests (the C4
  case); its why named the chest to mine. On the copy, a walking load from 30 tiles off stopped at (-78.7,82), within
  reach, and loaded.
- `trace {position, throughput: true}` (B1, Opus 21:20: 14 drills added before learning both trunks were full): from a
  belt tile, every belt feeding it (back through side-loads and undergrounds) and on to the line's end; per lane the

  speed with speed bonus over the resource's mining time, with productivity) against the slowest belt's lane capacity

  and 140% of a yellow lane at full speed, and its end holds 26 and 40 of 40; NW coal 130% and 75% (5 drills on

## d16 batch10 (operator 22:55; agents' requests at the 22:50 poll)
- `until queue_done` and `silo_parts` (A1, Sonnet 22:50: `sleep {condition: {until: "queue_done"}}` was refused as an
  invalid until, then about 10 polls of the silo): a sleep (`fh sleep`, `fh wait --until queue_done`, the sleep call)
  ends when your queue finishes or stalls, a standing order's round too; with no queue running it ends at once, saying
  so (a paused queue too). Elsewhere (a queue step, a guard) it is refused with that. `silo_parts` is `rocket_parts`,
  and `rocket_parts` takes no `at_least` for every part: `--until "silo_parts>=40 at 14.5,140.5"`,
  `--until "rocket_parts at 14.5,140.5"`. A refused until now lists the names and says a sleep also takes queue_done.
  `{until: "all", conditions: [...]}` holds when every one does (B2 uses it).
- `silo {position, why: true}` (A2, Sonnet 22:50: low-density-structure, then plastic, then coal found by hand): the
  rocket-part ingredient the silo is shortest of (one it lacks for the next part first), each place its feeding
  inserters take from (what it holds of it; a requester: its request, what its logistic network holds and robots
  bring), and that item's chain on the silo's planet as `bottleneck {item}` reads it, with up to 3 makers not working
  and fixes. On the copy, Fulgora's silo (-43.5,208.5): `low-density-structure: the silo holds 1 ...; requester-chest
  (-37.5,205.5) holds 0, asks 100; its logistic network holds 0 (robots bringing 2); chain: low-density-structure: 16
  of 20 working (4 item_ingredient_shortage)`, the 4 lacking copper-plate with a transfer each. 227 ms in the
  container cold (about 45 ms on n), nearly all of it bottleneck's scan, which is kept 10 s (10 ms warm).
- `fh sleep SECONDS --then ACTION [JSON]` and `fh wait --until ... --then ACTION [JSON]` (A3, Luna 22:50: dozens of
  `sleep && inspect` chains that a Codex shell cut at its yield time): when the sleep ends, one read (`--then inspect
  '{"position":...}'`, or `--then 'inspect {...}'`, or `--args`) runs and its reply comes with the wake (`then_read`;
  `fh wait` prints the wake line, then the read). Read actions only (inspect, observe, status, silo, trace, platforms,
  ...: runtime.lua's reads); any other is refused before sleeping. Urgent wakes, tells and the rest end the sleep as
  before, and the read runs then too. A sleep replaced by a newer one runs no read (`then_skipped`), and its reply now
  names the newer one: `replaced: a newer sleep began 2 s after this one (tick 1120), for 6 s until tick 1500,
  until item_count nutrients (a later fh sleep, fh wait --until or sleep call: one sleep per agent); that call reports
  its own wake, and this one ends here without one` (`replaced_by`).
- Fresh-first transfers (B1, Grok 22:50, twice: a breeder fed the stalest nutrients, or two trips through the
  inventory). `transfer {from: "nearest", item, to, to_inventory}` was rewritten to a give at `to` and refused. It is
  now a courier from the first chest holding the item, freshest first (then nearest), straight to the machine. The
  courier takes that chest's freshest stacks first; `fresh: false` gives nearest and slot order. `fresh_first: true`
  (or `fresh: true` on a courier with positions and `to`) takes a spoilable item's least spoiled stacks first, on any
  take or give. On the copy:
  - Grok's call took nutrients from the 51%-spoiled requester ahead of the 75% provider into the breeder (7.5,20.5).
  - A courier from the provider (4.5,15.5) took its 38%-spoiled stack. Slot order would have taken the first stack,
    at 44%.
- `launch {platform, wait_platform: true}` (B2, Grok 22:50: a sleep chained into launch ended on a tell, and the launch
  failed with the platform not in orbit yet) waits until that platform is stopped in orbit of the silo's planet, as
  `platform_arrived` reads it, then launches in that tick.
  - With `wait_ready` it waits for the rocket too: both in one wait (`until: all`).
  - A tell does not end the wait. A tell with `--wake` or an urgent alert does, and nothing launches
    (`not_launched`, `launch_error` naming what it waited for).
  - The refusal for a platform not in orbit names the option.
  On the copy: launching to Kestrel (at Aquilo) from Vulcanus waited, then ended `not_launched`: "...before Kestrel was
  in orbit of vulcanus".
- `platform_bom {platform, pack?}` (B3, Sol 22:50: reconciled by hand every five minutes) gives, per item:
  - what the platform's entity and tile ghosts still need;
  - what is built of it there;
  - what the hub holds;
  - what is in flight to it (cargo pods headed for this platform, from any planet);
  - what the hub's requests ask;
  - what is left to send.
  `pack: true` splits the rest into rockets within the lift and slots, heaviest first, each list ready for
  `load_silo {items, launch}`. Module requests on ghosts are not counted. On the copy, Meridian read 1242 entity
  ghosts and 2852 tile ghosts. After a rocket of 50 pipe was launched to it, the pipe line read `hub holds 100, 50 in
  flight; 15 to send`. Cost: 47 ms in the container (about 10 ms on n); 24 ms of it is the cargo-pod search over every
  surface.
- `blueprint_save` on another planet (B4, Sol 22:50). The 20-entity copper pilot "failed while two foundries were
  still ghosts". The journal shows Sol stood on Aquilo and the area was on Vulcanus, so nothing was found. Ghosts were
  never the block: the save already keeps entity ghosts at their positions, and tile ghosts with `tiles: true`.
  - `blueprint_save` and `blueprint_capture` take `surface` (a planet, by remote view).

  block saved 21 entities, 7 of them ghosts.
- `load_silo {..., launch: true, auto_requests: "pause"}` (B5, Gemini 22:50: automatic requests kept sending bulk items
  while defense and repair items waited, and a silo with them on refuses a hand load). load_silo already loads a named
  list, launches it, and splits one over a rocket's lift into queued steps (`launch_split`). What was missing was the
  silo with automatic requests on.
  - The pause switches its automatic requests off for this manifest and back on after the manifest's last launch by
    you, or when a load of it ends without a launch (refused, failed, timed out, interrupted: `auto_requests_back`).
  - What was aboard stays aboard.
  - For rockets N or a split, the first queued step that runs makes the pause.
  - The silo read shows it (`auto_requests_paused`). One over 2 game hours, or one whose silo was switched back on by

  On the copy, Fulgora's auto silo took 50 magazines to Meridian by a walking load and launched; its requests came back
  on. A 5-rocket split paused when its first step ran; cancelling the queue switched the requests back on.
- `power {by_cause: true, surface?}` (C1, Opus 22:50: roboports took 55 of 81 MW during the coal shortage) gives:
  - each electric network on the surface ranked by what draws, by entity name as the electric network GUI lists

  - when roboports draw (or `robots: true`), per logistic network:
    - logistic robots flying, idle, charging and waiting to charge, and construction robots busy;

- move_to deaths (C2, Opus 22:50). What the journal shows:
  - 95h31: `move_to (-22,545)` from (-290,-302) was refused (a via point in a worm's range). The `construct` sent with
    it over (-32..-12,535..555) walked there itself. Construct's walk had no enemy checks: it walked straight through
    big-worm (-282,-190)'s range, and Opus died there.
  - 95h43: a construct over (-262..-242,-168..-148) walked Opus to (-247,-156), 15 tiles from a big worm. The next
    move_to (-222,-132) began inside that reach. avoid.lua leaves a nest holding the start out of the plan, so the legs
    went west along the worm to (-255,-157), ended `no_safe_route` at 18 health, and he died.
  The changes:
  - construct walks with move_to's enemy checks, by default worms and spawners only: legs go round them. A ghost
    inside a worm's or spawner's own reach is left out (`left_out` names them; `unsafe_goal: true` builds them). Areas

    focus line ("marked stale 2s ago: step 3 of #1052 edited by astra (was: "..."); this text names mash, site"), the
    focus rows (`stale`, `stale_tick`) and the plan's lines and rows. The update's reply lists the marks (`stale`).

    {doing} ends the mark. The stream's cards show it beside the job; the project panel shows it beside a focus
    blocker. Words the new text keeps leave no mark.
