### Group C
- C1 (Grok): a gate on bioflux over 200 and agricultural science under 500 was flipped by hand about six times; an
  inserter's logistic condition holds one test. The game's way is a decider combinator reading the logistic network
  (a roboport set to read its items) with both tests joined by and, wired to the inserter's circuit condition. A
  helper, `circuit_gate {position, all: [cond, ...], at?, source?}` (circgate.lua), does what a player does by hand
  with the calls an agent has, in this order: `build` a decider-combinator from the character's inventory (a free tile
  in build reach and within wire reach of the entity and the source, nearest the entity; or `at`); `circuit_set` the
  roboport to read its network's items (when the source is a roboport); a red `wire` source -> decider input;
  `circuit_set` the decider (every test, `and`, output signal-check 1); a green `wire` decider output -> entity;
  `circuit_set` the entity enabled when signal-check > 0, its logistic condition off. It is survival-fair: the decider
  comes from the agent's inventory and each step is an action the agent could call itself. A failed step stops it and
  says what was done and the calls left; no decider held or no tile within reach of both: refused first, with the
  calls. tests/d17_batch20.lua (the calls and their arguments, a failed step, the refusal).

  the game; the reply's `trash_unrequested`: `on: robots take to storage what no request names: spoilage*34` (a chest:
  what it holds now that no active section names), or `off`. Grok's spoilage clears in shift30 were 18 from passive
  provider chests and 2 from requester chests. A passive provider, active provider or storage chest has no such
  switch; the refusal says so with what the game does: robots take spoilage from it only to a requester or buffer

## d17 batch31 (the agents' 06:20 poll)

- A1 (Sonnet: coal -> petroleum -> plastic -> LDS -> silo; Opus: crude -> refinery -> petroleum -> chem plant -> plastic,
  about 30 minutes by hand each time): `bottleneck {item, chain: true, surface?}` walks the item's recipe chain back
  from the item, one link per item (chain.lua):
  - Makers: the crafters on the recipe most of them run (the other recipes making it counted in), drills on its
    resource, and offshore pumps of the fluid. They come from the census pass's entity lists (census.lua lists crafters
    by recipe, drills by resource and pumps by fluid; no find in the read). Up to 24 a link are read now: state,
    crafting or mining speed, productivity.
  - Rates: made and used a minute now (the surface's production statistics, last 10 minutes), and full, what its makers
    make at full speed (the read makers' average times all of them; a pumpjack at its yield).
  - asked: what the link it feeds takes at that link's full speed, per recipe that takes it, net of what the recipe
    gives back.
  - stock: what the surface's logistic networks hold (items).
  - `limit`: from the item down, while most of a link's read makers lack an input, the ingredient made the smallest
    share of its ask while below it. The walk ends at the link where that stops, with its numbers and its makers' own
    states: lack an input, output full, lack power or fuel, off by a condition, or working with full speed below the
    ask.

## d17 batch34 (the agents' 12:20 poll)

- A1 (Astra: about 65 medium-pole ghosts stood over live small poles while `ghosts` read "robots can build it"; robots
  held poles until the small poles were marked for upgrade):
  - robots.lua `M.under(g)`: a live entity of ours on an entity ghost's spot (its box shrunk by 0.1, or a quarter of a
    side), whose collision layers meet the ghost's, marked neither for upgrade nor for deconstruction. Characters,
    vehicles, robots, ghosts and proxies are left out. It is of the ghost's kind when it is another name of the same
    fast-replace group and size.
  - `ghosts`: such a ghost's verdict reads `blocked: our live X (x,y) stands on its spot, not marked for upgrade (robots
    do not build it until it is)` (or deconstruction), counted in the summary as `blocked: a live entity of ours on its
    spot, ...`. `blocked` gives a line per ghost and entity name with the count and the call that marks them:
    `upgrade {area, from, to}` for one of its kind (the area round them when it fits 128 tiles, else the first 16
    positions), else `deconstruct {area, entity_names}`. Only the nearest 512 entity ghosts are checked
    (`blocked_checked` says so past that).
  - `construction_robots`: a robot whose order targets such a ghost is held up by it (its line says so), and
    `ghosts_blocked` counts the ghosts in the orders of robots in the air (512 at most) as `ghosts` does.
  - Cost on world n (read-only probe, the module loaded into a throwaway env): 14 ghosts 0.17 ms, 69 ghosts 0.81 ms,
    about 12 us a ghost, so 512 is about 6 ms. Nauvis had no blocked ghost by then, so the hit path ran in tests only.
- A2 (Astra, Luna: Petrel's drop 1376 of 3 underground belts and a chest landed in Gleba's pad and construction robots
  spent them on unrelated ghosts within seconds; four reads found nothing):
  - drops.lua: a drop sent to a landing pad records the pad's count of each sent item before (at the send) and when it
    lands. Then for 20 s (sampled every 15 ticks, with drops.tick) each fall in the pad's count reads the construction
    and logistic robots of ours within 8 tiles of the pad holding that item (each robot counted once) and the ghost or
    entity its first order is on. What fell with no robot seen is said as such (an inserter, a player, or a robot
    already gone). No on_robot_* event is used.
  - The drop's landing line in the team block waits for those 20 s and carries the pad line. `drops` gives `pad`,
    `pad_verdict` (`landed, then taken by construction robots`, `landed, then N of M taken by construction robots`,
    `landed, then N of M left the pad`) and `pad_now`.
  - `where_is {item}` adds `drops` (the last 4 drops of it into a pad on that surface) and `shipment` adds the
    platform's last 2 drops into a pad at each stop's planet, each with the verdict. The game reserves nothing for the
    sender; the docs say so.

  - Found in the journals: the platform_bom keeper (Sol's `request: true, tail: true` since 17:52) asked 72 foundation in
    Sol's reads at ticks 28354138 and 28356049, and Muse's observe at 28355157 listed no foundation slot. An earlier
    read (28234653) lacked it the same way between 972 and 891. Both times items sorted before it in the section had

    rewrite put each item at its sorted place, so every later item was written into the slot another held. The vanish

  - The keeper now keeps each item in the slot it has. An item no longer needed is cleared where it stands, and a new
    one takes a free slot (or the next past the end). A slot as wanted is not written again. Duplicate slots of one
    item are cleared.

    request, or how many have none) and `unrequested`: each item the ghosts need, beyond the hub, pods in flight and

- A4 (Sol: Swiftlet's LDS gate timed out twice; the failed step was removed, so a plain resume would have flown short):
  - A queued `wait_until` takes `on_timeout: "hold"` (or `"fail"`, the default). On timing out, the step is recorded
    `timed_out` with `held: true`, a copy goes back first in pending (same id, label and args), and the queue pauses.
    `paused_why` names the condition still unmet with what it saw. `queue_resume` waits for it again with a fresh
    timeout. Remote lanes run the same code.
  - In a standing order's run it fails as before. A direct `wait_until` with `on_timeout` is refused.

- B3 (Opus, 3 times: a deconstruct of two chests 450 tiles away sent about 300 robots, some lost; 20 old requesters

  - robottrips.lua `preview(surface, force, jobs)`: jobs grouped by kind, item and 32-tile cell (32 groups). Trips:

    construct jobs on the far east network: 5.4 ms with the enemy read, 0.9 ms for 24 without. A first version that
    read enemies leg by leg and every roboport per group ran 88 ms for 36 jobs; the structures read once and the
    roboports read once a network brought it down.

  cryogenic science; the character held all 1000 and stood "in gather" at (20.34,0.63) for over 40 s; stopped, and a
  load_silo without from launched):
  - Found in the journal: the gather phase had ended. The tour stood at its silo stop in reach (the silo's box is
    within 10 tiles of (20.34,0.63); "14 tiles" was to its centre), holding for the rocket, as a walking load with
    `launch` does (Astra 06:23's rule: nothing goes into a rocket not ready).
  - In status during the hold: `silo_wait` parts 29, 22 of them added in the 42 s, 31 a minute. The stopped step's
    last read "waiting at the silo for the rocket to be ready (building the rocket: parts 22/50); nothing loaded yet".
    But status's active gave `progress: stop 3 of 3 (rocket-silo ...), 14 tiles to it` and `stuck_s: 42`, and the
    warning line "made no progress ... likely physically stuck". That read as a stalled walk.
  - Status now: a gather holding at its silo stop gives `holding` (rocketload.lua `hold_line`: the stop, in reach,
    why, rocket parts of required and their rate, the time to the last part at that rate, held for it, how long, the
    give-up tick). It gives no `progress` and no `stuck_s`, so no stuck warning.
  - Test: tests/rocketload.lua, two sources: both taken (60 and 40), then the hold at the silo, nothing loaded, and
    the hold line.

## d17 batch35 (the agents' 13:50 poll)

- A failed direct call that pauses the queue says so first (A5, Muse 14:16: rocket launches stalled 5+ minutes until a
  queue_status read showed `paused_by`). A direct call that drives the character pauses a running queue at its start;
  when it then fails, the error opens with `this failed move_to paused your queue (plan #1, step 1 of 2 #job-1
  move_to): queue_resume resumes it; the call: ...` (a standing order: `the standing order keeps its steps for
  later`). `paused_by` reads `your move_to call failed while your queue ran (...)`, and while the queue stays paused
  that way every reply's team block carries `queue_paused: your queue is paused since your move_to failed 40s ago
  (...): queue_resume resumes it`. A failed read, a hand craft or a queue call pauses nothing and says nothing.
- C1 (Muse: three long walking tours; "no bot-fetch to player inventory"): already there. `requests` with no position
  sets the character's own logistic requests, and the network's logistic robots bring them while the character stands
  in its logistic area. Opus used it on shift35 at 131h: copper-plate 28 to 500 in about 80 s, advanced-circuit 38 to
  304 in 2 min. moving-items.md now says so with an example (its unfilled lines, clear, the item_count wait). No code.
- C2 (Haiku, about 10 times in 30 minutes: take ammo from a chest, then a rearm tour, skipping turrets with enemies
  near and coming back when they clear): a rearm `from` argument, not a queue plan.
  - `rearm {from: {position, count?}}`: a transfer of the ammo (default 200) from that chest to you, walking to it.
    The tour then runs with the other arguments once the take ends `transferred`, `collected` or `topped_up`
    (`then_after`: finish now runs a then_call after those outcomes too, not only after a met wait). In reach, the tour
    runs at once (`took_first`).
  - `retry_when_clear` now also covers turrets a tour leaves out for passing enemies (stock.screen records their
    positions, 64). Once the tour ends, it runs `rearm {positions: them, walk, retry_when_clear}` (`left_out_retry`),
    which waits for units_clear as a refused rearm does (6 tries in all).
- C3 (Haiku: a move_to --wait that exits 3 broke an && chain): exit 3 is a --wait that a tell, a mention or an urgent
  alert ended (or whose time ran out) while the walk goes on (host STILL_RUNNING_EXIT; stderr says so already).
  - A move_to --wait reply's first line now says whether the walk arrived (host/format.ts `walkLine`): `walk: arrived
    at (x,y)`, `walk: arrived (arrived_near)`, `walk: not arrived: unreachable`, or `walk: not arrived: move_to goes
    on, up to N s more; a tell from sol ended the wait (exit 3: fh wait waits for it again; --wait-through-tells: a
    tell or mention does not end the wait)`. JSON output gives it as result.walk.
  - The documented way for a chain is `--wait-through-tells` (movement-combat.md). `--require-met` stays with sleep
    and wait conditions.
- C4 (Grok: a breeder cycle in one call): collect's wait_ticks at one machine takes `give: {item: count}` (put in first
  by hand, in reach, as transfer infers the inventory: recipe input, else fuel) and `take_back: [items]`. At the wait's
  end (finish), the stacks of those items left in the machine's input and fuel go back to the character, each keeping
  its spoilage (`last.taken_back`). With `give` and `item` and no `count`, count is the recipe's yield of item (the
  pentapod-egg recipe on world n: 1 egg, 30 nutrients and 60 water make 2 eggs in 15 s).
- C5 (Grok: a full inventory hid the egg hatch times): `inventory` gives `spoiling`. These are the main inventory's
  spoilable stacks, soonest first (24, then `spoiling_more`), each with its slot, the time left (spoil_tick) and spoil
  percent. An item with spoil_to_trigger_result reads `hatches in` (pentapod-egg on world n; nutrients spoil to
  spoilage).

## d18 batch36 (the agents' 15:20 poll)

- `logistics_audit {network | position, backlog: true}` (A1, Luna and Grok, all of shift35: Gleba's science requester
  at (15.5,28.5) lacked 10 nutrients for about 36 minutes with about 98 in a provider 9 tiles off; logistics_audit said
  not_sent and "all 250 logistic bots occupied"). Per network: the oldest unfilled requests first (256 requester points
  read, 12 rows, `limit` up to 48): chest, item, short, `short_s` (how long since the networks watch first saw it
  short), the provider the game would take it from (select_pickup_point) with what it holds and what robots already
  reserve there (its targeted_items_pickup), and `held_by`, the first of these that reads true now: the delivery on
  the way covers it; no room in the chest; none in the network's providers or storage; no provider the game picks;
  every unit there reserved; no idle logistic robot (with how many hold cargo with no order and what, the orders the
  rest are on by type and what they carry, and the queue to charge); robots queued to charge with every charging slot
  taken; else idle robots and an unreserved provider, not sent yet (the game's dispatch is not exposed). `robots`:
  total, idle (available_logistic_robots), on orders by type (robot_order_queue), carrying (top 5), holding cargo
  with no order, charging and queued to charge (each cell's charging_robot_count and to_charge_robot_count), charging
  slots (each roboport's logistic_parameters.charging_station_count) and how many are free. Read from the game: those
  fields. Not read: when the game will dispatch a robot, and any minimum the game sends for (a requester chest has
  none the API shows). On world n (18 Oct, network #98 on Gleba, 122 requester points, 250 robots) it ran
  3.1-3.4 ms; in three reads a few minutes apart the robots were 201 holding cargo with no order (firearm-magazine 396,
  ice 348, agricultural-science-pack 36, cannon-shell 20) and 4 idle, then all 250 on orders (126 deliver, 124
  pickup) with 25 queued to charge, and nutrients read none free in the network for 21 short requesters.
- `launch_needs` (A2, viewer Aurora 15:36: Swiftlet waited at a stop for carbon fiber while the silo there could not
  finish rockets for want of processing units Swiftlet's hub held). On platform_schedule's reply, the platforms read
  of one platform, and each silo line of shipment's readiness read: for a stop that waits on items (an item_count or
  request wait) at the planet the platform is stopped at (else the stop it flies to), each rocket silo of ours there
  whose input holds less than one rocket part's worth of an ingredient while it has parts left to make, and what of
  that ingredient the waiting platform's own hub holds: `Swiftlet holds 400 processing-unit; rocket-silo (5.5,10.5)
  on fulgora: its rocket parts lack it (holds 0, 10 a part; parts 12/50)`. The silos come from the census pass (no
  search; a whole-surface find took 10.5 ms on Nauvis); 0.01-0.25 ms a platform on world n. Only rocket parts are
  read: a payload is the platform's own requests, which its hub already holds and asks more of.
- Stop waits as the game evaluates them (A3, Luna 15:58: an item-count OR time departure written without compare: "or"
  ran as and, so the gate held past the time fallback; viewer Aurora 16:09: Spindle needed repeated fixes).
  waitgroups.lua, for platform_schedule (stops and stop/wait) and train schedules:
  - Waits of more than one kind with no compare past the first are refused, naming the default and the way to say
    or: `stop 1: its waits mix item_count and time with no compare on wait 2; the game joins a wait with no compare by
    and (the default), so every one must hold. Say each: compare: "and" or compare: "or" ...`. Waits of one kind keep
    the default and. In shifts 33-36, 69 of 506 platform wait lists mixed kinds with no compare.
  - `wait: {any_of: [...]}` or `{all_of: [...]}` is written as the game's chain (any_of may hold all_of groups; the
    chain is ors of ands, so (a or b) and c is written as two all_of groups); read_as says so.
  - The readback groups the waits as the game evaluates them (and binds before or): `nauvis (fluid_count
    thruster-fuel >= 24000 or time 300s) [branch 2, time 300s, departs with no fuel condition]`. A branch is named when
    another branch has a fuel (thruster-fuel, or an item with a fuel value), oxidizer or ammunition condition and it
    has none.
  - A platform stop's `save_as: NAME` keeps its wait list (as written) in the harness's storage, and `wait_from: NAME`
    takes it on another stop or platform; read_as says which and who saved it.
- `configure {position, hand_size}` on an inserter, built or ghost (C1, Astra: a one-egg surplus export took a
  constant combinator and a stack size signal only to set hand size 1). The 2.0 inserter GUI has the setting: a
  forum thread asks to rename its "Stack size override", and Bilka renamed it "Override hand size" for 2.1.22
  (forums.factorio.com/viewtopic.php?p=646961). hand_size sets LuaEntity.inserter_stack_size_override: 1 up to the
  inserter's hand size now (1, its prototype's bonus and the force's inserter or bulk capacity bonus), 0 or false
  for none. Returns hand_size, hand_size_before, hand_max, and circuit_note when the inserter's circuit set stack
  size is on (that signal sets the hand while it is on the wires). It goes with filters and spoil_priority in the
  same call. No combinator is placed.
- `wake: {near: N}` on sleep, wait_ticks and wait_until, `fh ... --wake-near N` (B1, Haiku: an urgent alert every 15-30
  s on Nauvis woke each wait). Only an attack on our structures or buildings of ours destroyed within N tiles of the
  character (1..200) wake it as urgent; every other urgent alert (enemy groups, platform hits, a teammate's death, power
  cut or collapse, an outpost's output, a captive spawner) is held and given with the reply: `held_alerts` (up to 8
  lines) and `held_alerts_count` (a direct wait's `last` has them). Damage to the character, tells and mentions wake as
  before. The direct wait_until now takes `wake_on_urgent` too: the scheduler's schema lacked it, so `fh call
  wait_until --no-urgent` and `--urgent-radius` were refused as an unknown argument.
- Each leg re-checked before it starts (B2, Haiku: 8 hits from big spitters at (-112,240) on a rearm tour whose walk
  started clear). A tour's next stop (rearm, feed, refuel, collect, recover, transfer tours) and a move_to's next via
  leg are checked against enemy groups and enemy units seen now (and demolishers): one whose reach (24 tiles) the
  straight leg passes through stops the walk where it stands, outcome `enemies_ahead`, and `last.why` /
  `last.enemies_ahead` name it with what it does and where it stopped: `the leg from (-100,200) to (-120,280) passes 1
  enemy unit (1 big-spitter) at (-110,238), 7.6 tiles from it: moving units (big-spitter (-110,238) wandering, facing
  west); stopped at (-100.0,200.0) before it, 3 of 7 stops done`. unsafe_goal (true or "moving") walks on;
  avoid_enemies false checks nothing.

  it out): every move into one says `request` (`requester-chest asks iron-plate 150..250; it holds 300 now: 50 over its
  request max (trash unrequested off)`) and `over_request`; `up_to_request: true` moves only up to its request (its
  max, else its min). The request is summed over the chest's active sections for that item and quality.
- Cargo bays in a dry run (C2, Astra twice: two placeable bays that joined nothing, mined and moved after inspect said
  not_connected_to_hub_or_pad). place_ghosts, build and paste dry runs give `cargo_bays`: each planned bay joins the
  platform hub or the landing pad (touching it edge to edge, or through a bay that does: built, a ghost, or one planned
  before it) or joins nothing, with the nearest joined one and its distance; and per hub or pad its slots now, its own,
  the built bays joined, and the slots after the planned bays join. A bay's slots are not in the API (cargo-bay has no
  inventory_size_bonus on 2.0.77): they are read from the hub or pad, its slots now less its prototype's own over the
  built bays joined to it (on world n a pad's own is 80, a hub's 59); with no built bay joined, the reply says so.
- `clear_obstacles: true` on build and place_ghosts (C1, Opus, 3 times placing small cells: each tree in a footprint
  stopped the batch). The trees and rocks (a simple entity the game counts as a rock) in the entries' footprints are
  marked for deconstruction, as a player's planner marks them; those in reach are mined by hand (a timed construct
  over them, as move_to's mine_out does), the rest are left to the construction robots. Once every one is gone the call
  runs again, without clear_obstacles (watched 10 min; `last.cleared` says which). Returns cleared (what was marked),
  mining, robots, then_runs; with none in the way the call runs at once and cleared says so. Dry runs give
  `trees_rocks`: the trees and rocks in the planned footprints.
- `silo {surface: "all"}` or `silo {all: true}` (D1, Gemini): every silo of ours on every planet (16 at most) in one
  call, a line each: its rocket parts (as the silo read says them) and their rate, what is aboard, the platform its
  automatic requests fill for with what of that request it holds, and next_auto_launch; `silos` keeps each silo's full
  read. The silos come from the census pass (one search a planet before the first pass). On world n: 9 silos on 5
  planets in 4.6 ms.
- Train actions that omit coordinates (D2, Gemini: in shifts 33-36 `train {}` read "position requires x and y" 17
  times, and `train {id}` / `{train}` were unknown arguments 16 times). The actions that take a position: train
  (position or train_id; stops and all read every stop or train), train_stop (position, name) and rail_route (from,
  to). Each names what is missing with its shape: `train needs which train or stop: position {x, y} (a locomotive,
  wagon or train stop, as the map shows it; surface for another planet) or train_id N ...`, `train_stop needs position
  {x, y}: a spot beside a straight rail ...`, `rail_route needs from: from {x, y} (where the rails start) and to {x,
  y} ...`. train {id: N} and {train: N} run as train_id (corrected says so).
- `shipment {ledger: true, surface?}` (D3, Luna 15:48: the silo chain inferred across cargo, shipment and inspect; an
  LDS delivery that looked done did not reach the feeders): the surface's cargo ledger in time order. Each rocket
  launched up, recorded as it goes (ledger.lua, on the game's launch-ordered event): `up #12, 4m10s ago: rocket-silo
  (15.5,59.5) launched low-density-structure*50 to Wren; Wren asked low-density-structure 100 (holds 20) (its
  automatic requests)`. Each drop down (drops.lua's records, now with what the pad asked for the items then): `down
  drop #7, ...: from Wren, iron-plate*100; the pad asked iron-plate 200 (held 0); landed in ...; the pad held ... and
  in the 20 s after: iron-plate: logistic robots took 100 (first orders: ...) (verdict)`. Ids follow an entry. What it
  cannot know: launches before this runtime ran, more than 64 launches a surface, drops beyond the 20 drops.lua keeps,
  and a drop's pad asks before this runtime (the note says so).
- D1 fix (operator 16:03): after a stream service restart, a re-read backlog line in viewer-relayed.jsonl reads
  relayed; one the verdict logs refused keeps that verdict; any other carries no delivery and logs nothing.

## d18 batch37 (the agents' 16:50 poll)

- `supply {item, surface?, makers: "all", from?}` (A1, A3; Opus about 10 times a shift with a 16-call grid script,
  Astra 4+, Haiku: which shell maker lacked what). Every machine of ours on the surface whose recipe makes the item,
  from the census pass's per-recipe lists (no search; a machine built since its last pass of the surface is not in
  them), nearest you first, 24 a call (`next_from`). Each row: position, recipe, status, and why when it is not
  working: its own circuit or logistic condition with what it reads now, an input inserter off by its condition, or the
  ingredients it is short of; its rate now (crafts a minute at its speed and productivity, times the item a craft); its
  inputs against one craft (`tungsten-plate 0/4`); what its output holds; and what its output inserters drop into.
  `makers`, `by_status`, `by_recipe`. On world n (Nauvis): 13 gear makers in 0.85 ms, 20 circuit makers in 1.6 ms; the
  first call after a load also reads every recipe once for those that make the item (2.4-3.6 ms, kept after).
- supply's `makers_worst` (A2, Opus): a machine off by its own circuit or logistic condition now ranks with those an
  input inserter's condition holds back, so it is among the worst three with its condition and what it reads (it ranked
  last, behind every machine short of an ingredient).
- D3 (viewer Aurora, Sol 14:07: reminder 59, a shared review, reached 10 missed runs for Grok and 16 for Sonnet before a
  viewer asked): reminders.lua tells the owner when a recipient has missed 2 runs. It is one tell from `reminder #N`
  naming the recipient, the reminder and its cadence, how long it has waited, the last result (by whom, how long ago)
  and the `reminder_edit {id, recipients: [...]}` call without that recipient. It goes once until that recipient
  acknowledges or the recipients change, and never about the owner's own runs. The reminders read gives `missed`
  ({name: runs}) and states says "the owner told"; the stream service's reminders snapshot passes `missed` to the site,
  whose chips show the states.
- D4 (Nick 14:10: route viewer lines that name no agent by what they are about; tools/stream/router.py, viewers.py):
  - The rules that work are kept (named or @ agents, @operator, @viewer, staff, chatter). For the rest:
    - A platform or planet the line names maps to its owners by the board (open claims, and the tasks, requests and
      projects agents hold), when one or two hold it. This is deterministic and needs no Clef: "to Sol: about
      Wayfarer".
    - Else a second choice question in the same Clef batch call: each agent by its work (one line from live state:
      where, its board doing line, what it holds), the agent this viewer was just talking to (`same`), the operator
      (to the inbox) or other viewers (shown, never relayed; only at 0.8). Two agents when both are at 0.3 and
      together at 0.5.
    - Clef unavailable or under 0.5: today's rotation, which keeps a viewer's agent of the last 5 minutes. The
      delivery says "in turn (Clef unsure)".

- Transfer chains (C1, Sonnet: 10+ chained transfers a brick cycle; a failure mid-chain left items in the pack):
  `transfer {steps: [{take: [{x,y}, ...], item, count?}, {give: [{x,y}, ...], item, split?: "even" | "fill", count?}], on_fail?}`
  walks the chests in order in one call (32 at most; transferchain.lua over stock.lua's courier legs, never re-routed).
  A take takes the item (`count` in all across its chests, default all); a give gives what you hold of it: `fill` (default)
  all that fits at each in turn, `even` an even share of what is held now at each chest left in the step, `count` at
  most that many in all. The first leg that fails (the entity gone, a transfer refused) or is not reached ends it:
  `last.chain_held` (what of its items you hold) and `last.chain_left` (each leg left: step, take or give, item, position).
  `on_fail: "return"` then walks what the chain took and you still hold back to the chests it came from, as a transfer
  chain of its own started next tick (`last.chain_return`; that walk's last has `started_by` and `chain_failed`, the
  failed chain's outcome, error, held and left). `keep` (default) leaves it in your pack.

  lines) and `held_alerts_count` (a direct wait's `last` has them). Damage to the character, tells and mentions wake as
  before. The direct wait_until now takes `wake_on_urgent` too: the scheduler's schema lacked it, so `fh call
  wait_until --no-urgent` and `--urgent-radius` were refused as an unknown argument.
- Each leg re-checked before it starts (B2, Haiku: 8 hits from big spitters at (-112,240) on a rearm tour whose walk
  started clear). A tour's next stop (rearm, feed, refuel, collect, recover, transfer tours) and a move_to's next via
  leg are checked against enemy groups and enemy units seen now (and demolishers): one whose reach (24 tiles) the
  straight leg passes through stops the walk where it stands, outcome `enemies_ahead`, and `last.why` /
  `last.enemies_ahead` name it with what it does and where it stopped: `the leg from (-100,200) to (-120,280) passes 1
  enemy unit (1 big-spitter) at (-110,238), 7.6 tiles from it: moving units (big-spitter (-110,238) wandering, facing
  west); stopped at (-100.0,200.0) before it, 3 of 7 stops done`. unsafe_goal (true or "moving") walks on;
  avoid_enemies false checks nothing.
- rotate in the remote and platform queue lanes (C4, Astra: queue_submit refused steps[7] rotate in the remote lane though
  a direct rotate takes platform): a rotate step with platform (on that platform) or surface (by remote view on a
  planet) goes in lane remote or platform:NAME, as the direct call takes it; without either it is refused there.
- transfer into a requester or buffer chest (C3, Grok: a hand transfer over the request went to trash and robots hauled
  it out): every move into one says `request` (`requester-chest asks iron-plate 150..250; it holds 300 now: 50 over its
  request max (trash unrequested off)`) and `over_request`; `up_to_request: true` moves only up to its request (its
  max, else its min). The request is summed over the chest's active sections for that item and quality.
- Cargo bays in a dry run (C2, Astra twice: two placeable bays that joined nothing, mined and moved after inspect said
  not_connected_to_hub_or_pad). place_ghosts, build and paste dry runs give `cargo_bays`: each planned bay joins the
  platform hub or the landing pad (touching it edge to edge, or through a bay that does: built, a ghost, or one planned
  before it) or joins nothing, with the nearest joined one and its distance; and per hub or pad its slots now, its own,
  the built bays joined, and the slots after the planned bays join. A bay's slots are not in the API (cargo-bay has no
  inventory_size_bonus on 2.0.77): they are read from the hub or pad, its slots now less its prototype's own over the
  built bays joined to it (on world n a pad's own is 80, a hub's 59); with no built bay joined, the reply says so.
- `clear_obstacles: true` on build and place_ghosts (C1, Opus, 3 times placing small cells: each tree in a footprint
  stopped the batch). The trees and rocks (a simple entity the game counts as a rock) in the entries' footprints are
  marked for deconstruction, as a player's planner marks them; those in reach are mined by hand (a timed construct
  over them, as move_to's mine_out does), the rest are left to the construction robots. Once every one is gone the call
  runs again, without clear_obstacles (watched 10 min; `last.cleared` says which). Returns cleared (what was marked),
  mining, robots, then_runs; with none in the way the call runs at once and cleared says so. Dry runs give
  `trees_rocks`: the trees and rocks in the planned footprints.
- `silo {surface: "all"}` or `silo {all: true}` (D1, Gemini): every silo of ours on every planet (16 at most) in one
  call, a line each: its rocket parts (as the silo read says them) and their rate, what is aboard, the platform its
  automatic requests fill for with what of that request it holds, and next_auto_launch; `silos` keeps each silo's full
  read. The silos come from the census pass (one search a planet before the first pass). On world n: 9 silos on 5
  planets in 4.6 ms.
- Train actions that omit coordinates (D2, Gemini: in shifts 33-36 `train {}` read "position requires x and y" 17
  times, and `train {id}` / `{train}` were unknown arguments 16 times). The actions that take a position: train
  (position or train_id; stops and all read every stop or train), train_stop (position, name) and rail_route (from,
  to). Each names what is missing with its shape: `train needs which train or stop: position {x, y} (a locomotive,
  wagon or train stop, as the map shows it; surface for another planet) or train_id N ...`, `train_stop needs position
  {x, y}: a spot beside a straight rail ...`, `rail_route needs from: from {x, y} (where the rails start) and to {x,
  y} ...`. train {id: N} and {train: N} run as train_id (corrected says so).
- `shipment {ledger: true, surface?}` (D3, Luna 15:48: the silo chain inferred across cargo, shipment and inspect; an
  LDS delivery that looked done did not reach the feeders): the surface's cargo ledger in time order. Each rocket
  launched up, recorded as it goes (ledger.lua, on the game's launch-ordered event): `up #12, 4m10s ago: rocket-silo
  (15.5,59.5) launched low-density-structure*50 to Wren; Wren asked low-density-structure 100 (holds 20) (its
  automatic requests)`. Each drop down (drops.lua's records, now with what the pad asked for the items then): `down
  drop #7, ...: from Wren, iron-plate*100; the pad asked iron-plate 200 (held 0); landed in ...; the pad held ... and
  in the 20 s after: iron-plate: logistic robots took 100 (first orders: ...) (verdict)`. Ids follow an entry. What it
  cannot know: launches before this runtime ran, more than 64 launches a surface, drops beyond the 20 drops.lua keeps,
  and a drop's pad asks before this runtime (the note says so).
- D1 fix (operator 16:03): after a stream service restart, a re-read backlog line in viewer-relayed.jsonl reads
  relayed; one the verdict logs refused keeps that verdict; any other carries no delivery and logs nothing.
- D3 (viewer Aurora, Sol 14:07: reminder 59, a shared review, reached 10 missed runs for Grok and 16 for Sonnet before a
  viewer asked): reminders.lua tells the owner when a recipient has missed 2 runs. It is one tell from `reminder #N`
  naming the recipient, the reminder and its cadence, how long it has waited, the last result (by whom, how long ago)
  and the `reminder_edit {id, recipients: [...]}` call without that recipient. It goes once until that recipient
  acknowledges or the recipients change, and never about the owner's own runs. The reminders read gives `missed`
  ({name: runs}) and states says "the owner told"; the stream service's reminders snapshot passes `missed` to the site,
  whose chips show the states.
- D4 (Nick 14:10: route viewer lines that name no agent by what they are about; tools/stream/router.py, viewers.py):
  - The rules that work are kept (named or @ agents, @operator, @viewer, staff, chatter). For the rest:
    - A platform or planet the line names maps to its owners by the board (open claims, and the tasks, requests and
      projects agents hold), when one or two hold it. This is deterministic and needs no Clef: "to Sol: about
      Wayfarer".
    - Else a second choice question in the same Clef batch call: each agent by its work (one line from live state:
      where, its board doing line, what it holds), the agent this viewer was just talking to (`same`), the operator
      (to the inbox) or other viewers (shown, never relayed; only at 0.8). Two agents when both are at 0.3 and
      together at 0.5.
    - Clef unavailable or under 0.5: today's rotation, which keeps a viewer's agent of the last 5 minutes. The
      delivery says "in turn (Clef unsure)".
  - Off by default: the switch is runs/RUN/viewers-route.on, beside viewers-relay.on. serve.py hands the relay the team
    each snapshot (Relay.set_team). The verdict log keeps each line's route.
  - The site's delivery shows the route and why: "to Sol: about Wayfarer", "to Muse: about its work (...)".
  - About 1,800 characters a routed line with 9 agents, so about 1.7 cents per 1,000 routed lines. Only unaddressed
    lines are asked: 52 of 199 passed today.
  - tools/stream/route_replay.py replays verdict logs through it against the game chat's record of whom each line
    went to (with the team as the live state shows it now).
- D2 (viewer Aurora 12:5x: "Keep routine digests to changed blockers, failed checks and needed decisions, routed to
  their owners. Keep full censuses on demand"): the scheduled digest (idle_nudge.py at deadline - 2 h,
  tools/factory_digest.py) is a delta against the last digest, this run's or the run it resumed from.
  - Its facts: per surface, the blockers (drills with no resources, input shortage and full output by machine type,
    boilers and furnaces without fuel, labs not working); the failed checks (lessons whose check is not met); and
    the decisions needed (items blocked, requests nobody owns). Each is said when it is new, has moved (by 2 and a
    fifth) or has cleared.
  - Each fact goes to its owner. A position goes to the claim holding it. A surface goes to every open claim on it,
    else to the agents holding items whose title names it (at most 3). Otherwise it goes to the team, and so does a
    request nobody owns.
  - One tell list per recipient: "Factory digest, changed since the last one (tick T, N game min ago): blockers: ...;
    failed checks: ...; decisions needed: ...". Nothing changed: no tell.
  - The full census goes to the team on request (`idle_nudge.py --digest-now`).
  - Reads: factory_digest, and operator board reads for claims, blocked items, open requests and held items. The
    operator may now read `lessons` (board.lua M.operator); a runtime without it gives no failed checks.
  - On world n now, the first delta would be 14 tells to 8 agents and the team, against 13 census tells to everyone.

## d18 batch38 (the 18:20 poll; eng/d18-batch38)

- A1 (Sol 18:21: platform_schedule refused for no_schedule while the platform began flying moments later; duplicate
  edits and reversals followed):
  - The state was read in the call's tick, but the game updates a platform in a later tick. On shift36, Cinder
    (`next: true` at tick 29119760) was flying 39 ticks later, and Wayfarer (`stop 2, go: true` at 29611678) left
    within 265 ticks. Calls whose platform still read no_schedule 175-334 ticks later stayed put.
  - Now a no_schedule or no_path read starts a recheck (space.lua `M.recheck_read`): read every 10 ticks for up to 300,
    ending as soon as it reads otherwise. paused is still read at once.
  - A queue step (body or platform lane) waits for that read (scheduler.lua) and fails only when it still reads so,
    with both reads in the reason. A direct call's reply has `recheck` and its line, and the second read comes as a
    tell from `platform_schedule`.
- A2 (Grok 18:20, twice: copper from Petrel read "to the ground (no pad takes it)" and landed in the pad at (54,8),
  shift36 drops #1496 and #1498):
  - A pod waiting to launch or rising names no station yet, and the game lands a platform's pods for a planet in that
    planet's landing pad. Every shift36 drop to Gleba landed in its pad, whatever the pad's requests.
  - pods.lua: with no station named, the force's landing pad on that surface (one bounded find), marked `guessed` and
    read again while the pod flies. The ground only with no landing pad of ours there.
  - The arrival alert, the team block and where_is say it: "the landing pad at (54,8) (gleba's pad: pods from a
    platform land in it; this one names no station yet)".
- A3 (Astra; withdrawn 18:22, the worm was alive): each worm or spawner robot_dispatch warns of carries its read's
  age (avoid.lua's chunk cache, at most a minute old) and whether its chunk is in sight now ("read 10s ago, its chunk
  charted, not in sight now").
- A4 (Astra: "its network holds no big-electric-pole" while a robot carried one to it):
  - ghosts reads the flying robot with an order on the ghost first. One holding the item reads "in transit: a
    construction robot carries ITEM to it (N tiles away, its order K)" with `in_transit`. The shortage now says "its
    network holds no ITEM and no robot carries one to it".
  - construction_robots `sources` gives, per group, how many are in transit in robots' cargo (and the nearest), then
    the chests (or "no chest in the network holds it") for the rest only.
- B1 (Haiku, 3 times: "construct stops the whole batch when one item is missing: a 4-laser + pole batch built 0
  poles"):
  - Found on shift36: construct already skips a ghost whose item is neither held nor crafting and builds the rest
    (construction.lua). In Haiku's batches at ticks 29635899 and 29637477, the 3 medium poles were left out inside a
    spitter spawner's sight ((-26,-394), 40 tiles), and the 2 laser ghosts it took up were skipped (no lasers held).
    The reply's `materials` counted every ghost in the area, so a laser shortage and the poles' left out read as one.
  - Now the reply has a `line`: the ghosts it builds by name, those you hold too few for, and those left out inside
    an enemy's reach. The result's `last.line` says "built 0 of the 2 ghosts it took up; skipped, item missing ...:
    2 laser-turret short; left out inside an enemy's reach ... : 3 medium-electric-pole, 2 laser-turret".
- B2 (Haiku: big pole ghosts whose network held none, 3 times; a pole ghost outside every roboport's construction
  area): robot_dispatch (place_ghosts, paste and blueprint_place dry runs; robottrips.lua) says, per group of ghosts
  (item and 32-tile cell):
  - "2 big-electric-pole ghosts near (11,10): network 5 covering them holds no big-electric-pole";
  - "1 big-electric-pole ghost near (67,3): no roboport's construction area covers it; the nearest roboport, roboport
    (0,0) (network 5), covers 55 tiles round it, and it is 12 tiles outside that". The construction area is a
    square, and the cells read are our networks' on the surface, the first 2048. On world n, 153 cells took 0.3 ms.
- B3 (Luna: the only roboport that landed was built at a duplicate ghost (67,44), not the claimed one at (204,69)):
  the game sets no build priority among ghosts. ghostlist.lua `contested(surface, force, item, from)` gives the entity
  ghosts of ours in the construction area of the network covering `from` that the item places, when there are more
  than the network holds. Each ghost has where it is, the claim holding it and its owner, and its distance from
  `from`. It runs only when the network holds 16 or fewer: the search covers the network's box, 9 ms for Nauvis's on
  world n, 0.9 ms for Gleba's.
  - The drop's landing line: for the first 2 such items sent, from where it landed.
  - deconstruct (dry run and live) `contested`: for the items the marked entities free (the first 2).
  - ghosts read `contested`: per network and item, from the network's pickup point for it, at most 3 searches a read.
- Waiting out a leg enemies pass (U1, Haiku shift37: a 480-tile rearm leg was cut 5 times in 2 minutes by units and
  an attack group passing it, retry_when_clear or not). batch36 B2's leg check (stock.lua) now waits when the action
  has `ahead_wait`. That is rearm by default, and a walking transfer (or a transfer chain) with `retry_when_clear: true`.
  The character stands where it is and rechecks the leg every 3 s. Once the leg is clear it walks on, and
  `last.ahead_waited` names each wait: seconds, where, before which stop, what held it. If the leg is still unclear
  when the wait runs out (`retry_ticks` with retry_when_clear, else 60 s), the tour ends with `enemies_ahead`, saying
  how long it waited. The wait is added to the tour's time. `retry_when_clear: false` on rearm keeps the old behavior,
  which ends the tour at once.
- Alert waits and repeats (U2, Haiku shift37: three `wait --until alert` in a row woke after 29 s, 1 s and 1 s on the
  same attack #8793 as its hit count grew). A sleep or wait with `until: alert` records the attacks known when it
  begins: each one's attackers seen, its hits, and the loss count (urgent.lua alert_known). Such an attack wakes the
  wait only when it changed: more attackers seen (a group joined), or one of ours lost within 48 tiles of it since the
  wait began. The line then says `(changed since your wait began: ...)`. A new attack, a new enemy group and nest news
  wake it as before (`(new since your wait began)`). Hits alone are held. The reply's `alert_held`, also on fh wait's
  line, gives each known attack's hits held ("held the repeats of attack #8793 hit 6 more times ..."), whatever woke
  the wait. Urgent wakes (urgent.lua) are unchanged: they are told once each.
- C1 (Sonnet: many chests to many chests) is left for batch37 C1 (transfer `steps`), which is not done yet: batch37 is
  at its Group A checkpoint. The short form `from: [positions], to: [positions], item, count` belongs with it.
- C2 (Sonnet: load_silo should split by rocket by default): with `launch`, a list over one rocket's lift or cargo slots
  now goes as rockets of at most a full rocket each, one load_silo step each appended to the queue. The reply has
  `rockets`, `rocket_cargo` ("rocket 1: agricultural-science-pack 600", ...) and `split`. `launch_split: false`
  refuses it, naming the split. `all_or_nothing` and `wait_platform`, one rocket each, still refuse unless
  `launch_split: true`.
- C3 (Sonnet: "the silo part rate (0.3/min idle vs 55/min while a load waits) is confusing"): each 10-s sample of a
  silo's products_finished now keeps what the silo was doing: building parts, short of an ingredient, or holding a
  built rocket. `parts_rate` gives the rate, its window and the time in each state, counted at each interval's start:
  "5 a minute over the last 10m00s (samples at most every 10 s): building parts 1m00s (50 a minute then), holding a
  built rocket (no parts until it launches) 9m00s". The `silo {surface: "all"}` lines add "(N while building)".
- C4 (Grok 18:20: about 200 agricultural packs were inside 5 minutes of spoiling after Petrel left): a silo alert,
  `silo_spoils` (pushalerts.lua `silo_spoils`, to the silo's builder as silo alerts go).
  - For each platform of ours not at the silo's planet whose hub asks this planet for a spoilable item, the stacks of
    it in the silo's rocket and in the storage and provider chests of the silo's network (32 chests an item) that
    spoil before that platform's next arrival here.
  - The ETA is the current leg's when it flies here, else freight.before_departure through its schedule.
  - "250 agricultural-science-pack staged for Petrel (its hub asks gleba for it) spoil before its next arrival here
    in about 600s: the first in 300s (the silo's rocket); in storage-chest (24.5,47.5) 50, the silo's rocket 200".
  - Read at most every 30 s a silo, ahead of the silo's other alerts. 0.09 ms for Gleba's silo on world n.
- Silo and shipment on one launch (batch39 B1, Astra 138h31). Astra's journal shows no lag: the silo read at 02:44:37
  (ready, last launch 3m05s ago) came 14 s before the cryogenic launch, and the next silo read, at 02:44:56, said
  launching, last launch 5 s ago. shipment's "launched 32 s ago" at 02:45:24 was that launch. silo.lua's records,
  freight.lua's incoming list (shipment's "launched" line) and the cargo ledger are all written in the same
  on_rocket_launch_ordered event. The ledger now runs first and its launch id travels with the other two. silo's last
  launch reads `last launch 1m31s ago (up #7, tick T) to ...`, shipment's `a rocket launched 32s ago (up #7, tick T)
  carries ...`, and `shipment {ledger}` lists `up #7`. Each silo row has `read_tick`, and its line ends
  `read at tick T`.
- A burner stopped by its own spoilage (batch39 B2, Grok: the nutrient chamber at (7.5,24.5) at energy 0, spoilage in
  its slots, its status busy, the egg loop stalled for minutes). burnt.lua's full burnt-result slot (shift14) was
  already read by inspect, scan, supply, the status survey and makers. Now:
  - `fuel_unusable`: nothing burning and a fuel slot holding only what the burner does not burn (spoilage in a
    biochamber), said the same way, with the slots' contents.
  - supply.makers {makers: "all"} gives the line as each row's why.
  - A burner alert: the seed check's surface turn (every 10 s, one surface) reads the census crafters whose prototype
    burns fuel. Each that is stopped is told once, waking, to its builder: what it makes and what fills its slots.
    It is told again only after the machine ran.
- Another planet's map (D1; Sol on Aquilo could not survey Nauvis; Astra 17:29 planned Nauvis defenses lake to lake from
  Aquilo). `map`, `grid` and `observe` are in bots.lua's SURFACE_ACTIONS: `surface: NAME` reads that planet by remote
  view.
  - On another planet they need `position` there (grid takes `area` too), since your character stands elsewhere.
    `position` must be in a charted chunk, as before.
  - Only what our force has charted is read. map: charted chunks, as before. grid: its water now only in charted chunks.
    observe: entities by the known rule (enemy units only where visible), as before.
  - `observe {tile_runs: true, tile_names?, tiles_limit?}` gives the charted tiles in the radius (up to 32) as runs
    along x, row by row: `[{x,y,count,name}]`, `tile_count`, with `tile_runs_truncated` past tiles_limit (1024 runs by
    default). Pass tile_names to keep only some, e.g. a lake's water.
  - `tiles_limit` is now in observe's schema (the code read it before, but the arg check refused it).
- Where a deconstructed item went (D3, Astra: recovered artillery silently built an older ghost elsewhere). A robot's
  mining of one of our entities, or of an item on the ground (on_robot_mined_entity; trees, rocks and other neutral
  clearing are skipped), is followed by deconwent.lua every second.
  - While the robot holds the item: the order it flies. When it carries the item to a ghost, the ghost and who placed
    it.
  - When the robot no longer holds it, one of: it built that ghost (an entity of the ghost's name now stands there);
    it put the item into a storage chest within 3 tiles; or neither was seen.
  - A storage chest is then watched. A construction robot within 8 tiles holding the item when the chest's count
    falls is followed the same way (3 robots a record).
  - Limits: 16 followed at once, 2 minutes a robot, 5 minutes a chest, 32 records kept.
  - `where_is {item}` gives `deconstructed`: the last 6 for that item or entity name on the surface, each step with
    its time after the mining.
  - The robot-built event is not forwarded to the runtime (control.lua's fixed list, which only a mod reload changes),
    so a build is known by the entity standing at the ghost's place. An item taken from storage may be another of the
    same name in that chest.
- Compact replies (batch39 C1, Astra, about 30 times a shift with a local JSON projection). `fields: [...]` (a list,
  or one string joined by `|` or `,`, as scan's) on platform, platforms, inspect and status returns only those fields.
  A field is matched as a top-level key, a key of each row, or one level down (`"hub.cargo"`). Rows are platforms'
  rows and inspect's results or entities, and each row keeps its name and position. A name this reply lacks that the
  read can have (its describe text names it, or an earlier reply had it: eta_min, leg, freshness in some states only)
  is listed in `absent` (batch90 AZ3: 177 such refusals in s55-57); a name the read never has is refused with the names
  the reply has. The read runs whole (M.project cuts the reply), so the game-side cost is the
  same; the agent's context is what shrinks.
- The refusals the harness's own wording invited (batch90 AZ3, the AU1 review's finding 6: unknown-argument refusals
  rose 115, 151, 179 over shifts 55-57):
  - `board_plan {doing}` takes up to 240 characters (at 160, 101 refusals in s57, 27% of writes; the median refused
    line was 179).
  - `chat_ack {all: true}` is `{seq: "all"}`; the unread-tells line reads `chat_ack {seq: N} or {seq: "all"}`.
  - Aliases: `scan {centre}`, `inspect {at}` and `nearest {centre}` are `position`; `rates {items}` is `item`;
    `nearest {count}` is `limit`, `{entity_names}` is `name`.
  - `describe {action}` (a name or a list of 1..16) returns only those entries, and for a name there is not, the
    closest real ones (`unknown`).
  - `reminders {id}` reads that one reminder (the whole read it fell back to was 30-98 KB).
  - An unknown action is refused naming the closest real ones (`unsupported action; closest: technologies; call
    describe`): one that contains the name or that it contains, or a typo of up to 2 letters, else one sharing a
    word of 3+ letters, at most 6; the host adds their reference topics.
  - `fh call help|more|wait ...` runs `fh help`, `fh more` or `fh wait`.
  - `nearest {surface | platform}` reads there by remote view, as scan does: what the map shows there, charted chunks
    only (a planet needs `position` there; a platform is centred on its hub).
- A whole leg's production (batch39 C2, Sol: a wrapper sampled every 1-2 min, and dock bursts looked sustainable).
  freight.lua's segments (each stop and each leg) now keep thruster fuel and oxidizer made and used (fluid statistics
  totals) at their start and end, beside the ammunition counts they kept already. `platform_production {platform,
  leg: true}` gives two windows:
  - Since the platform last departed: the leg and the stop after it so far.
  - While it is stopped, the last full leg alone.
  Each window has each fluid's and ammunition's made and used (totals, a minute, net a minute), cargo loaded (rockets
  launched to it) and cargo dropped (its cargo pods received by a landing pad or landed as containers; those gone
  before leaving are not counted), with the window's ticks. A leg that began before this runtime has no fuel sample,
  and says so. When the cargo records cannot be read, fuel and ammunition still stand (`cargo not read: ...`).
- belt_route on a platform with an ejection end (batch39 C3, Sol: about 10 min and 6 dry runs on Wayfarer).
  belt_route was already in SURFACE_ACTIONS (a platform's name as `surface`). It is now also in PLATFORM_ACTIONS, so
  `platform: NAME` works. route.lua plans by can_place_entity, which keeps the line to foundation and to free
  footprints, and an underground pair never passes under empty space (UNDER).
  - `eject: true` (or an inserter name; default inserter) with `to` near the hull edge looks within 6 tiles of `to`
    for the nearest tile where that inserter, on foundation, picks from a belt tile and drops onto empty space
    (targets.lua's pickup and drop points by direction, both free to place).
  - The route then ends on that belt tile, and the inserter's ghost goes with the line's ghosts.
  - The reply's `eject` names the belt, the inserter and its facing, and the drop tile. No spot found is refused,
    with the radius.
- D1 with batch37 D2 (Sol: hub stock against each belt reader; a filter set from a constant minus a whole-belt reader
  starved the crusher feed): circuit_audit {platform} gives `feeders` (circaudit.lua `feeder`).
  - Each inserter of ours whose filters the circuit sets or which the circuit turns on and off gets one line: what it
    takes now, its pickup and the signals on its red and green networks.
  - The line follows the combinators putting out onto those networks and what their inputs read, 3 deep, wire by wire
    (player wires only), and names constant combinators.
  - The hub's read is said apart ("its own signal").
  - Each belt reader there: its mode and the belts its count covers. Hold is its own belt. Whole belt is the game's
    segment, in flow order: the straight input at a side-load, undergrounds to their pair, stopping at a splitter or a
    change of segment length. Then what it holds now of the inserter's items, the belts of it past the inserter's
    pickup ("it cannot take what they hold", with the count there), and belts side-loading inside the count (marked
    when upstream of the pickup).

    already holds.

    `board_held_count` come with the wake. An @-mention of the agent in a board edit is a chat mention and still
    wakes, unless `wake_on_messages: false`. A runtime from before this: the host says so on stderr.

    ledger (ledger.lua `latest_to`): "#57 from gleba 12s ago (bioflux*400)".

  - research_done's entries give `level`, the level done by the same rule.

    research_use and unlocks checks read named finite technologies or `researched` sets. An infinite technology's
    levels never appear there, which is unchanged. researchtarget already used level > N.
  - Not seen on n: whether on_research_finished's technology already reads the next level. The done log assumes it
    does, as the 10-s poll path sees it.

  hull edge holding 3 iron ore. It builds on belt_flow's lane_mix (batch35 B2) and trace's lane reads (batch32 B1);
  side-load merges are not re-read here.

  private copy the call was 33 ms for that area on Nauvis, 240 ms for 17 machines with 13 short on Vulcanus, and 0.7 to
  1.9 s for dense 128x128 areas of Nauvis. Each short item's donor search found every holder within 64 tiles again

  16 come back in `left`; with all, a machine short of nothing gives its line only (32 machines' reply was 26 KB, 9 ms
  to encode).

  block:
  - threat.watch (25 to 35 ms with 430 spawners within 512 tiles) is now asked for in the reply and read in the
    background (threat.watch_step: listed in one tick, then 64 spawners a tick, then the news). Its sort and

- Item 5 (Sol 16:45, operator-inbox seq 874: `fh call sleep {seconds: 40, wake_on_messages: false, wake_from:
  [operator], wake_on_board: false, wake_local: true}` woke after 4 s on Luna's ordinary tell, and after 22 s on
  Astra's): `fh call sleep` runs the host's sleep loop (it polls sleep_check), and that loop built the runtime's
  `sleep` from the command-line flags only: the journal shows `sleep {seconds: 40}` sent, every wake argument dropped.
  Now the call's arguments past `seconds` and `condition` go to the runtime's sleep, over what the flags say (a call's

  (board.deliver): batch43's split tells (parts before the last fyi) and batch41's edit tells (from the editing agent)

  station called (it was waiting at nauvis), the records and their waits kept`; `paused` may go with it. A `current`

  one, stops with current rewrites the schedule`.

  after the departure and waited for a later one): a platform_schedule call that makes the platform leave its station
  records the departure (from, tick, who; the reply says `departed: left aquilo at tick T ...`), and `platform_left`
  counts it when the wait began in the same tick or up to 60 ticks after (a queue's previous step), from `location`
  when given: `Kestrel IV left aquilo at tick T (platform_schedule by sol, 0 ticks before this wait began)`. A
  departure by the game's own schedule (its waits met) is not recorded this way; a wait begun while the platform still
  waits there is met when it leaves, as before. `platform_arrived` reads the state (stopped there), so it is met at
  once when the platform arrived before the wait began: no such gap. Test tests/d19_batch48.lua.

  queue step failed after 305 ticks; a 2-stop [nauvis, fulgora] current 2 too): the game keeps a platform at its
  station until the rockets launched to it arrive, and it reads no_schedule meanwhile. On shift42 Kestrel IV left
  Nauvis 2129 and 2116 ticks after a rocket was launched to it (33991951 -> 33994080, 34340264 -> 34342380; the 2-stop
  call's own recheck read on_the_path 284 ticks after the call) and left Aquilo at once with none on the way. The
  harness's records and current were as asked (the reply's schedule read `nauvis | >fulgora`). Now a no_schedule read
  while rockets launched to it are on the way (freight.lua's incoming, with their arrival estimate) is read again until
  about 3 s after the last one's expected arrival, at most 3600 ticks from the call, and the lines say so: `1 rocket
  launched to it is still on the way (a rocket from nauvis launched 10s ago ...); the game keeps a platform at its
  station until the rockets launched to it arrive, reading no_schedule meanwhile ...`; the second read adds `(it waited
  for the rockets launched to it)`. Without a rocket on the way the recheck is 300 ticks as before. It applies to
  stops, stop + wait, next and current alone (one recheck). Test tests/d19_batch48.lua.

  "surface":"aquilo","speaker_alert":{"speaker_sound":{"volume":0.5,"note":"siren"}}}'`) because configure's own keys

  (140 s of it at the stop before it left): thruster-fuel used 1778/min, ...`. A leg first seen under way says `under
  way 0m40s since first seen (the departure was before the runtime counted)`. endurance.fuel_outlook adds
  since_departure_s, samples [{seconds, at_stop_s, fluids {name: {used_per_min, made_per_min, tanks_first,
  tanks_last}}}] and since_line; its line (platform_endurance, platform_digest) is unchanged. Tests:

- N2 (viewer Aurora, shift47 13:26 PDT: "Sampling every 60 ticks can miss a 20-tick pulse entirely, so longer averages
  still report 0%"). The pump duty in the platforms read's engine lines (`N pumps working X% of the time`, engine.lua)
  read each pump's status on the runtime's once-a-second tick, always at tick 0 of the second: a pump working ticks
  0-19 of every 60 read 100%, one working ticks 30-49 read 0%. The pumps are now read once a second at a phase that
  moves 7 ticks each second (7 and 60 share no factor), so 60 samples meet every tick of a second once; both pumps read
  33%. The line says what the figure is built from: `1 pumps working 33% of the time (60 samples, one a second at a
  phase 7 ticks later each second: every tick of a second sampled once a minute)`; under 60 samples `(N of the 60 ticks
  of a second sampled)`; before the first read `N pumps, not sampled yet`. The window's first sample is left out of the
  duty (N seconds, N samples). The game keeps no count of a pump's working ticks. The cost is the same reads as before
  (each platform's pumps once a second) plus one modulo a tick. Other working shares checked: efficiency.lua credits a
  drill's or lab's output from its status at each visit of its walk (a credit estimate marked "about", not a duty
  figure); the rest of the "working" counts in the reads are the status now. Tests: tests/engine.lua,
  tests/d20_batch54.lua.

  stream service reads `board_focus {}` with its board reads (live.py read_focus; a runtime without rows or the action

  job_age_s and job_label: the focus `focus, set 5 min ago: #1355 Steel line coal; step 2 ...; blocker: ...`; no focus,

  12 min ago; no focus set: ...`; neither `no focus, plan line or notes job`. Ages are game time for the focus and the
  plan line, the file's age for notes. The site's agent cards and portrait tip and the stream overlay's cards show the
  label before the job. Tests: tools/stream/test_jobcard.py, site/test_jobcard.py, tests/d20_batch54.lua.

  copy (2.0.77), on a test platform: LuaSpacePlatform.destroy() schedules the deletion 18000 ticks (5 min) ahead

  and cargo pods on their way (freight's incoming) or on it, and says whether the call would be refused; a platform that

- N9 (Sol, board #1427: a one-belt repair on Edge8 needed ghosts_waiting off while the platform_loss, ammo and fluid
  guards stayed; queue_edit edited only pending steps, so Sol replaced the whole plan, which ran platform_schedule
  current 2 again (failed: already current) and paused the queue from 39007306 to 39008146 with no guard, then needed

  guard keeps. ammo_below and fluid_count have no start count; they read the game at each check against count or

  guards set before this runtime get ids on the first read; every queue write's brief reply names them (guard_ids:
  `guard-1 ammo_below`, ...) and queue_status lists them in full. The reply: revision, guards [{id, until, set_tick,

  (revision 9): 2 kept, 0 replaced, 0 added, 1 removed (guard-3); the active step (job-2 wait_until) and the 1 pending
  step go on`. It refuses: no expected_revision or a stale one; guards with id, index, steps, remove or to; an unknown
  guard id (it lists the guards); a guard removed and replaced at once; past 8 guards. A full-plan replace is unchanged

  ghosts_waiting; ghosts_waiting removed at tick 2000; ghosts then appear and nothing fires, the wait and the pending

## d20 batch55 (eng/d20-batch55)
- P1 (viewer Aurora, shift47 13:59: "Could factory snapshots retain their capture time after refresh errors and
  reject older background results?"). Both were true in every cached read refreshed by a background job, and both are
  fixed there (snapfail.lua):
  - A failed refresh set the cached read's tick to the failure's, so it read as new: the factory survey (`status`
    factory and warnings), threat's chart, game_alerts' scan, the ground watch (status ground alerts), the census
    pass (its `as_of`, used by where_is, supply makers, gates, fuel_budget and silo reads) and networks' view and pole
    map. Each now keeps the tick it was captured at and notes the failure beside it (when, the error); the next try
    starts a period after the failure, as before. Replies say its age and that the last refresh failed, with the
    error: `status` `factory_age_s`, `factory_refresh_failed` and `chart.refresh_failed`; `game_alerts`
    `refresh_failed`; the ground alert line; census `age_s` and `refresh_failed` (also in where_is's index);
    `networks` `refresh_failed` (the view's, else the pole map's); the operator factory_digest's `refresh_failed`.
  - A finished background job replaced the cached read whatever was there, so a job started before a newer read
    (status `machines=true` or `threats=true`; a force's first game_alerts, ground watch, networks view or pole map,
    made at once in a reply) overwrote it with older data. A job's result is now dropped when the read held was
    captured after the job started.
  - Checked and not affected: ores.lua (each chunk read keeps its own read tick; a failed pass records `error`),
    beltgaps.lua (its multi-step refresh keeps tile sightings newer than its find), the spawner index (threat.lua;
    nothing else writes it), ghosttally.lua, defense, drill_sites, elsewhere and fuel_budget (made in the reply, no
    background job).
  Tests: tests/survey.lua, threat.lua, pushalerts.lua, census.lua, networks.lua (a failure mid-refresh; a job
  finishing after a newer read) and tests/d20_batch55.lua (snapfail.lua, the ground watch).
- P2 (viewer Aurora 14:37: "Could task and blueprint checks show observed pass, fail or stale, and rerun after
  relevant changes?"). What existed: board items' `evidence` (metric, decision, result as text, owner, next_check: a
  tick past which status lists the item overdue; no pass or fail); progress.lua's check of each owned item every 10
  game minutes in the background (progress seen, unchanged, stalled; not a pass or fail); board_focus `verify` (text:
  your next verification); a lesson's `check` (a wait_until condition read every minute until it holds: resolved
  with its tick, never read again after; a lesson not verified for 12 game hours reads stale); reminder checklists
  (each step's result as text with its tick) and `serves` (the machine still there); blueprint_place's report of one
  paste (not placed and why, settings that differ), with no record of where a paste put each entity.
  Added: `checks` (checks.lua). A check is a wait_until condition, or a library blueprint's last placement
  (blueprint_place {name} now records where the paste put each entity and its facing, the last 4 a name): each
  entity built there, facing as placed. It may name a board item (its full view lists its checks) and an area (a
  placement's box for a blueprint check). Its result is pass or fail with the tick, who ran it and what it saw; it
  reads stale when, after that run, our entities in its area differ from what stood there at the run (built,
  removed, turned: compared when the check is read, one bounded find each, up to 6 a listing; `checks {id}` compares
  one), its blueprint was pasted there again, or the run is older than its stale age (stale_after_s, default 30 game
  minutes). It runs when added and on `checks {run}`, never in the background. Cost on the private copy: a find over
  a 96x96 box of the base (3221 of ours) took 5.3 ms, so each find stops at 601 entities (0.86 ms; an area holding
  more is said not compared); a blueprint run reads at most 1201 (1.8 ms). Checked there: a 17-entity library paste
  read fail (17 ghosts), pass once built, stale after an inserter was rotated (named), fail when run again (facing
  otherwise). The index lists `checks`; agent/team.md has no line (the codex core is at its cap). Tests:
  tests/d20_batch55.lua (P2).
- P3 (viewer Aurora 14:38: "Could alerts include the owner's dated recovery check?"). What existed: loss incidents
  (runtime.lua record_loss: losses on a surface within 32 tiles of a box, one raid, an id, the last 64 kept) had no
  owner or acknowledgment; a reader is told each incident once and then its growth (losses_told), and a shift start
  closes them. Added: `losses {incident, recovery: {checked, result?, check?}}` sets the incident's recovery check (who,
  now, what was checked, the result, and a `checks` check whose state its line shows); `false` clears it, a new one
  replaces it (said). The incident's lines (team.alerts, status alerts.latest) end with `handled by sol, checked 12m00s
  ago: walls at the east gate: 2 walls rebuilt`; its row (alerts.incidents) has `recovery {by, tick, checked, result,
  check, reopened, reopened_tick, lost_since}`. A loss after the check that joins the incident, or lands within 2
  tiles of its box (a new incident after 5 quiet minutes), reopens it: `reopened: 1 lost there since sol's recovery
  check 6m14s ago (1 stone-wall; the first 1s ago; that check: ...)`. Counted as each loss is recorded (the incidents
  are looped there already); nothing is read from the map. An argument on `losses`, so no new index line. Tests:
  tests/board.lua (recovery checks).
- P4 (Sol #1393: Fulgora's EM plant (-41,81) read 106 crafts in 161 s, 39.4/min, "153%" of 25.8/min, while working
  all the time; inspect: 25.8 crafts/min at productivity 54%). products_finished counts every completion, the
  productivity bar's extra ones too, and uptime called them all crafts. It now gives `crafts` (base crafts, from the
  completions and the bar: base x (1 + productivity) = completions + bonus_progress at the end - at the start) against
  `full_speed_per_min`, and `completions` (the game's count), `bonus_completions`, `completions_per_min` against
  `full_speed_completions_per_min` (the craft rate with productivity), `productivity` and `working_share` (% of
  samples working) apart. Sol's case reads `69 crafts in 161s (25.7/min, 100% of its 25.8/min at full speed) and 37
  productivity completions (productivity +54%): 106 completions, 39.5/min against 39.7/min at full speed; working

- P8 (Sol #1439: uptime refused a biolab as not a crafting machine). uptime takes labs and biolabs with crafting
  machines (up to 16 in all). A lab's row (`kind: lab`) gives its status samples at the moving phase (working, missing
  science packs, no power, as the lab GUI shows), `working_share`, and per pack it held: `held_least`/`held_most` at
  the samples, `empty_samples`, and `used`. 2.0.77 keeps no count per lab. A pack in a lab loses durability as it
  researches and is gone at 0 (on the private copy a biolab drained 0.099 of each pack in 123 ticks, the force's
  research progress times its 50% drain), and a spoiled pack's result goes to the lab's trash slot (lab_trash). So
  `used` is the durability drained between samples: a pack put in or taken out whole moves the held durability by whole
  packs, and the drain is the change modulo a pack while the lab cannot drain a whole pack between samples (its
  researching speed times 1 + speed_bonus, which holds the force's lab speed, over the research's unit time, times the
  lab's drain rate). Otherwise that interval is unknown (`unknown_intervals`, `unknown_why`: it could use a whole pack
  between samples), as is an interval where a spoilable pack spoiled, or with packs above normal quality; the line
  says "at least". `spoil_results` counts what appeared in the lab's trash. With a lab in the watch the reply adds
  `research` (the force's progress gained on its current technology in units, levels and finishes followed, every lab
  of the force) and `packs_used_up` (the surface's production statistics: whole packs used up, every lab there). On
  the private copy a biolab with every pack, refilled during the watch, read `working 100%; packs used in 40s
  (durability drained): automation-science-pack 1.93, ...; held at the samples: automation-science-pack 1-3, ...`,
  with research 3.87 units (x 50% = 1.93) and 1 of each pack used up on nauvis; a lab missing the electromagnetic pack
  read `missing science packs 100%`, used 0, and agricultural packs spoiled in it read `used unknown for
  agricultural-science-pack in 1 of 22 intervals (packs spoiled); spoil results in its trash: spoilage 3`.
  Tests: tests/d20_batch55.lua (P8).

- Z1 (Sol #1515: the crusher on Petrel (-17,-10.5) read no_recipe at tick 40313975 with Set recipe on while its green
  wire (network 1307, a decider's output) carried recipe:oxide-asteroid-crushing = 1; configure was refused as
  "recipe incompatible with machine"). What 2.0.77's Set recipe takes, seen on a private copy with a crusher and a
  constant combinator, each case from no recipe: a recipe signal above 0 sets that recipe at the signal's quality, on
  red or green alike (the two summed); among several recipe signals the lowest recipe order wins whatever the counts
  (metallic b-a-a, carbonic b-a-b, oxide b-a-c, advanced oxide f), normal before rare; a recipe the machine cannot
  make or the force has not researched is skipped; recipe signals come before item signals, and an item signal alone
  picks a recipe of the machine that has it as a product (ice and the oxide chunk: oxide-asteroid-crushing; calcite:
  advanced-oxide; iron ore: metallic), at its quality; virtual signals are ignored. A constant combinator slot with no
  quality sends nothing; circuit_set's signals are written with quality normal, which the game takes. When the wires
  change the recipe, the running craft finishes, then the old recipe's ingredients and products go to the machine's
  dump slots (defines.inventory.assembling_machine_dump) and it has no recipe until they are empty; an inserter taking
  from it empties them (one with filters only its filter items), and the new recipe goes in. A recipe set by hand
  (set_recipe) is ignored while Set recipe is on, which configure read as "recipe incompatible with machine"; with it
  off, set_recipe works while the dump still holds items and returns none of them. Sol's case: Petrel's two deciders
  switch the crusher between advanced-oxide (calcite < 20, or ice >= 100 and calcite < 100, read from a belt) and oxide
  (ice < 100 and calcite >= 20); a switch put the old recipe's items in the dump, and the takers (a bulk inserter
  filtered to ice and calcite, a fast inserter filtered to the oxide chunk, both onto belts) had not emptied it (what it
  held then is not recorded: inspect did not list the dump; configure's change with Set recipe off left it, and it is
  empty now). Now: inspect's `circuit_recipe` (an assembling machine with Set recipe on) gives what the wires give
  (`wires_give`, `from`), `recipe_now`, the dump's contents, the inserters taking from it with their filters and what
  each takes (`takers`, `dump_left`), the signals not used and why, the rule, and a line, e.g. `Set recipe is on: its
  wires give oxide-asteroid-crushing (recipe:oxide-asteroid-crushing); it has no recipe: the new one waits until its
  dump slots are empty: they hold carbon*20, carbonic-asteroid-chunk*2 (...); inserters taking from it: ...`; the dump
  is listed in inventories (assembling_machine_dump) and transfer takes from it (take-only). configure with Set recipe
  on is refused before any change, naming what the wires give and the two ways in the game's terms (Set recipe off,
  then configure; or the recipe signal on a wire). Tests: tests/d21_batch64.lua.
