## d20 batch62 (eng/d20-batch62)

- X1 (viewer Aurora, operator inbox 23:40: "Sol's 600-second trial advanced after 464 seconds when he equipped a
  weapon"). Sol's journal, shift49: at 04:31:30Z (line 1314) a body-lane `queue_submit` mode replace with
  `wait_ticks 34458` then `circuit_set` on fulgora (23.5,184.5) (quality-module uncommon > 999999); the queue had
  `resume_after_direct` on. At 04:39:13Z (line 2056) `equip {item: submachine-gun, slot: gun, index: 1}`, 463 s of
  wall clock and 25985 ticks (433 game seconds) into the wait. equip is a direct call that drives the character, so it
  paused the body queue; the pause requeued only absolute-goal steps, and `wait_ticks`, as a relative step, was
  recorded `interrupted` and dropped; `resume_after_direct` ran the queue again as the equip ended, and the
  `circuit_set` ran at that tick (39783165), 8473 ticks before the wait's end tick 39791638 (queue_status at 04:40:23Z,
  line 2081). The 600 s run at 04:42:28Z (line 2168, `wait_ticks 35950`) ran in full: no direct call that drives the
  character came during it, and the queue was done by tick 39830060 (end tick 39830043). `queue_pause` dropped a
  running wait the same way, and the next step ran at `queue_resume`.
- Now a queued `wait_ticks` that a pause interrupts (a direct call that drives the character, `queue_pause`, a harness
  update, a standing order's preemption) is requeued at the head with its end tick: it ends at that tick, or at once
  when the queue resumes after it, and the steps after it never run sooner. The interrupted history entry says
  `resumed_from: keeps its end tick T (N ticks left)`; while the queue is paused, queue_status and the queue replies
  give `kept_wait` (`job-5 wait_ticks was interrupted and keeps its end tick T (N s left); the steps after it run from
  then, once queue_resume runs the queue`, or `... its end tick T passed N s ago while your queue is paused:
  queue_resume runs the steps after it`); the finished entry's `kept` says whether it ended at its tick or as the queue
  resumed after it. A resumed standing order keeps the end tick too. `mode: "ahead"` with an active wait_ticks now
  runs the new steps first and then the wait to its end tick (it refused before). `queue_cancel` still ends a running
  wait (the agent's own cancel); its reply's `cancelled_wait` says how long before its end tick, and with `clear: false`
  that the steps after it are held in the paused queue until `queue_resume`.
- Which calls pause a body-lane queue: every direct call except reads, talk (say, tell, chat), calls by remote view or
  on another surface, queue calls and the passive list in runtime.lua (requests, circuit_set, wire, craft,
  place_ghosts, blueprints, platform_schedule, launch, order and reminder calls, ...). equip, unequip, transfer,
  move_to, build, mine, use_item, shoot and the like pause it. Equipping a gun stops no timer a player keeps; the
  pause still stops the running step of the queue (a walk, a transfer), and the wait now keeps its end tick through it.
- Checked on the private copy (2.0.77): Sol `queue_submit` body, resume_after_direct, wait_ticks 600 then wait_ticks 1;
  `equip pistol` (already in gun slot 2: selected) 251 ticks in: the wait was requeued with end tick 26654117 and
  ended there, and the next step started at 26654117. Without resume_after_direct, the same equip left the queue
  paused; the end tick passed while paused, `kept_wait` said so, and `queue_resume` at 26655644 ended the wait that tick
  and ran the next step at 26655645. Tests: tests/d20_batch62.lua; tests/scheduler.lua (ahead) and tests/orders.lua
  (a resumed order's kept wait) updated.

  `area` {left_top, right_bottom} (up to 200 tiles a side) with an optional `recipe` (and `quality`): the crafting
  machines of ours in it, each still in sight. With 2 or more machines the reply gives `groups` per recipe and quality
  (machines, completions and completions_per_min against full_speed_completions_per_min, crafts against
  full_speed_per_min when every machine's are known, status_shares of all their samples, line) first in `lines`, with
  the per-machine lines after. Still one finite watch per agent. A reply's numbers are what its encoding pays for: on the
  private copy helpers.table_to_json took 23 ms for 64 rows of 15 fields, 0.07 ms for 64 lines of text, and 6.2 ms for
  16 rows. So above 16 machines the rows are left out (`machine_rows` says so; `lines` has each machine), group rows
  above 8 groups and flow rows above 10. Cost on a private copy (its own container, 64 assembling machines, half
  short of plates, one with quality modules; Factorio x86 under Rosetta): a sample of 64 machines 1.0-1.5 ms (seconds
  with two samples up to 2.9 ms); the seconds in which a garbage collection of the harness heap finished (it fell 100-190
  MB) read 4.3-8.1 ms, and one 84.6 ms (a 55 MB fall; the collector runs in whatever code allocates then). The start
  of a 64-machine area watch: 5.7 ms of its own (area 0.25, machines 4.3 with machines alike sharing one craftrate read,
  items 0.1, first sample 1.0; the reply's team block comes on top); a read so far 7.4 ms with 1.2 ms encoding. The
  profiler (profile_ticks) names the parts: uptime.tick, uptime.area, uptime.machines, uptime.flows, uptime.sample.
- T3 (Sol #1460: produced and consumed by quality over a window). 2.0.77's production statistics keep counts by quality:
  `get_input_count`/`get_output_count`/`get_flow_count` take `{name, quality}`, and the name alone counts normal (on the
  private copy an uncommon gear recipe's 9 crafts read 9 uncommon gears produced and 20 uncommon plates consumed, the
  name alone 0 of either), as the production statistics window shows a player by quality. uptime's `items` (1..8, a
  name read at every quality, or {name, quality}) reads them on the watch's surface: `items_recent` at the start (the
  last 10 minutes) and `flows` over the watch (produced, consumed, net, per minute, for every machine and hand on the
  surface; qualities with nothing are left out unless named); `uptime {items}` alone is a statistics-only watch. Stock
  change is never counted. Each machine also gives its outputs by quality as its output slot shows them
  (`outputs_by_quality`): between two samples the slot's gain must equal its completions times the product's amount,
  every quality gaining or level, for the gain to count; otherwise products were taken out (or spoiled) between samples
  and the interval is unknown (`outputs_unknown_intervals` of `outputs_intervals`); a product by chance or in a range
  has no fixed amount and gives none. On the private copy a gear bank read `outputs by quality in its output slot:
  iron-gear-wheel normal 39` for 39 crafts; with a fast inserter taking every gear, 35 of 35 intervals read unknown;
  the statistics read 10 uncommon gears from a machine with legendary quality modules. A fact seen there: an assembler
  has one output slot, so an uncommon gear in it stops the next normal one (status full output) until it is taken.

  solar-panel@rare 2. Taking the 6 normal panels out changed no slot. The rare slot fell as the hub spent rare panels.
  A built epic panel cleared its slot at the 10 s rewrite, and the rare slot stayed where it was. min_payload by
  `item@quality` and by `item` set the slots.

AB5 (viewer Aurora, operator inbox 13:02 PDT: "Could delivery watches follow cargo to a named consumer, with a

silo.").
- What the reads tracked before:
  - shipment: a hub request's state on its way up (delivered, in flight, launched, loading, waiting with the silo's
    flag), and what a planet's pads ask of the hub.
  - freight: each rocket launched to a platform, and each cargo pod from a hub to the pad that received it or to the
    ground.
  - pods and landed: pods in the sky, containers on the ground.
  - drops: one drop's pod to its container.
  - freight_audit: one item's stock across planets and platforms.
  None followed a count of an item to the chest, silo or machine that uses it.
- New: `delivery_watch {item, count, to: {position, surface | platform}, deadline_min, from?}` (delivwatch.lua; runtime
  deploy needed).
  - The consumer is an entity of ours within 2 tiles of the position, in a chunk our force has charted.
  - Once a second, 4 watches a pass, each watch reads what a player sees and keeps the first tick of each stage.
  - Down (the consumer on a planet):
    - loaded: a platform's hub holds the item (`from`, else the first platform with it whose schedule stops there);
    - departed, in_transit (flying to that planet), arrived;
    - landed: its pod received by a landing pad (freight's pod receipts now carry the pad's position), or landed with
      no pad;
    - network: the pad's logistic network and the consumer's;
    - reached: the consumer holds `count` more than at the start.
  - Up (the consumer aboard a platform):
    - loaded: a silo of `from` with it in its rocket (the census pass's silos);
    - launched and in_transit: a rocket with it launched to the platform;
    - landed: the hub holds more of it;
    - reached.
  - Blockers: the pad's network is not the consumer's, or the consumer is in none; the platform is stopped there with
    it but no landing pad there has room for it, or there is none; a pod with it landed with no pad; the platform is
    paused, or its schedule has no stop there; up: not stopped at `from`; a requester or buffer chest asks none of it;
    the consumer is gone.
  - The setter hears each in team.alerts: each blocker once, a blocker gone, the deadline passed while not reached
    (with the last confirmed stage and the blocker), and the arrival. `{}` lists the force's watches; `{id}` reads
    one; `{id, clear: true}` ends one. At most 16 open a force; a watch is kept 10 minutes after it ends.

  - With 50 tungsten carbide in its hub, the pad (52,54) got a request for it (section added, then removed). Two
    watches: one to a wooden chest at (-43.5,134.5) in no logistic network, one to the silo (15.5,59.5) in network
    #243.
  - Both read "loaded", "arrived" and "blocked: no landing pad of ours on nauvis has room for tungsten-carbide

    consumer wooden-chest (-43.5,134.5) is in no logistic network". The silo: in #243, no blocker.

## d21 batch73 AI: census.step within the tick budget

World n, d21 19:52-19:55 (operator): 35-55 UPS; in a 60 s profile `census.step` took 7.18 ms a tick, worst second
1180 ms, and the Lua heap grew 24 MB a second. On the private copy loaded with world n's 19:01 save (x86 under
Rosetta), before: 9.85 ms a tick, worst second 1734 ms; the pass took 2127 steps, so it stepped every tick and each
pass began as the last ended.
- Where it went: the census's sightings (readmemory.observe for every entity read: the summary ring's key and
  copies, the fog memory's chunk key, row key and row text, belt memory's chunk and tile keys) were 90% of a step,
  15.5 ms per 100 entities. In the game's Lua a number turned into text by `..` or tostring costs about 8 µs on the
  copy (string.format('%d') 0.3 µs, a numeric table key 0.2 µs).
- Now (census.lua, readmemory.observe_seen, fogmem.note_seen, beltgaps.observe_seen, numtext.lua):
  - number text by numtext (string.format for integers and halves; the same text as before, checked over 52,000
    positions in the game; -0 and other fractions as before);
  - each chunk's sight, fog-memory chunk and belt-memory chunk looked up once a step; the row texts made once;
  - the census no longer writes the summary ring (2048 entries against about 200,000 entities a pass, so it held the
    last few steps); agents' own reads, builds and inspects still do, and an out-of-sight inspect with no sighting
    reads the fog memory;
  - a one-tile belt seen as it was (name, place, direction) keeps its row, brought up to date (tick, items,
    carried_tick, by, an underground's pairing);
  - no closures in the per-entity reads; one position read an entity; Nauvis's box kept during the walk;
  - paced by work: 8 units a tick (an entity read 1, an entity a band's find returns 0.2, a band 1, a grid point
    0.05, a dense-core point 0.2, an ore resource 0.2, a nest or ore band 5), up to 32 kept; the bands one chunk
    each (a band grown to 32 sparse chunks found about 30,000 entities in one tick: 460 ms of census.step in that
    second).
- After, on the copy (300 s profile, one pass): census.step 0.167 ms a tick (from 9.85), median second 8.3 ms;
  seconds over 15 ms: 34 of 301, those over 22 ms all in a second where a garbage collection finished (or the next),
  up to 65 ms, when every part of the tick grows (scheduler.tick 36-43 ms, networks.tick 33 ms). Holding the census
  idle left the heap's growth at 7.2 MB a second (7.3 with it): the census's garbage is now small. The whole harness
  tick: 12.1 ms a tick before, 2.4 after. A pass: 35,104 ticks (9.8 min, 33,358 steps); its building counts equal a
  direct count on every planet (Nauvis 45,404, Vulcanus 8,437, Fulgora 5,855, Gleba 4,807, Aquilo 868). WORK is
  the knob: the pass's length goes as 1/WORK and its cost per second as WORK.

  reactors and fusion generators were not in its type filter, so Asterion's wait on fluoroketone-cold read the pipes
  and left out the 2000 in its two reactors.

  boilers and generators (heat exchangers, steam engines and turbines: `boilers and generators`) and mining drills

  thruster-oxidizer in the thrusters, pipes, pumps and tanks, which hold them. `harness: true` waits (platwait.lua) read
  the storage tanks, as documented. Neither is changed.
- Seen on a copy of world n's `_autosave8` (tick 46406483): on main, `fluoroketone-cold` on Asterion read 1612 (pipes
  1200, machines 412), with 1000 in each of its two reactors left out; `fusion-plasma` read none. Kestrel IVa, Kestrel
  IVb and Crucible each had a reactor's 1000 left out too. With this change: Asterion 3618 (pipes 1200, machines 418,
  fusion reactors and generators 2000) and fusion-plasma 60 (6).
- Cost: the scan finds 725 entities on Asterion against 719 before; 10 scans each, alternating, took 2.2-4.8 ms
  with either filter on the copy.
### Items on the ground: the stack in inspect and scan (d22 batch78 AN1, Astra #1809)

Astra: "Gleba has thousands of dropped items. inspect item-on-ground gives no stack name/count and scan
inventory/spoil also omits it." Reproduced on a private copy of world n's shift57 save (05:16 PDT): inspect of an
item-on-ground on Vulcanus gave `inventories: {}` and no stack; `scan {type: "item-entity", fields: [inventory,
spoil]}` gave rows with name and position only; `inspect {area, types: ["item-entity"]}` said "no item-entity of
ours" (ground items belong to no force). That save held no ground items on Gleba (Vulcanus 895, Nauvis 175). Now, as
hovering a stack shows (groundstack.lua):
- inspect of one: `stack {name, quality, count, fresh}` (fresh: percent fresh, only for an item that spoils) and
  `holds` (`yumako*3, 61% fresh`);
- inspect over an area with `types: ["item-entity"]` or `name: "item-on-ground"`: the ground stacks are listed (each
  row with `stack` and `holds`, compact lines `item-on-ground (x,y): yumako*3, 61% fresh`) and `ground_items`, all of
  them by item;
- scan: each item-entity row has `stack`; fields `inventory` (`yumako*3`) and `spoil` (`yumako*3 61%`) read it;
  `ground_items` is given with a name or type filter too, summed over every stack found before `limit`;
- `ground_items` items (scan, observe, inspect) carry `fresh`: the stalest stack's freshness, for an item that spoils.
Area inspect also checks sight once per chunk (it checked each entity) and reads each position once for its sort.
Measured on the copy with 2,880 stacks spilled on Gleba (32-tile radius; x86 under Rosetta, the JSON encoding slow
there), before -> after: scan unfiltered 67-73 -> 70-77 ms; scan `type: item-entity` with fields inventory and spoil
(256 rows) 295-301 -> 124-140 ms (the inventory field tried every inventory kind on each stack); the same with limit
1024 and no fields 177-190 -> 235-330 ms (each row now carries its stack: 69 -> 147 KB); inspect of the 30x32 area
(refused before) 59-63 ms; inspect of one stack 3.5-4.3 -> 3.4-4.0 ms. Tests: tests/d22_batch78.lua.

### Floating asteroid chunks and collector reach (d22 batch78 AN2, Astra #1774)

Astra: "Asterion reports about 90 asteroid_chunks but 24 collectors have collected zero past 10 min. scan cannot name
chunk prototypes; platform_supply gives connections but no geometry of uncollected chunks." Reproduced on a private
copy of world n's shift57 save (05:16 PDT): Asterion over Nauvis, 89 chunks (33 carbonic, 38 metallic, 18 oxide), 12
collectors in two columns at x = -53.5 (facing west) and 53.5 (facing east), y 119.5 to 134.5; `platforms` gave only
the count by type. `platform_supply {platform, collection: true}` (collectreach.lua) now gives, read only:
- the view: the chunks of the platform's surface holding foundation, 32 tiles out on every side (Asterion:
  (-96,-96)-(96,288)); chunks in it by type, in 16-tile groups (count, box, drift in tiles a second), and the 12
  nearest a collector's reach (`outside`: tiles beyond it, 0 inside);
- each collector: `reach` {from, to, radius}: every point within `collection_radius` of the line from its centre to
  the point `collection_box_offset` tiles in front. 2.0.77 gives the offset on LuaEntityPrototype (5) but not the
  radius (7.5 in space-age/prototypes/entity/entities.lua, kept in collectreach.lua's RADIUS). The shape is fitted to
  what the copy's collectors took (below), not read from the game; status, filters, what its output
  holds (the arm's load has no inventory to read: get_inventory gives only the output), the chunks in its reach now
  and the nearest outside it;
- `collected`: each chunk type's count in the platform's production statistics (the production GUI) over the last
  minute and 10 minutes, and its total;
- with `seconds` (10..3600): a collector_tally watch (one an agent, a bounded watch in measures.lua: idle checks and
  the agent cards show it): every 10 ticks, a chunk in a reach at one read that is gone from where its drift puts it
  at the next counts as taken by that collector (the one deepest in whose reach it lay). This is an estimate beside the
  exact platform count: on the copy, rises in each collector's output saw 1 of 4 collected chunks (the inserters
  empty it within 10 ticks); vanishing from a circle around the front point saw 6 of 12; from the line-shaped reach,
  3 of 4 over 120 s, all 3 metallic where the platform collected 2 metallic, 1 carbonic and 1 oxide. Chunks also
  vanish where they hit the hull and where they leave the view, outside every reach. The watch's tick: 0.007 ms a tick
  on average (profile_ticks over 1,801 ticks with it running: 12.9 ms in all, worst game second 0.84 ms; the harness
  tick 3.09 ms); with no watch, one state check a tick.
On the copy, Asterion's chunks drift at about 1 tile a second; at the reads none was in a reach and the nearest was
0.2 tiles outside one; the platform collected 13-22 of each type in 10 minutes. Logging every chunk that vanished
near Asterion over 7,025 ticks (8 collected): 9 vanished in empty space within 7.6 tiles of a collector's front line,
several 7.3-7.6 tiles beside a collector's centre, outside a circle around the front point; hence the line shape. Reach check on the east-facing collector at (53.5,119.5), chunks placed at rest (offsets: x in
front, y to the side): with its neighbours on, it took 12 and 12.4 in front (beyond any neighbour's reach) and left
12.7, 13.2 and 14; with the other collectors switched off, it took (2,0), (1.6,3), (3,6.8) and (9,6) and left
(1.2,0), (0,3), (-1,0), (11,4), (2.5,-6) and (5,-7.4), all within the line-shaped reach; after those captures it took
nothing more (a chunk placed at (4,1) stayed 765 ticks, power full, output empty), which this read does not explain. Cost on
the copy (x86 under Rosetta, about 12 UPS), timed in the same minute: the read 24-26 ms on Asterion (55 ms the first
call) and 19-21 ms on Anvil (157 chunks), the existing platform_supply read on Asterion 18-23 ms; the extent, chunk
and collector lookups take 3.6 ms of it. Tests: tests/d22_batch78.lua.

## d22 batch81 AQ1: the collector tally is inferred, by filter, beside the exact count (Sol #1852)

- Sol's case: Spindle's collector at (5.5,-22.5) takes oxide only, and the collector_tally credited it 92 metallic, 54
  carbonic and 33 oxide (242 in all) while production statistics said the platform collected 132.
- Seen on a copy of world n's `_autosave5` (tick 46892405, Spindle over Fulgora, three collectors: (-13.5,-0.5) west,
  metallic only; (5.5,-22.5) north, oxide only; (17.5,-0.5) east, every type):
  - main's tally over 103.5 s credited the oxide collector 4 metallic, 4 oxide and 7 carbonic, and the metallic
    collector 1 oxide, against 21 collected;
  - every chunk round Spindle read every tick for 14,034 ticks: 103 vanished. 70 vanished where their drift put them
    on a platform tile (they struck the hull: the oxide collector stands on the hull's north edge and its reach covers
    the hull behind it), 20 left the 128-tile area read, and 13 as the platform's count rose (16 collected);
  - each collected chunk vanished 1-4 ticks before the count rose, at 0.18 inside to 0.92 outside the fitted reach
    (one at 2.77): a collector takes a chunk as it crosses into its reach, so a chunk read inside a reach at one
    10-tick read is rarely there at the next.
- 2.0.77 has no per-collector catch count: no event for a collected chunk (defines.events has only map chunk events),
  the collector's arm inventory (`defines.inventory.asteroid_collector_arm`) reads nil, the output inventory is
  emptied by its inserter within ticks, and production statistics are the platform's.
- The tally now (collectreach.lua):
  - watches chunks within 2 tiles (plus a read's drift) of the reach of a collector whose filters take their type;
  - a watched chunk gone from where its drift puts it at the next read counts as `gone_in_reach` for the collector
    whose reach its drift's path came nearest, within 1 tile; a chunk is never credited to a collector whose filters
    exclude it;
  - not counted: one found where its drift puts it (it drifted on), one gone where its drift puts it on a platform
    tile (`hit_hull`), one whose path came near no such reach (`gone_elsewhere`);
  - the fields and lines say inferred (`gone_in_reach`, `gone_in_reach_total`; `taken` and `taken_seen` are gone);
    beside them `collected` (production statistics, exact, the platform's), `inferred_minus_collected` and `by_type`
    [{name, inferred, collected, difference}];
  - the read gives each collector's `in_reach_it_takes` beside `in_reach`, and its line names its filters.
- On the logged ticks, replayed at the watch's 10-tick reads: the old rules gave 15 (8 of them against the
  collector's filter), the new 11 of the 16 collected, each credited to a collector that takes its type (the oxide
  collector its 2 oxide). A chunk taken without being seen near a reach first is missed, so the inferred sum can fall
  short of the exact count; the line says by how much.
- Filters are read at each read of the watch (`filters_changed` counts changes): on the copy the east collector's
  filters changed 17 times in a 300 s watch (metallic, carbonic and oxide at first; metallic and oxide; carbonic and
  oxide; oxide), so filters taken once at the start credited metallic it no longer took and missed carbonic.
- Live on the copy, 300 s with filters read at each read: 71 collected (34 oxide, 28 metallic, 9 carbonic), 53
  inferred (24 metallic to the metallic collector, 15 oxide to the oxide collector, 7 carbonic and 7 oxide to the east
  one), 18 fewer than collected; 5 struck the hull, 28 gone away from every reach.
- Cost (profile_ticks 60 s, a watch running on Spindle; the copy's chunk count changed from run to run):

  | run | chunks in view | collector_tally.tick over 3,600 ticks | a tick | worst second |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | main, baseline | 11-30 | 160.8 ms | 0.045 ms | 29.1 ms |
  | main, round 1 | 56 | 296.8 ms | 0.082 ms | 227.1 ms |
  | main, round 2 | 135 | 169.2 ms | 0.047 ms | 28.0 ms |
  | branch, round 1 | 77 | 77.5 ms | 0.022 ms | 8.9 ms |
  | branch, round 2 | 102 | 70.2 ms | 0.019 ms | 15.4 ms |
  | branch, round 3 | 55 | 36.9 ms | 0.010 ms | 2.4 ms |
  | branch, filters at each read | 109 | 185.6 ms | 0.052 ms | 24.0 ms |

  The sample builds no position tables and keeps only the chunks near a reach of a collector that takes them for the

## d20 batch79 AO1 (eng/d20-batch79): uptime, when the non-working samples fell (Astra #1845)

- Astra's 600 s watch of six Vulcanus machines from tick 46697072 read "low power 0%" for 3 of 601 samples, with no

## d22 batch82 AR1 (eng/d20-batch82): platform_defense {platform, asteroids: true, seconds} (Astra #1855)

- Astra (Nick's note): Asterion's side weapons shoot asteroids that pass harmlessly; the defense read gives geometric
  reach only. Main before: nothing read asteroids' paths; turret_tally gives each turret's kills and damage dealt, not
  on what.
- What 2.0.77 gives (private copy of world n's _autosave6, tick 46946172; Asterion flying Nauvis to Gleba, 110
  asteroids on its surface, 91 ammo turrets): an asteroid is an entity (type asteroid, force enemy) with a position and
  no movement or speed to read; between reads it moves in a straight line against the platform (0.031-0.039 tiles a
  tick south, about 2 tiles a second, then 0.4 tiles a second later in the flight). A turret's shot on one is an
  on_entity_damaged event with the turret as cause, its kill an on_entity_died with the turret as cause; an asteroid's
  hit on us an on_entity_damaged on our entity with the asteroid as cause (69.4 damage from a medium one). Reading all
  19,321 foundation tiles took 948 ms on the copy, so the hull is found from its chunks and a binary search of strips.
- The watch (asteroidwatch.lua; measures kind asteroid_watch, one an agent): every 15 ticks the asteroids in the view
  (the foundation's chunks, 32 tiles out), each one's velocity from its last two positions; its approach by where its
  straight line from where it was first seen enters the hull's box (widened by its radius); a straight-line projection
  over foundation tiles (8-tile cells with no foundation counted once and crossed without reading their tiles, at most
  600 lookups a read); outcomes and turret hits, kills and damage from the events, classed when the result is read;
  each turret's ammo slot read once a second. platform_defense's other arguments are unchanged; seconds and reason go
  with asteroids only. It is a mode of platform_defense so the Codex core (21995 of 22000 bytes) needs no new index
  entry.

  1 front missing, 10 clear), none hit; the front gun groups put 6 hits each on clear asteroids. With Asterion's 91

  and hitting within 1-2 tiles of the projected tile (e.g. "medium-carbonic-asteroid hit arithmetic-combinator

  the view; the 2 side ones projected to miss were still in view at the end.
- Cost (profile_ticks 60 s on the copy, about 60 UPS under Rosetta, the watch running on Asterion with its turrets on):
  asteroid_watch.tick 278.5 ms over 3600 ticks (0.077 ms a tick), worst game second 9.6 ms; of it the asteroid find
  210 ms (240 reads of the view), projections 4.1 ms, ammo 29.7 ms (a quarter of the turrets each read). Before the
  ammo reads were spread, one read of all 91 turrets in a second fell in a garbage collection: 18.9 ms. Events with
  the watch on: on_entity_damaged 66 us and on_entity_died 98 us a call, against 47 and 81 us without it. Seconds

### d22 batch88: the endurance forecast's damage is ammo_use's

- AX1 (Astra #1876: Asterion's forecast read 3 rockets a 400 hp medium asteroid and 89 magazines, where

  kills). 2.0.77 keeps an ammunition's category on its item prototype (`ammo_category`); `get_ammo_type().category`
  reads nil (read on a private copy of world n's 10:18 autosave), so the forecast found no damage bonus and no turret
  (routeammo.lua). It now takes the shot from `ammorate.row` with platdefense's damage reader, which is what ammo_use
  uses: the ammunition's damage, times its quality's multiplier (the quality the turrets hold), times (1 + the damage
  bonus), times (1 + the turret's attack bonus). Against each asteroid of the route, and its fragments, it applies the
  game's resistance rule. The forecast adds a block of lines, one per ammunition and one per asteroid; asteroids alike
  in health and resistances share a line:
  `rocket (rocket-turret, normal): 1160 explosion a shot = 200 explosion x (1 +480% rocket damage) x (1 +0%
  rocket-turret attack)`, then `medium-carbonic/metallic/oxide-asteroid 400 hp: explosion (1160 - 0 flat) x (1 - 30%)
  = 812 a hit: 1 shot`. The reply adds `forecast_damage [{ammo, ammo_quality, turret, damage, damage_per_shot, asteroid,
  hp, per_hit, shots}]`. The uncalibrated-route warning is unchanged.

## d22 batch92 BB1-BB3 (eng/d20-batch92): platform_hit (platform_damage), platform_energy_below, platform_progress (Sol #1884, Astra #1886, #1887)

- Why: platform_loss fires only once something of ours is destroyed. Medium asteroid impacts can follow one another
  before the next flight_watch read. `damaged` reads no platform, and a repaired hit leaves no damaged entity to find.
  No condition read a platform's accumulators.
- `wait_until {until: "platform_hit", platform, at_least?, damage?, entity_names?, since_tick?}` (`platform_damage` is
  another name for it). It counts hits on our entities on that platform by anything not of our force (asteroids,
  enemies), as the platform's hit alerts count them (platalerts.lua's on_entity_damaged), since the wait or guard began.
  That is `since_tick`, by default its first check. The baseline is kept on the wait's record, or on the guard's
  condition in the queue, so a save or a runtime deploy keeps it. A guard added or replaced by queue_edit starts its
  own baseline; one kept keeps it.
  - It is met at `at_least` hits or at `damage` (the hits' damage summed, a hit repaired since still counted), whichever
    is given and reached first. With neither, it is met on the first hit. `entity_names` (1..16) counts only hits on
    those.
  - Its saw: `platform Edge5: 1 hit, 123.3 damage, on ours since tick 1200, first: thruster (-4.5,10.5) 123.3 damage
    by medium-carbonic-asteroid 1s ago`. A hit with no cause reads `(impact, no cause)`, naming the damage type. Up to 4
    first hits are named, then `+N more`.
  - When a guard on it fires, the queue history entry (and the stopped step's record) keeps the first hits as
    `evidence` [{t, n, x, y, d, c|k}] beside the saw line.
- How hits are kept: platalerts.lua already counts each hit on a platform (per minute and in running totals). It now
  also writes one row a hit into a ring of that platform's last 64 hits: hit number, tick, entity, position, damage,
  the platform's damage total after it, cause or damage type. That one row is the added per-event cost.
  - A check reads only the rows since the one before. The hit count and the damage come from the running totals, so
    they are exact even when more than 64 hits come between two checks (every 10 ticks).
  - With `entity_names`, hits the ring no longer holds cannot be named, and the saw says how many.
  - A `since_tick` before the ring's oldest row counts from that row, and the saw says so.
- `wait_until {until: "platform_energy_below", platform, fraction}`: the platform's accumulators together hold under
  `fraction` (over 0, up to 1) of what they can hold (each one's energy over its electric buffer size, as its GUI shows
  them). Saw: `platform Edge5: 2 accumulators hold 2.5 of 10.0 MJ (25%; met under 30%)`. With no accumulator it is not
  met, and says so. It is found and read at each check.
- `wait_until {until: "platform_progress", platform, at_least, from?, to?}` (Astra #1887: a probe flight turned back at
  20% of its outer leg, whatever its speed). It reads the share of its leg the platform has flown, in the direction it
  flies, as the platforms read gives it (freight.lua `leg`; `at: "fulgora->nauvis 48%"`). It is met at `at_least`
  (over 0, up to 1), on the leg asked only (`from`, `to`, each optional):
  - A return leg, another leg or a stop never meets it, and the saw says why: `platform Asterion: flying
    aquilo->gleba, 92.3% flown: not the leg asked, not counted (asked: gleba->any)`, or `platform Petrel II: not flying
    (at nauvis): not counted`.
  - When met, it keeps `evidence {tick, from, to, flown, length_km}` on the condition.
- A fired guard's queue history entry (and the stopped step's record) carries `evidence`: platform_hit's first hits,
  or platform_progress's progress and leg.
- Guards are checked every 10 ticks, so a guard fires at the first check past its threshold. On the copy, a guard
  `platform_damage` 40 fired at 20 hits and 100 damage under 2 hits a tick.
- All three conditions are taken by the remote and platform lanes, as waits and as guards' `when`. None changes
  anything.
- Cost, on the copy of world n (_autosave8, Rosetta):
  - The load: a level script hit 2 of Meridian-V's 1,095 entities a tick (120 hits a second), with an asteroid as
    cause, healing each back.
  - The ring write alone, timed in the game over 20,000 rows: 0.8 us a hit, written over in place (0.3 us of it the
    entity's position). A new table a hit was 2.7 us, plus garbage.
  - A platform_energy_below check on Asterion (160 accumulators): 0.41 ms. A guard checks every 10 ticks, so 0.04 ms a
    tick on average.
  - profile_ticks {seconds=60}, before (main) and after (this branch, with a platform_hit guard on Meridian-V, an energy
    guard on Asterion and a progress guard on Spindle, all checked and never met):
    - event on_entity_damaged: 0.139 ms a hit before, 0.161 after;
    - part scheduler.tick: 0.668 ms before, 0.829 after;
    - the whole tick: 3.07 ms before, 3.65 after.
    In 6 to 9 of the 61 seconds of each run a garbage collection finished inside the measured events and ticks, so
    these runs differ by more than the parts added. The first after run, with a new row a hit, read 0.191 ms a hit.
- Existing equivalents: none for the hits or the leg's progress (the platforms read shows it; nothing waited on it). For the energy, `circuit_signal` could read an accumulator's charge signal
  only when that accumulator is wired to the hub.
- Tests: tests/d22_batch92.lua. It covers:
  - a hit before the baseline, our own force's damage, and another platform's hit;
  - the first hit with its line, a hit with no cause, at_least, damage, and since_tick read back through the ring;
  - entity_names, and 70 hits between two checks;
  - the ring rows, the energy condition, the refusals and the lane checks.
### d22 batch91: quality in silo and shipment

- BA1 (Sol #1881: Meridian-V asked thruster@legendary 4 from Vulcanus and silo/shipment read "holds 0" and "the
  network can give 0" while 4 legendary sat in storage). On 2.0.77 `get_item_count(name)` counts normal quality alone
  (a copy of world n's 11:19 autosave: Meridian-V's hub read 2 solar-panel by name and held 4 epic; network 22 read 0
  accumulator by name and held 12 epic).
  - What the reads count: silo's platform request rows (`silo`, `shipment {ready}`, the auto-wait line) and shipment's
    up rows now count by the request's quality and comparator (its value `{name, quality, comparator}`; "=" when none;
    `>=`, `<=`, `>`, `<`, `!=` count each quality whose level passes). That covers what the hub holds, what is on the
    way, the silo network's stock (providers and storage) and other networks', the silo's own request against its
    rocket, and the planet's stock elsewhere (with "=").
  - Rows: they add `quality`, `comparator` and `custom_minimum` (the request's min payload). Lines name the quality
    when it is not normal, with the comparator when it is not "=": `Meridian-V asks accumulator (epic) 8 (holds 4,
    lacks 4), min payload 1 (its custom minimum), the silo's network can give 12 now (provider chests 0, storage chests
    12 ...)`. Normal "=" requests read as before.
  - The game's pick: shipment's up rows add `picked_silo` (a silo whose automatic requests fill a rocket for this
    platform now, its `transitional_request_target`), and a waiting line ends `the game's pick: rocket-silo at (15,141)
    fills a rocket for Meridian-V now` or `the game's pick: no silo on vulcanus fills a rocket for Meridian-V now`.
  - Not told apart: a rocket on its way keeps its cargo by name (`carries 1 of any quality` on a quality request). The
    down rows (pads' asks) stay by name.
  - Checked on the copy: Meridian-V's accumulator (epic) 8 read holds 4, network 12 (storage 12), `matched`; before,
    holds 0, network 0, `below_min_payload`.
## d22 batch90 AZ5: assembler_batch's holds are false at any count (Sol board #1878)

- A logistic condition reads the network's count less what deliveries have reserved, so it goes negative under
  reservations (Sol's legendary thruster batch read thruster -3): the batch's hold `PRODUCT < 0` held true there, the
  output inserter ran, and three legendary thrusters left the machine while the staging waited.
- Every hold the batch writes is now `ITEM < -2147483648` (the least 32-bit constant, as circuit_set `switch_off`
  writes on signal-dot): false whatever the network count. The output hold, the input hold while the requester fills,
  and the input off after the batch; `logistic: false` releases each as before. The plan and its schema say it.
- Audit of the other generated holds: batch.lua held the only fixed `< 0`; circuits.lua `switch_off` and platwait.lua
  already use the least constant. Checked on a copy of world n's 10:33 save: the dry run at Sol's machine (21.5,263.5)
  writes `thruster < -2147483648` and `steel-plate < -2147483648`; circuit_set with it on the output inserter reads
  `logistic_met: false`.

## d22 batch94 BD1: reminder gaps stay open, triggers besides the cadence, gear facts (viewer Aurora site:4267-4268)

- Reminder #114 personal-equipment-standard is Astra's: added d21 04:22 UTC (shift49) every 1 h to the team, its text
  edited at 11:30 to "after gear unlock/delivery and hourly, compare grid to stock ...", recipients named at 13:24
  (shift51), and the cadence set to 6 h on d22 18:38 UTC (shift58) with the text left as it was. "Missed" in
  reminders.lua: a run that comes while that recipient's line from an earlier run waits for reminder_ack; it folds into
  the waiting line. Haiku's (and Sonnet's) line waits from the run at tick 46207740 (their last ack: 46000623 and
  45999459); the six hourly runs from 46423740 to 47503740 are the six missed, the last 475 ticks before the 6 h edit.
- An ack's state (`states`, `latest[].state`, `yours`, and the ack's own `state`): `done` with a result; `open
  (acknowledged without a result)`; `open (gap: ITEMS)` with `gap_items`; `deferred (open[, gap: ITEMS])[: REASON]`
  with `deferred` (true or a reason up to 300 characters). An ack with a result and no gap_items closes it. The batch90
  AZ2 state (`acknowledged, not done: board #N ... unchanged since the ack`) still applies to a result on a board-linked
  reminder. `reminders {pending: true}` adds `open`: what the reader acknowledged that stays open. A checklist reads
  done once every step is recorded; `deferred`, `gap_items` and `gear` are refused on one.
- `gap_items` (1..8 item names): each read of the reminder gives `latest[].gap_facts` for that recipient, read then
  (gapfacts.lua): the recipes that make the item (hidden ones, recycling, left out) and whether each is enabled, the
  technologies whose effects unlock them and whether each is researched, the count in the logistic networks of the
  recipient's surface by quality (on a platform the hub's too), and the recipient's own count; one `line` each, also in
  the recipient's `latest` line. Nothing is refused on them.
- `gear: true` on an ack keeps the acker's own armor read (armor@quality, grid size, equipment by name and quality,
  free cells, shield, battery) with the result: `latest[].gear`, `gear_tick`, and in the line. Refused with `for` (a
  teammate's armor is not readable).
- `on {research?, delivered?, respawn?}` on reminder_add / reminder_edit (`false` clears), the owner's choice:
  - `research`: `true` (any technology), `"equipment"` (one whose unlock-recipe effects make an item placing as
    equipment or of type armor), or 1..16 names (a leveled one matches its base name); from on_research_finished.
  - `delivered`: `true` or `{items?: "equipment" | [names], surface?}`: a cargo pod received by a landing pad (freight's
    receipt) or a rocket's pod reaching a platform's hub (freight's up_settle), on that surface (a planet name, or a
    platform's name or surface; default the reminder's `surface`, else any).
  - `respawn: true`: a recipient's own respawn (bots.lua spawn 'respawn'), that recipient's run only.
  - A trigger starts a run for each recipient whose line does not wait (the line ends `this run on WHY`); a waiting
    one gets no second line and no missed run: `latest[].triggers_while_waiting` and `last_trigger` count them. The
    cadence's next run stays where it was. The row gives `on` (text) and `last_trigger {tick, why}`.
- `equipment {operation: "list"}` (an agent's own armor): `armor` (the armor worn, name@quality above normal), and
  `equipment` counts by name and quality (`energy-shield-equipment@rare*1`). The operator's `loadout` groups its
  equipment rows by quality too (`quality` on each).
- Checked on a copy of world n's 12:19 save (tick 47868759): a calcite pod from Solstice received at Nauvis's pad
  (52,54) started #118's run (on.delivered calcite, nauvis) and the next ten pods counted beside the wait;
  `energy-shield-mk2-equipment` set researched started it again (research "equipment"; captive-biter-spawner did
  not); Haiku's respawn started Haiku's run. Haiku's gap_facts: energy-shield-mk2-equipment recipe not enabled,
  technology not researched, 0 in Nauvis's 7 networks; battery-mk2-equipment researched, 963 there.
- BA2 (Sol #1882: Meridian-V's speed governor kept about 5k of fluid past its pumps, and the thrusters ran 43 s after a
  pump cut; Sol asked for the GUI's flush). `flush` already did this (the GUI's flush, `LuaFluidBox.flush`, reach or
  remote view as `configure`, `platform=` on a platform). Read on the copy (Meridian-V):
  - Without a fluid name 2.0.77's `flush(index)` removes nothing and returns `{}`, so `flush {position}` flushed
    nothing. It now flushes each fluid the segment holds, by name, as the GUI's button empties the segment.
  - The flush is the segment only. Emptying the thrusters' oxidizer segment left the pipes on the other side of the
    pump at 7205 before and after; a pump's own box is in no segment and kept its 400.
  - The game's count can be more than the segment read: the fuel segment read 12100 (its 7 thrusters' boxes, 1000 each,
    within it) and the flush returned 19100. The reply gives both: `flushed` (the game's count), `held_before` and
    `held_after` (the segment read before and after), and a line.
  - `dry_run: true`: `would_flush {fluid: amount}`, `amount`, `segment {id, extent, size, capacity, entities}` and a
    line (`would flush thruster-oxidizer 7205.5 from the segment of pipe (-14.5,36.5) (65 entities with fluidboxes,
    33x38 tiles); a pump bounds it: ...`), nothing flushed.
  - No other fluid edit and no spawning; the guest group cannot flush (`flush_opened_entity_fluid`).
  - Cost on the copy (x86 under Rosetta, a dispatch timed with the game's profiler, by remote view on Meridian-V): a

## d22 batch95 BE1 (eng/d20-batch95): a place_ghosts dry run that agrees with the placement on tiles (Astra #1892)

- Why: on Aquilo, Astra's dry run of a decider combinator on rough ice said `stands on 1 ice-rough tile: needs 1
  concrete first`, yet its verdict was `ok: every entry places`. The real call refused it: `placement blocked by
  tiles: ice-rough (needs concrete)`, with no tile ghost laid. Entries on brash ice and ammoniacal ocean read `no tile
  item makes it buildable`, though ice platform is made for them.
- The game's rules (2.0.77, read on the copy of world n):
  - Rough and smooth ice are ground and meltable. A decider, an assembler, inserters, pipes, belts and heat pipes
    collide with meltable; a medium pole does not.
  - Concrete goes on any tile that is not water. Ice platform goes only on ammoniacal ocean (both) and brash ice, and
    its tile is itself meltable. So a building there needs ice platform, then concrete on it.
  - The game's forced ghost check lays tile ghosts under an entity only for foundation-like tiles (landfill,
    foundation, ice platform). It refuses the ghost over tiles that need concrete.
  - The game takes an entity ghost over concrete tile ghosts. It takes a concrete tile ghost over an ice platform tile
    ghost. place_ghosts places its entries in order, and its `tiles` argument after them all.
- Checked on the copy:

  | Case | Dry run before | Real call | Dry run now |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | decider alone on rough ice | needs_tiles, verdict ok | refused | fails, naming the concrete |
  | concrete entries before it | after_tiles, ok | placed 3 | after_tiles, ok |
  | concrete entries after it | after_tiles, ok | refused | blocked: `entry #3 lays a tile under it after this one` |
  | decider alone on brash ice or ammoniacal ocean | `no tile item` | refused | blocked: `no one tile item makes it buildable; two do: ice-platform, then concrete on it` |
  | ice platform, concrete, decider | blocked: `the game refuses concrete there now` | placed 5 | after_tiles, ok |

- What changed:
  - **Entry note:** an entry that needs tiles the real call does not lay, where the game refuses its ghost now, says
    `...; the game refuses its ghost on ice-rough now, and place_ghosts lays no concrete ghost under it: concrete tile
    entries before it in this call lay them first`.
  - **Verdict:** it fails on those entries, as `1 entry the game refuses on the tiles there now, with no tile entry
    before it (...)`. The dry run gives `refused_until_tiles` and `refused_until_tiles_first`.
  - **Tile order:** an entity that tile entries after it (or the `tiles` argument) would make buildable is blocked,
    naming the order. One whose tile entries come before it is `after_tiles` and passes.
  - **Planned tiles:** each is checked against what lies under it then: an earlier entry's tile there, a tile ghost
    there, else the surface's. So concrete over a planned ice platform is taken.
  - **Two-step tiles:** with no one tile item, the dry run and the real refusal name two that do (`ice-platform, then
    concrete on it`).
  - **Real refusal:** place_ghosts' refusal on tiles adds that those tile entries before it lay the tile ghosts first.
- Tests: tests/dryrun.lua (BE1 block: an Aquilo-like world with rough ice, brash ice, concrete, ice platform and a
  meltable decider; the three orders, the two-step and the verdict).

  and the input off after the batch; `logistic: false` releases each as before. The plan and its schema say it.

  already use the least constant. Checked on a copy of world n's 10:33 save: the dry run at Sol's machine (21.5,263.5)
  writes `thruster < -2147483648` and `steel-plate < -2147483648`; circuit_set with it on the output inserter reads
  `logistic_met: false`.

### d22 batch96 BF1: single reads that stall a tick on world n

The 14:06 profile on world n (60 UPS on average, harness tick work 3.71 ms a tick) had single calls that each held one
tick. Measured on a private copy of world n's 13:05 autosave (`_autosave2`), each call timed with the game's profiler
around the runtime's dispatch. The copy runs the background work at world n's pace: survey.slice 0.41 ms a step
against 0.39, survey.band 0.52 against 0.55, census.step 0.10 against 0.08. So the ratio is 1:1, though the Mac was
loaded (load average 14-31) and single calls vary by up to 2x from one run to the next; the figures are each call's
best of three.

- Part 1, `platform NAME` (world n: 5 calls, 40.6 ms average, worst 83.5). Main's runtime on the copy: Asterion 73-93
  ms, of it `freight.stock_places` 36-49 (its 6,651 belts found in 24 ms and read in 44), the damaged list 4-5 (a find
  of every entity aboard: 7,957 in 33 ms, and its limit of 5,000 left 2,957 unread), the ammo model's quarter-minute
  stepping up to 5.9 ms a row, and the hub inserters (every inserter aboard, at most 500).
  - `stock_places` (the platform read, platform_endurance, preflight's ammo, freight's snapshots at a leg's ends)
    takes belts and inserter hands from the platform's last background read (`freight.belt_tick`). That read covers
    each platform read in the last 10 minutes, refreshed after a minute. A band of the platform's chunks is found
    every 3 ticks and at most 100 of what it found is read a step. On the copy, all 19 platforms (12,218 belts) were
    read within 60 s; `freight.belts` took 0.38 ms a step, a median 3.2 ms a game second (90th percentile 20.9). The
    ammo rows say `belts and inserter hands as read in the background N ago`. The hub, turrets and machine outputs
    are read now. Before a platform's first background read, the census pass's belts and hands are used (its pass
    takes about 10 minutes, said as its age), else all are read now as before.
  - The census counts an underground exit's buried lines once (its entrance's), as stock_places did (`where_is`
    counted them twice).
  - The damaged list: the game's damage events on our platform entities (platalerts.lua, up to 512 a platform) after
    one read of every entity aboard seeds it; a read checks those (healed or gone ones drop out). No 5,000 limit.
  - The hub inserters: those within 4 tiles of the hub's box (a long-handed one picks up 2 tiles out), not every one.
  - The thrusters are found once a tick (the thrust lines and after_pumps shared it); thrust's upstream machines come
    from the census's list.
  - The ammo model's `lasts`: the first quarter minute the stock is gone by halving the steps, then halved to a second
    as before (the same answer: tests/d22_batch96.lua).
  - On the copy, main's runtime and this one deployed in turn, each platform's best of three, twice:

    | | median | worst |
    |---|---|---|
    | main | 15.5-15.9 ms | 52.6-73.1 ms (Asterion, Petrel II) |
    | this branch | 11.4-11.8 ms | 16.5-18.5 ms (Meridian-V, Spindle) |

    Replies are the same size (13.3 KB median, 26 KB at most), plus the belt read's age note. Each read had one
    warm-up call first: the first call after a deploy fills caches.
  - The worst platforms are still over 10 ms. On Asterion (16-19 ms) that is the thrust lines' upstream walk of its

## d22 batch100 BJ1 (eng/d20-batch100): a platform_left wait counts the departure just before it (Sol #1905)

- Sol (shift59): queue lane `platform:Meridian-V`, a platform_schedule step (`stops [nauvis (time 0), vulcanus]`,
  `current: 2`, `paused: false`) then `wait_until platform_left {location: nauvis}`. The wait began with the platform
  already on its path and read `flying nauvis->vulcanus 12%; met when it stops at nauvis and leaves again (a departure
  before this wait does not count)`, so the pumps the steps after it switch on stayed off.
- Reproduced on the private copy (world n's 13:52 autosave, tick 48189019, Sol's queue in it; 200 uranium rounds added
  to the hub so its fuel and ammo wait was met). With the save's runtime, the platform_schedule step read `on_the_path,
  nauvis->vulcanus 0%` at tick 48193552 with no `departed` note. The wait began in the same tick and read, a second
  later, `Meridian-V flying nauvis->vulcanus 11%; ... (a departure before this wait does not count)`.
- Why: d19 batch48 made platform_schedule record the departure it causes, and a platform_left wait begun within 60
  ticks counts it. It kept the platform only when `type(platform) == 'table'`. Every game object is userdata in 2.0
  (read on the copy: a LuaSpacePlatform, LuaForce and LuaSurface are all `userdata`). So no departure was ever recorded
  on the real engine; the tests' platforms are tables. A direct `platform_schedule {platform: Solstice, current: 2}` on
  the copy sent Solstice off and recorded nothing either (`schedule_departures` nil).
- Fixed: space.lua keeps the platform whenever M.platform finds it. The same table check in platform_schedule_call
  (space.lua) also turns off the platform schedule edit log (`told_of_setting_edit`, `told_of_edit`) on the real
  engine. That is unchanged here: turning it on would start tells that have never been sent.
- And: `platform_left` counts a departure in the platform log (freight.lua: arrivals and departures, logged on the game
  second after, the last 40) at or after a baseline:
  - `since_tick`, when given (a game tick up to now; platform_left's, as platform_loss's and platform_hit's);
  - in a queue, the tick the step before it in the same plan began (the scheduler keeps the last started step on the
    queue and gives the wait `after_step {tick, action}`); a wait that begins a plan has no such step;
  - else, as before, its first check.
  saw: `Solstice left nauvis at tick 48194580 (after the step before this wait, wait_ticks, began at tick 48194422);
  now flying nauvis->gleba 0%`, or `(since_tick T)`; unmet with a baseline, `(a departure before tick T does not
  count)`.
- On the copy with the branch runtime (the save loaded again):
  - Sol's queue: the platform_schedule step's reply has `departed: left nauvis at tick 48193352 (state on_the_path) ...`.

## d22 batch101 BK1: a spidertron's route as its remote gives it (viewer Aurora site:4308)

- `vehicle {go_to}` used to append every target (`add_autopilot_destination`). The game walks a spidertron in a
  straight line toward its next target and keeps a target its legs cannot reach: speed 0, the target kept, nothing
  said. On world n's save (d22 14:38) Opus's spidertron #23036938 stood at a lake's edge at (-133.9,-433) with
  [(185,175), (-60,-300)] queued since shift59 22:28 (the first across deep water, the detour behind it), and #22731300
  at (-40,498) with [(-70,545), (-72,545)] since shift58 19:28. Opus's shift58 calls show the trap: at 20:46 the
  spidertron stood at (-102.05,-680.04) with (-16,-962) ahead, and three more go_to calls in two minutes queued behind it.
- Now `go_to` replaces the route by default, as a click on the spidertron remote does; `mode: "append"` adds at the
  end, as a shift-click; `go_to` takes one point or a list of 1..16; `clear: true` empties the route. The default is
  replace: a call to a spidertron with no route behaves as before either way, and a call meant as "go there now"
  (every one in shifts 58-59) no longer waits behind an unreachable target. The reply carries `route` (the targets in
  order), `route_line`, `replaced` (the targets it dropped), `cleared` (how many).
- `vehicle {position}` (or `remote: true, vehicle`) of a spidertron with nothing else reads `route`, `route_line` and,
  when stalled, `stalled` {since_tick, for_s, position, target, ahead, line}; a spidertron no one sent this way is
  sampled from that read on (`sampling`). Any other vehicle with only a position is refused as before.
- spiderroute.lua samples each spidertron sent by go_to every 60 ticks: no move of 0.5 tiles and no nearer to its
  target for 600 ticks while it has a target is a stall. The sender gets one line in its next reply ("spidertron
  #23036938: no progress toward (185,175) for 10s, standing at (-133.9,-433) (687 tiles from it); on the straight line
  ahead: water at (-133.5,-432.5), 1 tile ahead (collision layers it shares with the legs: player); its route: ..."),
  and one when it moves again; status lists `spidertrons` with a route and their stalls. "Ahead": the first tile or
  entity within 24 tiles on the straight line whose collision mask shares a layer with the leg prototype's.
- Measured on a copy of that save (about 60 UPS): spiderroute.tick 60 runs in 60 s, 4.38 ms in all (0.073 ms a run,
  the worst 2.82 ms: the run that found the stall and read the line ahead), one spidertron sampled.

## d22 batch97 BG3 cp2 (eng/d20-batch97): the `chart` operator read, for the site's chart

Nick asked for a map like the Galaxy of Fame's; batch97's study recommends drawing it from data. The stream service
(tools/stream/chart.py, cp3) draws every planet and platform as 384-tile cells at 1 px a tile in the game's map colours
from this read. New operator read `chart` (chart.lua; describe's operator_reads lists it; agents cannot call it), read
only:
- `chart {surfaces: true}`: every planet and platform surface: `[{name, index, platform, dirty, read}]` (2.3 ms on the
  d22 copy of world n, 23 surfaces).
- `chart {protos: true}`: one string, `E name type w h friendly enemy map` a line per entity prototype (colours rrggbb,
  `-` none; `friendly_map_color` is set on every entity prototype, `map_color` only on resources, trees, rocks, cliffs
  and rails) and `T name map` a tile (419 lines, 18 KB, 11.6 ms; read once a service start).
- `chart {surface, list: [cx0, cy0, cx1, cy1]}`: which chunks our force has charted in that box, a string of 0 and 1 a
  chunk row, at most 4096 chunks (6.2 ms for 4096; Nauvis has 3,214 charted in the 64x64 chunks round the origin).
- `chart {surface, chunks: [cx, cy, ...]}` and `chart {surface, dirty: N, min_age?, check?}`: rows for those chunks, or
  for up to N chunks marked dirty (oldest mark first), each last read at least `min_age` ticks ago (default 36000, 10
  game minutes) or never. A read stops after 6 chunks or once 1200 entities are read (at least one chunk); `rest` the
  chunks left. `check: K` first counts the entities in up to K (at most 128) read chunks from a rotating cursor
  (count_entities_filtered with the read's filter) and marks a chunk whose count changed: robot builds, since
  control.lua forwards no on_robot_built_entity. Reply `{tick, surface, chunks, entities, rest, tn, en, rows}`, plus
  `waiting, checked, marked` for dirty; `rows` one string: `C cx cy`, `T` 32 tile rows of `index,run ...` joined by `|`
  (indices into `tn`), `E index x2 y2 direction force` an entity whose position is in the chunk (index into `en`,
  position in half tiles, force 1 ours, 2 enemy, 0 neutral), `R x2 y2 recipe`, `S x2 y2 stop name`; `U cx cy` a chunk
  not charted. Characters, units, corpses, ghosts, robots, rolling stock, fish and other short-lived types are left out.
- The dirty set: a forwarded on_built_entity, on_player_mined_entity, on_robot_mined_entity or on_entity_died marks the
  entity's chunk (one table write; ghosts and enemy units not); a read clears it. Kept in storage per surface: the
  dirty marks, each read chunk's read tick and entity count (Nauvis about 3,200 chunks).
Cost on the x86 private copy (world n's _autosave11 of d22): a read of the base's densest chunks 7.5-10.2 ms (3 to 6
chunks, 788-1,551 entities, 17-30 KB), 6 outer chunks 4.5-5.2 ms, `check` 64 or 128 with `dirty` 1.5 ms (about 0.06
ms a dense chunk counted). The event marks: see BG3 cp2 in the batch report (profile_ticks). Strings rather than
tables of numbers: table_to_json takes about 28 us a number on that copy. Tests: tests/d22_batch97.lua.
## d22 batch104 BN1: a belt pickup's count and where it went (Sol #1925)

- Sol's report: `pickup {belt: true}` on Fulgora (area (-346,-23)-(-345,-8), 15 belts) reported 1000 and 200 picked
  while scans before and after showed 120 scrap on the same 15 belts (full: 8 a tile).
- The count is what the belt lines gave up: each take inserts into the character, then `remove_item` on the lane, and
  only what that returns is counted (what the belt did not give back is taken out of the character again). Reproduced
  on a copy of world n's _autosave12 (d22, the save before Sol's calls), Sol's character placed where it stood, the 15
  belts given 58 scrap: the pickup took 60 (the 58 and 2 that the belt brought in from upstream), the belts held 0 after.
  Sol's request max for scrap is 0, so the game moves what is picked to the trash slots within a few ticks, and the
  logistic robots of network 848 took it from there within about 60 ticks to the storage chest at (-316.5,-11.5)
  (541 -> 601). Between the saves before and after Sol's calls that chest went 541 -> 1100. So an item counted had left
  the belt; a belt fed from upstream as fast as it is taken (a fast belt brings up to 30 items a second; Sol's first
  pickup took 1000 in 2089 ticks, 0.48 a tick) shows the same count before and after.
- Now the end says it: `last.belt` gives each belt before -> after (those that changed first, 32 at most),
  `area_before`, `area_after`, `came_in` (taken less the area's drop), and where what was taken is: `kept` (main
  inventory), `in_trash` (trash slots), `gone_from_you` (to the trash over a request max and taken by robots, or used),
  and a `line` saying all of it. Three passes over belts in reach that show the items but remove none end it
  `nothing_removed` (before, it tried until its ticks ran out).

## d22 batch105 BO1 (eng/d20-batch105): the forecast over the part of a leg flown (Astra #1927)

- Astra: Asterion flew only the first part of its outer legs, and `platform_endurance {forecast: true}` scaled them
  `x1.00`, as if the legs flown were the whole connection.
- Reproduced on a private copy of world n's _autosave1 (15:53, tick ~48621000), route aquilo -> solar-system-edge ->
  aquilo, with the save's runtime:
  - `scaled from the legs flown in the last 2 hours: aquilo->solar-system-edge, solar-system-edge->aquilo, ...`;
  - every kind `(flown ...)` equal to the leg's own mean;
  - each ammunition `x1.00`.
- What freight.lua had recorded for Asterion: aquilo->solar-system-edge (100,000 km) flown 0-13% then turned back
  (solar-system-edge->aquilo 87-100%), the same again to 15%, and out now at 13%.
- Now (routeammo.lua):
  - The legs flown are those finished in the last 2 hours and the leg flown now, so far. The moving rate they scale
    counts it too.
  - Each has the part of its connection flown, `km0 / length` to `km1 / length` the way it was flown (freight's distance
    along the connection). A leg recorded before those were kept counts as flown whole (0-100%). One opened mid-flight
    without them says `the part flown not recorded: the whole connection taken`.
  - Its asteroids are the game's spawn chance over that part: `asteroid_spawn_definitions`' spawn points, by distance
    from the connection's own `from` (a leg flown the other way reads them from 1), linear between points, averaged
    over the part (`density_range`). The use is scaled by the route leg's whole mean over that.
  - Each route leg's line adds how much of it the legs flown cover, the way it flies: `the legs flown cover 15% of it
    (0-15%); the other 85% is the game's spawn definition, not measured`, or `cover all of it`, or `include none of
    this connection: all of it is the game's spawn definition, scaled by the rate measured elsewhere`.
  - `forecast_coverage [{leg, flown (the parts, joined), flights, covered (0..1)}]`.
- On the copy with the branch:
  - `scaled from the legs flown in the last 2 hours (each the part of its connection flown, and minutes):
    aquilo->solar-system-edge 0-13% 15m00s, solar-system-edge->aquilo 87-100% 6m53s, aquilo->solar-system-edge 0-15%
    17m03s, solar-system-edge->aquilo 85-100% 7m44s, aquilo->solar-system-edge 0-13% (flying now) 14m09s (1h00m)`;
  - each outer leg `the legs flown cover 15% of it`;
  - the flown spawn chance of the huge asteroids is 0.0000 against 0.0003-0.0004 over the leg (they spawn further
    out);
  - so the use scales x2.61 (magazines), x2.66 (railgun ammo) and x16.30 (rockets, 432 a huge asteroid) instead of
    x1.00.
  - The read took 60-83 ms on the copy (173 ms with the save's runtime, the first call).
- Test tests/d22_batch105.lua:
  - the mean over a part, either way flown, and at a point;
  - the scale line with each part, and the leg flown now;
  - a route leg covered 25%, its scale x4.96 worked out by hand, and one not flown;
  - the coverage rows;
  - a leg flown whole before km was kept, and one with no part recorded.

## d22 batch105 BO2 (eng/d20-batch105): the forecast by the turrets' targets (Astra 20:24)

Astra after BO1: "forecast rocket line counts 432 shots per huge and scales x8.85, but Asterion rocket turrets target
ONLY big asteroids; rails handle huge." The forecast counted every asteroid of the route, and its fragments, against
every ammunition aboard.

- The game's rule (2.0.77; platdefense.lua reads the same): a turret fires at the entities on its own priority list
  (the turret GUI's) only when Ignore unprioritised targets is on; off, at any (the list only orders them). Turret,
  asteroid and ammunition prototypes share one target mask (common) and no ammunition has a target filter. A turret
  prototype has no default list to read at runtime; a rocket turret built new on the copy read an empty list and
  ignore off.
- platform_endurance `forecast: true` (routeammo.lua, endurance.lua; runtime deploy needed) reads the turrets aboard
  once (each one's ammunition category, ammo, list and ignore flag; before, a surface search per ammunition). For each
  ammunition, an asteroid counts its own shots only when one of the turrets that fire it targets it. Its fragments
  count when a turret aboard targets the asteroid, each fragment the same way. An asteroid no turret aboard targets
  counts for no ammunition, nor do its fragments. An asteroid targeted by turrets of two ammunitions counts in full for
  each. With no turret read aboard, every asteroid counts for each ammunition, as before, and the line says so.
- Shots text: `huge-metallic-asteroid not its turrets' target + 15 for its fragments`, `X: no turret aboard targets
  it`; `no turret aboard fires it: no use estimate`.
- A `turret targets as built` block:
  - per ammunition, the turrets that fire it with their settings grouped (`rocket: 26 turrets fire it, mixed settings:
    24 rocket-turret big only; 2 rocket-turret big, medium only`; `any asteroid (ignore unprioritised targets off)`;
    `its targets not read (counted as any)`);
  - per asteroid of the route and its fragments, the turrets that target it (`medium-carbonic/metallic/oxide-asteroid:
    gun-turret 48 (firearm-magazine), rocket-turret 2 (rocket)`; `no turret aboard targets it: no ammunition counted
    for it or its fragments`).
  Row `forecast_targets {ammo [{ammo, turrets, settings [{turret, count, targets (names, any, unknown)}], mixed}],
  asteroids [{asteroid, turrets [{turret, count, ammo}]}]}`.
- Headless copy of world n's 19:23 autosave, Asterion flying aquilo->solar-system-edge, route [aquilo,
  solar-system-edge, aquilo]: 23 railgun turrets huge only, 48 gun turrets small and medium only, 24 rocket turrets
  big only and 2 big and medium only, ignore unprioritised targets on for all 97.
  - rocket: x8.87 (huge 432 + 42 for its fragments) before; now x2.09 (big 2 + 3, huge not its target + 15), about
    13553 used on the first leg where it read 57500.
  - railgun-ammo: x2.12 before; now x17.59 (huge 1 each; its measured 0.9/min is from legs whose part flown spawns
    huge at under 0.00005), about 1702 on the first leg where it read 205.
  - firearm-magazine: x2.09 both (big and huge are other turrets' targets; their fragments counted before too).
  - The read: 26-48 ms before, 29-46 ms after (four calls each).
## d22 batch100 BJ2 (eng/d20-batch100): game objects checked as tables (audit)

BJ1 found `type(platform) == 'table'` dropping a LuaSpacePlatform. In 2.0 every game object is userdata. Read on a
private copy of world n's _autosave8 (14:38, tick 48351336): `prototypes`, `prototypes.entity`, a quality prototype, a
platform, a force and a surface are all `userdata`.
- Method: the runtime's 446 `type(x) == 'table'` checks, and its `'string'` checks on fields, narrowed in two ways:
  - by name (entity, surface, force, platform, prototype, quality, stack, ...);
  - by where the value came from: an API call or field within 40 lines above.
- The API values they test, read on the copy:
  - plain tables with string names and qualities: an inserter's `get_filter`, a splitter's filter, `get_contents` rows
    (inventories, transport lines), logistic section filter values, logistic point `filters`, a landing pad's
    `get_logistic_point()` (a table of 3 points);
  - userdata: `LuaItemStack.quality`, `entity.quality`, `get_recipe()` (a LuaRecipe and a quality), a robot order's
    `target_item.name` (LuaItemPrototype) and `.quality`;
  - `unit.spawner` is no key in 2.0.77 (`LuaEntity doesn't contain key spawner`); it is `unit.commandable.spawner`.

Fixed (each restores what it was written for; no new tell or alert):

| Where | What it skipped on the real engine | Seen on the copy |
|---|---|---|
| space.lua:2178 (cp1) | platform_schedule's departure record | BJ1 |
| lessonbook.lua:211 | `type(prototypes) == 'table'`: ground_rule_add/edit `applies_to` names never checked (a misspelled name was saved) | before: `ground_rule_edit {id: 3, applies_to: ["electric-mining-dril"]}` saved it; after: `applies_to: no entity, item or recipe named electric-mining-dril` |
| serves.lua:19 | the same: an order's or reminder's `serves.name` never checked | unit test |
| supply.lua:463 | a robot's pickup item (`target_item.name`, a prototype) never matched, so supply's network lines never named who reserved the providers' stock (`reserved for (x,y) requester-chest N`) | Nauvis, 7 items: 0 reservation lines before, every item named them after (e.g. iron-plate: `reserved for (-32.5,-9.5) requester-chest 76, ... (+35 more)`) |
| threat.lua:597 | an attack's source as the unit's own spawner (`from nest` instead of `likely from nest`): unit.spawner errors in 2.0.77, and the spawner, userdata, failed the table check | not seen to fire, see below |

threat.lua on the copy, three attacks on our entities:
- a big spitter and a big biter commanded to attack: at the hit their `commandable.spawner` read nil;
- a gun turret by a nest: worms hit first, and the source is looked up once an incident, on the first hit.

All three read `likely from nest`, the nearest charted spawner, as before. Idle units by a nest do give
`commandable.spawner`. The fix reads it when it is there.

Left, as the operator asked, because a fix would start messages:
- space.lua:2197, platform_schedule_call: the schedule edit log's tells (`told_of_setting_edit`, `told_of_edit`) have
  been off on the real engine since they were written.

  target, `j.order .. ' ' .. j.item` raises, so the robot_losses read and its alert groups fail for that robot. A fix
  would let those lines show.

Harmless (the check is wrong for userdata, but the code works):

  `ingredients` as well.
- the `type(x.quality) == 'table' and x.quality.name or x.quality` reads on `get_contents` rows (pods.lua:23,

Tests use userdata fakes (a file handle with its own metatable), never table fakes for game objects:

    and wait for a full one (stack-inserter: ...)"), and in inspect's `inserter_line` ("holding 3 iron-plate of
