## d24 batch147 PS1 (eng/d20-batch147): the blueprint library mirror's steady pass reads the revision alone
- tools/bplibrary.py's watch (start-team.sh, every 60 s) read every entry's facts each pass: 15.3 ms on world n
  (158 entries, 133 KB, tick 56169756), over world n's 10 ms rule.
- The operator read `blueprint_library` takes two new forms (blueprints.lua):
  - `{probe: true}`: `{revision, tick, count}` alone. 0.06 ms on world n (06:41, the read's Lua in the harness mod's
    state), 0.17 ms through dispatch on the private copy.
  - `{since, limit, after?}`: a page of `limit` entries by name after `after`, each with its facts, and the string of
    each changed since `since`, 400 KB of strings a page at most (at least one); `next_after` names the page's last entry
    while more follow.
  - Without `probe` or `limit`, the read is as before (`strings_after`).
- A pass reads the probe; when the revision is the one it last saw and every entry in index.json has its NAME.txt here,
  that is the pass. Otherwise it reads pages of 24 (`PAGE`) from `since` (from -1 when a file is missing), and writes
  NAME.txt, deleted/ and index.json once, after the last page. A page whose revision differs from the first page's ends
  the pass unwritten; the next pass reads again. A runtime without the probe answers with its whole read, which the
  pass still takes.
- Cost on world n (the page's Lua, one run each, smallest first): pages of 2, 4, 8, 16 entries 0.23, 0.47, 0.79,
  1.75 ms; pages of 32 2.5-4.9 ms (six pages). The JSON's numbers are most of it (on the copy each number in a reply
  costs about 0.03 ms). On the copy (4.6x world n's times: the old read 70.8 ms there): a page of 24 11.6 ms, the
  heaviest strings page (389 KB) 12.4 ms.
- The change path on the copy: a first pass 10 reads (158 strings); the next 1 read, index.json untouched; an import
  8 reads, its string alone written; its delete 8 reads, the file to deleted/.
- tools/stream/library.py reads index.json, never the game. The stream's `library_areas` (live.py, every 60 s) read
  3.1 ms on world n. tools/read_cost.py lists `blueprint_library_probe`, `blueprint_library_page` and `library_areas`.
- Tests: tools/test_bplibrary.py (probe, pages, a revision moving between pages, the older runtime); tests/blueprints.lua
  (probe, pages by name, the strings' budget). Both fail on main.
## d24 batch146 PR1 (eng/d20-batch146): a delivery watch with from ends by receipt only, and counts on after it ends (Sol #2152)
- Sol's watch #305 (1 calcite from Needle to Nauvis's pad) ended `reached` when another carrier's pod of 60 landed,
  with received 0. An ended watch was no longer registered for pods, so it froze while Needle's 8 pods brought 32.
- Now:
  - With `from`, the watch ends only when its count is received from that source (that platform's pods; up, rockets
    from that planet). The stock test stays `stock` {held, at_start, reached, ends_watch: false, line} and never ends
    it. Its line adds `; with from given it does not end the watch (it ends when N is received from X)`, and the setter
    hears once that it was met and does not end the watch.
  - With no `from`, batch134's rule stands: either test ends it. `ended_by` (stock or received) says which, and the end
    alert reads `reached by the stock test: ...` or `received ...` with the stock test apart.
  - A watch that ends before its deadline counts on until the deadline (`counting`, `reached_tick`; the line reads
    `ended by the received total, reached at tick T; still counting until the deadline (...): later pods add to
    received`). Its pods are still registered and its consumer's count still read. At the deadline the count ends,
    and the setter hears the total (`the deadline ended its count: received ...`). A watch that ends after its
    deadline does not count on. `{id, clear: true}` ends it at any time.
  - A from-watch past its deadline reads `deadline passed, not received from X`.
- Other watch kinds that end on a stock test: none with a carrier.
  - wait_until pod_landed counts freight's receipts from its named platform.
  - wait_until item_count, fluid_count and rocket_parts are stock conditions by design, with no source.
  - flight_watch, collector_tally, turret_tally, uptime, belt_flow, asteroid_watch and signal_watch end on time or
    arrival.
- On a headless copy of world n's 05:55 save (tick 56123930, Petrel II and Petrel III at Nauvis, pad (52,54) empty):
  a watch for 1 calcite from Petrel II, a drop of 60 from Petrel III, then two drops of 4 from Petrel II.
  - Before (world n's runtime): the watch read `reached`, received 0, once Petrel III's pod landed. After Petrel II's
    two pods it still read received 0, and its stock was frozen at 48.
  - After (this runtime, from the same save): it stayed `open` with the stock test met and `ends_watch: false`.
    Petrel II's first pod of 4 ended it (`received`, ended_by received, reached_tick 56127746, counting). Its second
    pod was counted after the end: received 8 in 2 pods, by_platform Petrel II 8.
- Tests: tests/d24_batch146.lua (fails on main: `before: reached`). tests/d21_batch66.lua, d22_batch107.lua and
  d23_batch134.lua: their from-watches now end by receipt (d23_batch134's last case was this fault: 150 of 400
  received from Kestrel IVa, read `reached` on stock 515).
## d24 batch148 PT1 (eng/d20-batch148): a queue paused by another process's read made as the agent (Astra #2159)
- Cause, found on a copy of world n's shift68 save (05:40, tick 56315793):
  - Astra's body lane was interrupted about every 1000 ticks with "a call of yours failed while your queue ran": job
    36694 (her courier of 199 tungsten-plate, interrupted at 56290477, "not run again") and job 36706 at 56293249,
    56294266, 56295334 and 56296376.
  - Her journal has no call at those ticks, except 56294733 (her own direct transfer). Her failed-call record
    (selfview) has none that minute.
  - With the copy running and nothing outside calling, her pause record did not change over 7000 ticks.
  - Each read the other processes make as her was sent on the copy with a queue running. Only `board_focus {peek:
    true}` interrupted it: board_focus was neither passive, a read nor a talk call, so dispatch_request's direct-call
    pause took her character.
  - The stream service reads board_focus as its reader, the team file's first bot (astra), each overlay pass.
  - The pause text was stop_player's for a failure ("a call of yours failed"), though nothing failed.
- Who dispatches under an agent's name:
  - the stream service (tools/stream/harness.py: profiles, chat, describe, board_events, board_focus,
    board_progress, platforms, reminders, board, status per agent, as the first bot);
  - the analyst (tools/analyst/game.py, `--bot` the first bot: describe, chat, board, status, profiles, power);
  - chat-log.py (`fh call chat --bot` the first bot);
  - fh_broker's status probe;
  - read_cost.py;
  - broker-probe.sh;
  - the live_check tools (their own test bots).
  - idle_nudge, the viewers relay, harness-requests and orders_kill dispatch as operator. Standing orders run in the
    agent's own queue while it is free.
- Changed:
  - Runtime:
    - board_focus is passive (a read or a focus set moves no character).
    - A request with `reader` (the reading process's name) takes reads only. One that could drive the character is
      refused (`reader stream: move_to acts as the agent ...`). It never pauses the queue or stops the character,
      failed or not, and is not counted as the agent's call (selfview, hauling, the failed-call record).
  - Tools: the stream service (`reader: "stream"`), the analyst (`"analyst"`), fh_broker's probe (`"broker"`) and
    read_cost (`"read_cost"`) send it; an older runtime ignores it. chat-log.py goes through `fh call` and reads chat,
    which is passive.
  - A pause names its call: the direct-call pause `paused by your direct move_to call (request ID), which drives your
    character`; a failed call `your move_to call (request ID) failed while your queue ran (...)` (M.last_failed,
    recorded by M.dispatch for a player's failed call).
  - scheduler.pause_inner: an interrupted transfer, feed, deliver or pickup step is never dropped. One that had moved
    nothing goes back to the head as it was (`requeued as it was: it had moved nothing`). One that had moved some with
    no remainder known (no tour stops left to go on from) holds the lane (`q.held`, so a direct call's end does not
    resume it), named in paused_why and the step's not_requeued: `held: job-N transfer was interrupted after moving N;
    the rest of it is not known, so it is not run again; queue_resume runs the plan's next step`.
- On the copy, before (world n's runtime): board_focus {peek: true} as astra interrupted her running wait_ticks with
  "a call of yours failed while your queue ran".
- After (this runtime):
  - board_focus as reader stream, and as astra herself, left the queue running. A reader's failed observe left it
    running, and a reader's move_to was refused and left it running.
  - Her own direct move_to paused it with `paused by your direct move_to call (request b148-3c96d6d849), which drives
    your character`.
  - Her courier with job 36694's arguments (to an empty chest), interrupted mid-walk by a direct move_to, went back to
    the head: `requeued as it was: it had moved nothing (an item move is not skipped)`.
- Tests: tests/d24_batch148.lua (fails on main: `before: paused by a call of yours failed`).


## d24 batch145 PQ1 (eng/d20-batch145): blueprint status marks; the site's blueprint page gets search, kinds, filters, sorting (viewer Foobator)
- Viewer Foobator (site:4615, 05:12): "could we have a search function and maybe categories for blueprints? also some
  kind of mark for current/experimental/obsolete and whatever else could be useful maybe?"
- Harness (blueprints.lua): an entry's `status {value, by, tick, note}`.
  - `blueprint_status {name, status, note?}`: status `current`, `experimental` or `obsolete`, `none` clears it; note
    1..200 characters (not with none). Any agent may set it on any entry; the mark keeps who and when. Reply: status,
    line (`experimental, marked by luna 0m ago: note`, or `NAME: not marked`), was, last_used, retired; or unchanged.
    Bumps the library revision (the operator mirror rewrites index.json).
  - `blueprint_save {status?, status_note?}`: sets it with the save (a bad status refuses before anything is saved);
    without status a replaced entry's mark is kept (`status_kept`). A rename keeps it (the same entry).
  - `blueprint_list` rows: status; one entry in full: status_by, status_set, status_note. The operator read
    (`blueprint_library`) adds status_tick and, for an entry saved on a platform, `platform_name` (the platform's
    name now).
  - Nothing sets a status by itself: not age, not blueprint_retire.
  - `status` and `note` are doc-only keys in describe (DOC_ONLY); EXTRA_ARGS lets them through for these actions.
- tools/bplibrary.py copies every entry's facts as the read gives them: status, status_by, status_tick, status_note,
  platform_name reach runs/RUN/blueprints/index.json with no change there. tools/stream/library.py's live rows carry
  status.
- Page (site/blueprints.py):
  - A search box over name, author, description, entity names, surface (and `platform N`, the platform's name) and the
    status: every word must match, any case; it filters as you type.
  - Filters: where saved (each planet, or Space platform), kind, status (current, experimental, obsolete, not marked),
    each option with its count. A kind is decided by the entry's entities: it holds at least one of the kind's
    entities (rail, power and heat, defence, science (labs), smelting and casting, mining and pumping, oil and
    chemistry, assembly and special crafting, platform hull, robots and logistic chests, circuits); the page lists the
    rules ("How a kind and a status are decided"). An entry can be in several kinds or none.
  - Sorting: newest saved, most used, name. "Showing N of M blueprints".
  - The URL keeps the view (?q=&place=&kind=&status=&sort=; history.replaceState, no reload).
  - Each entry: a status mark beside its name (`not marked` when none), a Status row (who marked it, the game time, the
    note), Retired when retired, Kinds, and Uses with its last use as before. Saved on adds the platform's name.
  - Without script every entry shows and the controls stay hidden. Pictures load only when asked, as before.
  - The page's scripts sit in its head: the filter script and the live-entries script (LIVE_JS) now start at
    DOMContentLoaded; before, LIVE_JS found no section and never showed entries saved since the build.
  - Phone width: an entry's facts column may shrink and long text wraps (entity lists ran past the screen at 390 px).
- Checked:
  - site/build.py on the real runs (shift 68's copy, 158 entries): 90 pages; screenshots in headless Chromium (the
    Playwright headless shell): desktop at 1300 px, `?q=turret&place=platform&sort=used` reads "Showing 40 of 158
    blueprints"; phone at 390 px with `?kind=defence`: 51 of 158, no page-wide scroll after the wrap fix.
  - world n (tick 56169756): the operator read without strings (as bplibrary.py makes each pass): 158 entries,
    revision 497, none marked; 15.3 ms, 133 KB.
  - headless copy of world n's 05:46 autosave: the same read 69-72 ms before the deploy and 71-82 ms after (the
    container is about 4.7x slower than world n); 1.4 KB more (platform names). luna's blueprint_status on
    Sol68-GreenPair-Feeds-OFF-DRAFT (experimental with a note), refused for "draft"; sol's blueprint_list of it read
    status_by luna; a blueprint_save with status current, saved again without status: status_kept; a
    bplibrary.mirror pass from the copy wrote both marks (with status_by, status_tick, status_note) and 52
    platform_name values into index.json.
- Tests: tests/blueprints.lua (status block: fails on main at the first status check), site/test_blueprints.py
  (marks, kinds, places, search text, controls; the filter script in a stub DOM under node: waits for
  DOMContentLoaded, the URL's view on load, search words, status filter, the three sorts, the count, the URL).

## d24 batch152 PX1 (eng/d20-batch152): power, inspect and the statistics reads leave out quality (Astra #2182)
- Cause: in 2.0.77 a LuaFlowStatistics read by name (`get_flow_count{name=...}`, `get_input_count(name)`,
  `get_output_count(name)`) counts normal quality only; `name={name=, quality=}` counts that quality (a `quality=`
  field beside the name is ignored), and `input_counts`/`output_counts` give each name's total over every quality.
  Measured on a copy of world n's 07:36 autosave (tick 56717928), Asterion (20 rare laser turrets, 1 rare and 4
  normal fusion generators, 2 uncommon asteroid collectors):
  - electric: laser-turret by name 0, as the rare pair 96000 J a tick (5.76 MW); input_counts' laser-turret equal to
    the rare total; fusion-generator's output_counts the normal plus the rare total;
  - item statistics: 21 items on Nauvis, 8 on Vulcanus, 30 on Fulgora and 1 on Gleba with counts at other qualities;
  - build statistics: fusion-generator 4 by name, 1 rare; laser-turret 0 by name, 20 rare;
  - kill statistics: platform-18's 6 lost solar panels epic (0 by name);
  - fluid statistics take a name only (a pair fails: "amount is missing"); pollution statistics too ("Invalid
    EntityID"); they stay plain;
  - a read is 0.4-5 us, a pair the same with its argument table kept.
- Changed:
  - mod/qflow.lua: a name's flow (`flow`, `flow_by`) or count (`count`, `count_by`) over every visible quality, with
    `by` (each quality with any, by level); given the name's input_counts/output_counts total, a name only ever
    counted at normal is read once.
  - power: consumers and producers a row per name and quality (`quality` when not normal), totals over every quality,
    `qualities`; the generator rows' `network_output_kw` is that name and quality's; the draw line names
    `laser-turret (rare)`. platform_power the same (`qualities`, the line says every quality); by_cause rows too.
  - inspect's electricity: `now_kw_its_quality` (its own quality), `now_kw_all_of_name` and `now_by_quality` (every
    quality); an electric turret's `buffer_kj`, `buffer_max_kj`, `buffer_pct`, `input_limit_kw`; an accumulator's
    `charge_kw`/`discharge_kw` from `get_input_flow_limit(quality)`/`get_output_flow_limit(quality)` (2.0.77's source

## d24 batch161 QD1 (eng/d20-batch161): the asteroid watch's trajectories by name, the rarest first (Astra #2212)
- Astra: Probe6's watch counted 1 huge-promethium destroyed and 3 big-promethium leaving the view, and its
  trajectories showed only the first 24 asteroids seen, all common, so the rare encounter could not be found.
- `platform_defense {platform, asteroids: true}` (the read, running or done): `trajectories` now covers every tracked
  asteroid (the first `tracked_cap`, 3000, seen), a page at a time, each row: `name`, `unit`, `first_tick`, `first_s`,
  `first_position`, `last_tick` (its outcome's tick when destroyed or it hit us, else its last sample), `last_s`,
  `last_position`, `approach`, `projected`, `assumed_drift`, `outcome`, `by` (the turret that destroyed it), `hit` and
  `hit_at` (what of ours it hit), `hit_by` [{turret, hits, damage, killed}] (the 3 turrets with most hits on it, from
  their damage events), `velocity`, and `points` [[tick, x, y]] for the first 24 tracked only: the sampling is as it
  was (no new tick work), so the rest have their first and last position.
- Order without a filter: the rarest names first by the watch's own `by_name` seen counts (promethium leads when the
  watch saw any), then by name, then first seen (then unit). `trajectory_page` {page, pages, per_page, total, returned,
  from, to, next, filter, order} says it.
- Read arguments: `asteroid_names` (1..16 names or patterns with `*`, such as `"*promethium*"`; an unknown name or a
  pattern matching no asteroid prototype is refused with the asteroid names), `trajectory_page` (1..),
  `trajectory_limit` (1..100, default 24). They are refused with `seconds` (the start). A picked name's asteroids past
  the cap: `trajectory_untracked` [{name, untracked}] and `trajectory_untracked_lines` ("big-promethium-asteroid: 2 past
  the 3000 tracked: in by_name (seen, destroyed, hit, left the view), no record or trajectory"); a pick with no tracked
  asteroid says so in `trajectory_page.line`.
- A done watch keeps every tracked asteroid's row (`recs` in its job; the per-asteroid working state is dropped as
  before), so a filter reads a done watch too. A watch that ended before this deploy has only its first 24: its read
  says so in `trajectory_note`.

## d24 batch165 QH1 (eng/d20-batch165): platform_plan {phases}, an ordered floor plan played read only (Sol #2223)
- Sol: Asterion's narrow hull 2210 took failed drafts: each floor check saw the marks of the moment, not the floor the
  steps before would leave. What worked (Astra, runs/shift69/team-tools/astra-shift69-narrow-report.md): the live
  marks cancelled, the left 4 support tiles (x -50, y 123..126) and a solid right fill (x 45..53, y 118..137), then
  the left wing and the right columns 53, 52, 51, 50 one at a time.
- floorphases.lua: `phases: [{cancel?, remove?, fill?, name?}]` (1..16), tiles as {x,y}, an area, "x0..x1,y0..y1"
  (inclusive tiles) or "x,y". A model of the floor: its tiles (read as reached), its deconstruction marks and
  foundation tile ghosts within 8 tiles of the phases' tiles, the hub's foundation and room. Each phase: cancel (marks
  and ghosts dropped), remove (floor marked; a ghost dropped), fill (a ghost on empty space; a marked tile kept), then
  the hub's rules (tilecheck.lua) played until nothing changes: every mark, then every ghost, in the order given, then
  each one beside a tile that changed. A marked tile goes with one run of empty space beside it, nothing standing on
  it, room in the hub; a ghost is built with foundation among its 8 neighbours, at most one run beside it, out of
  thruster exhaust, within 200 tiles north of the hub, while the hub holds foundation (a build takes one, a removal
  gives one back). The run count is tilecheck's runs (a test checks all 256 rings).
- Per phase: went, built, marks_waiting, ghosts_unbuilt, waiting and unbuilt ("(x,y): why", 8 each), cut (floor no
  longer joined to the hub's tile by sides, followed 256 tiles; what stands on it), settled, line. After: end
  (removed, added, as areas "x0..x1,y0..y1"), rollback (fill back the removed tiles, then take up the added, played
  the same way from the end: restores and order_checked, else "coordinates only"; its areas are phases input).
- Cost (copy of world n, _autosave9; the read's Lua costs about the same on world n: an 8x8 phase 2.6 ms there, 3.0
  ms on the copy). A rule check or tile read about 10-20 us; a whole-platform search on Asterion 2.5-3 ms; a number in
  a reply about 28 us in helpers.table_to_json (strings next to none, so lists and areas are strings). So the read is a
  job of steps charged in units (a rule check or tile read 1; a list entry walked 0.1-0.2; 4 tiles followed for a cut 1;
  a search the area it looks at / 250): 150 units in the call, then 120 a tick (floorphases.tick; the oldest running
  plan first; 4 kept, phases_check reads them). Areas stay areas until a phase walks them. Measured each tick and call
  (930 ticks of 14 plans, 2 rounds of Sol's five sequences and two 8192-tile plans): the call's own work 0.7-3.2 ms
  (the whole dispatch 4-5 ms); a tick p50 0.6 ms, at most 2.5 ms outside one stretch where every call on the copy ran
  4-5x slower (start calls 19-20 ms instead of 4-5; ticks up to 14.6 ms and one 61 ms); Sol's nine-phase sequence 27
  ticks, about 1.1 ms a tick. Reading a done plan 3.6-4.7 ms. floorphases.tick idle 0.006 ms a tick (profile_ticks 60 s;
  main has none). Bounded: 8192 tiles and 40000 rule checks a plan.
- The support read (platform_plan support: true) took 275 ms on the copy and 388 ms on world n (operator, 13:56); phases
  reads none of its entities (its own model and tilecheck's rules), so batch166's bound of support does not touch it.
- Test: tests/d24_batch165.lua (main has no phases: platform_plan ignores it).

## d24 batch168

- QK1 (operator 14:35; viewer Aurora 14:29: "The same Gemini #2035 handoff repeated four times in 3 minutes. Could these
  share backoff and name Gemini as owner, with a clear cover request?" and "Could routine idle repeats follow actionable
  changes or overdue checkpoints? Honor bounded watches, keep capped fallback checks for unexplained stalls, and
  preserve urgent alerts."), tools/idle_nudge.py:
  - shift70 13:52-14:32: 22 "gemini does not answer" handoffs, one a minute through each of Gemini's pace rests
    (resting.json reason pace, 5 and 10 min), and one for Grok (out of quota). Two causes: a rest of any kind sent a
    handoff whatever the reason the agent was not nudged ("active" while it rested), and the once-only mark was cleared
    on every poll where the agent's last nudge tell had been delivered.
  - A short pace rest (reason pace, at most 30 min) is the agent's own loop pacing its quota: no nudge and no handoff
    during it, its time is not standing, and it is a sign of life as a request of its own is (never "not answering").
  - A handoff is a cover request, once per episode: an episode begins when the agent rests (quota, or a pace rest over
    30 min) or does not answer, and ends when it makes a request of its own. A new episode's handoff waits every_min
    doubled for each handoff already sent for that agent, at most 4 h. Text: "Operator (automatic, facts only): cover
    request. gemini owns #2035, #523 and does not answer (out of quota until 15:59). Asked of you until gemini makes a
    request of its own: cover #2035 and what waits on it; board_update {id: 523, cover: true} for its claim #523 (you
    hear its alerts with gemini). Waiting on it: 2 requests or tells to gemini unanswered (...); 1 board item of
    gemini's (#2035 ...)." The open line's "none (...)" is no item (main read it as one).
  - Idle repeats: the first nudge of an idle stretch (standing since its last work) goes as before; a later one goes on
    an actionable change since the last (a new request or tell to it among the harness's unanswered items, which never
    count the operator's tells; a new mention; a watch newly late, stalled, invalid or with its final unread), at most
    every every_min, else as a fallback at every_min doubled for each nudge of the stretch (40, 80, 160 min, at most
    4 h). nudges.jsonl rows carry `repeat` {n, why}. The not-answering back-off applies as before.
  - A sleep or wait the agent set itself with a known end (idle_report sleep_left_s, action_until_s) holds the nudge
    until it ends, when it began less than idle_min after its last work; back-to-back waits are standing, as in shift07.
  - A running bounded watch (measuring), standing orders and the harness's own alerts and tells are unchanged.

    asteroids (unit numbers), each counted once, first seen after the cap.

    60 over which it fires fewer rounds than a magazine holds, or one shot at most with magazines of 1); rounds are
    each stack's (count - 1) * magazine_size + the top magazine's ammo left (LuaItemStack.ammo). Each read's change
    is split into rounds fired and whole items loaded: unique while the most rounds it can fire between two reads
    (attack_parameters.cooldown with the ammo's cooldown modifier and the force's shooting speed bonus, as
    ammorate.lua) is under the magazine size. World n's gun turrets: cooldown 6 / (1 + 1.5) = 2.4 ticks, at most 7
    rounds in 15 ticks under 10: `exact`. Rocket (27.3 ticks) and railgun (97.1) turrets have magazines of 1: a load
    and a shot between two reads offset each other; with instant ammo (railgun: delivery instant) the turret's hit
    events in that interval count the shot; a rocket's (delivery projectile) hit lands after its flight, often in a
    later interval, so that read is `unsure_reads` and counts none; `rounds_used_most` the most it can have fired.
    Fields: rounds_start, rounds_end, rounds_used, ammo_used (items), ammo_loaded, ammo, reads, every, unsure_reads,
    exact, rounds_used_most; groups add rounds_used and unsure_reads. Electric and fluid turrets have no rounds.
  - `platform_consumed`: each ammo item@quality's consumed count (item production statistics of the platform's surface,
    qflow.count_by at every quality) over the watch, beside the turrets' reads summed (`turrets_used`).

## d24 batch176

- QS1 (Astra #2248: Asterion's explosives line reads stopped at its blocked end (13.5,38.5) while inserters take from
  it before the end). `belt_flow {position, exact_tile: true, seconds?, platform?}` samples the belt at position only:
  its two lanes (a splitter: the half position is in, its input lanes 1,2 or 3,4; an underground: the tile's lanes 1,2),
  no line walked. The default line read is unchanged.
- 2.0.77's LuaTransportLine has no pass count (owner, line_length, total_segment_length, input_lines, output_lines;
  contents reads), so lanes are read by item id, every quarter tile at the belt's speed (4 ticks on a fast belt). An
  item seen on a lane and gone at a later sample left it:
  - `passed_on`: seen on what the tile feeds (the next belt's lines, an underground entrance's own lines 3,4, a
    splitter's lines 5..8);
  - `taken`: gone further from the exit than a sample's travel. A lane's positions count down to its exit (read on
    the copy: an item at 0.94 has just come on, one at 0.00 goes next);
  - `not_seen_after`: gone at the exit and not on what it feeds: taken there or here before a sample saw it.
  Each inserter whose pickup point is on the tile is read each sample: `picked` counts its hand's rises (the game's own
  read), so items it takes in the tick they arrive count there and not in the lane's `taken`. The reply names the tile
  (name, type, direction, unit number, half, underground), `feeds`, per lane `rate`, `left`, `passed_on`, `taken`,
  `not_seen_after`, `entered`, `held`, `held_max`, `state`, and `inserters` [{inserter, picked, rate, items}].
  - output_lines on a 2.0 belt's line names the segment's owner (13.5,28.5 for the tiles at 24.5 and 25.5), not the
    next tile, so the next tile is found by belt_neighbours.
- Verified on a copy of world n's 16:22 autosave (Asterion; the line x 13.5 facing south, full from 24.5 to its end at
  38.5; railgun-ammo assemblers' inserters pick at 25.5, 31.5 and 37.5, and one at (14.5,33.5) picks at 33.5). Each
  inserter's pickups were counted every tick by a separate script, over the same 30 s:
  - (13.5,24.5): 60/min left, 30 items, and the four inserters picked 30 together.
  - (13.5,31.5): right lane 20/min, 4 taken from mid-lane, 6 passed on; left 36/min passed on; its inserter picked 6
    by its hand and by the counter. The inserters downstream picked 24, and 24 passed on.
  - (13.5,37.5), the last one before the end: left lane stopped full; right lane 8/min, 4 taken; its inserter picked 6
    (the counter 6). The end (13.5,38.5) read stopped full on both lanes, and the line read there (73 tiles) read
    stopped with the end backed up.
  - A per-tick trace saw the 25.5 inserter take an item at its tile's 0.81 and 0.31, and one at the exit of (13.5,24.5)

- QAJ1: every filter list (configure, build and place_ghosts `configure`/settings, circuit_set `settings`, an entry's
  top-level `filters`) takes per filter: `"name"` (quality normal, comparator "=", as the game stores a name), 
  `"name@quality"`, `"name@<=quality"` (comparators `=`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`, and the game's signs ≤ ≥ ≠),
  `"name@any"` (no quality: every quality passes), or `{name|item, quality?, comparator?}` (2.0.77's ItemFilter; a
  table with no quality is every quality, as the game takes it). One filter alone is a list of one. Refused before
  anything is set: an unknown item, quality ("unknown quality mythic; qualities: normal, uncommon, rare, epic,
  legendary"; the hidden quality-unknown is not taken), comparator ("unknown comparator =<; comparators: =, !=, <, <=,
  >, >="), a comparator with no quality (the game drops it), `any` with a comparator, an unknown table key.

  placewhy's blueprint comparison) give each filter in the same string form: `plastic-bar`, `plastic-bar@epic`,
  `plastic-bar@<=epic`, `coal@any`. configure reads each slot back and says `not_as_asked` for one that holds other
  than asked.

QR1 (Sol #2337): a queue wait on landed freight from a fixed start. Sol's finite 750 uranium-rounds-magazine pickup
from Kestrel IVb to Aquilo takes longer than wait_until's 54000-tick maximum. pod_landed counted from the wait's first
check. A held wait (`on_timeout: "hold"`) and a requeued one (the queue paused while it ran) went back into pending as

- `wait_until {until: "pod_landed", platform, item?, quality?, at_least?, since_tick?}`: pods sent down from the
  platform that landed on any planet after `since_tick` (a whole tick 0..now), else after the wait's first check.
  Counted from the pod ledger (podlog.lua M.landed_from: the journeys down with that platform name, landed tick after
  the start; a planet's list walked from the newest until a journey sent 36000 ticks before the start). `quality`
  goes with item: that quality only; without it, or with "any", every quality counts.
- saw names the start tick ("since tick T" or "since the wait began (tick T)"), the newest landed pod's tick, pad and
  planet. When a planet's list is full (1000) and its oldest kept journey was sent after the start, saw says so.
- A held wait and a requeued wait keep their start (`pod_since`) and drop id (scheduler.lua hold and pause_inner). A
  failed or replaced wait does not: its saw gives the tick for since_tick in a new step.
- validate_condition checks since_tick and quality at submit and in queue_submit dry_run. On the copy dry_run refused
  since_tick past now, since_tick 5.5, timeout 54001 and quality without item, and took the real step.
- wait_line names "pod_landed ITEM landed from PLATFORM since tick T" (before, "in PLATFORM hub").
- On the copy: Kestrel IVb's last uranium-rounds-magazine pod to Aquilo before the copy landed at 61923898 (200). A
  platform-lane wait with since_tick 61900000 read "1 pod from Kestrel IVb landed since tick 61900000 with 200
  uranium-rounds-magazine (normal quality) (the last at tick 61923898, landing pad (-8,-22) on aquilo)". A
  Kestrel IVc wait held at 120 ticks (start 61972037) and resumed said "since the wait began (tick 61972037)".
- Cost on the copy. The ledger held 3812 journeys (aquilo 654, fulgora 1000, gleba 296, nauvis 1000, vulcanus 862).
  landed_from timed over 100 calls: 0.025 ms a call for start 61943185, 0.038 ms for 61900000, 0.44 ms for 59400000
  (every journey kept). A wait checks every 10 ticks: 0.0025, 0.0038 and 0.044 ms a tick. profile_ticks 60 s before and
  with the wait running: scheduler.wait_until rose from 720 calls / 107.1 ms to 1080 / 160.7 ms (0.149 ms a check,

replaces a watch, and only `{id}` read a full result; a queue step cannot know the id an earlier step's start returned.
- `flight_watch {platform, read: true}`: the force's watch with the highest id kept on that platform (matched by the
  platform's index, else by name for a platform gone), in full as `{id}` reads it, with `older` (the ids of older

  replaces or ends a watch. `{id}`, `{}` and starts are unchanged.

  replace); runtime.lua step_checks.flight_watch runs it at submit and in dry_run, and step_read_check checks the
  platform exists. In a platform lane `{read: true}` takes the lane's platform (queue_lanes.lua, as a start does).

QT3 (Sol #2351): Sol's body plan 768 at 62391635: build steps with wait: true and clear_obstacles: true returned
cleared, mining, then_runs and were marked ok at once. The next step ran while the clearing and its run again were
pending, and the plan ended done with 4 of 132 entities built. Each step's clear call replaced the one job an agent
keeps (clear_jobs by player), so the earlier step's run again was lost.
- runtime busy (scheduler_api): a build or place_ghosts step is running while its clear_obstacles job or its run
  again (then_calls) is pending (clearobs.pending). The run again's reply is kept (clearobs.ran). What it starts
  belongs to the queue, so the step ends when that build ends (its completion and failed entries as before), or at
  once with the reply when it builds at once.
- The step fails, outcome not_run_again with reason and cleared, when the job ends without the run again: the 10-minute
  watch is over ("1 of 1 trees and rocks still stand after 10 min: build not run again"), the run again was refused,
  or another action was running then.
- The run again never starts over another action, direct or queued. The job's own hand-mining construct
  (active.clear_job) does not count. With another action running: "the N trees and rocks in the footprints are gone;
  build not run again: your wait_ticks runs (started after the clear)" in last.cleared.
- queue_status active.continuation: "clear_obstacles: 2 of 2 trees and rocks in the footprints still stand (marked
  Ns ago); build runs again once all are gone (until tick T)", then "the trees and rocks are gone; build runs again
  this tick".
- A pause (a direct body call, queue_pause, a deploy) while the job is pending drops the job and its run again (the
  marks stay) and requeues the step as it was. resumed_from says so. queue_resume runs it again with clear_obstacles.

  `M.POSITIONS_MAX`, `M.TYPES_MAX`, `M.ITEMS_MAX`, `M.NAMES_MAX`, `M.LIST_NAMES`, `M.VIA_POINTS`, `M.ENTRIES_MAX`, ...;

  observe's entity and tile names (a queued observe reads a platform or a scope, which take none); fields inside list
  entries (stops[i].save_as, a schedule's records). The step label (64 bytes) was already checked at submit.

  1.2, epic 1.3, legendary 1.5); its minimum range is the prototype's at every quality. Measured on a copy of world n
  (d25 13:03 save), a turret of ours and an enemy gun turret as target past its prototype's range, 240-300 ticks:
  gun 23 tiles, laser 31, rocket 45, railgun 50 (powered), tesla 38, flamethrower 38: the legendary turret destroyed
  the target and the normal one did not fire; legendary rocket, flamethrower and railgun turrets fired at 18, 7.5 and
  4.5 tiles (inside 1.5 times their minimum range), a legendary railgun not at 2.5. ammorate's note said an electric
  turret's quality left its range unchanged; corrected (and agent/ref/space-age.md).
- platform_defense: turret rows give `quality`, `range` (at the quality) and `base_range` (the prototype's); the
  collectors, the hull's sides, the lines (nearest ... past its range) and the planned read use the range at the
  quality; a turret above normal is named with it in the lines (`rare laser-turret (-46,-50)`). Planned ghosts: the
  quality the ghost builds. The asteroid watch's turret rows add `base_range` (their `range` was already at the
  quality, batch200). The route damage and platform_endurance's forecast use no range (unchanged).
- inspect of a turret (built or ghost): `range`, `base_range`, `min_range` (platdefense.lua `M.reach`).
- defense (areas' cover) and flamers (the arc's reach) on planets, danger's egg-site cover (its find now 60 tiles, a
  legendary railgun's range) and damagelog's "its range R" use the range at the quality. Not changed: census's base
  map turret circles (prototype range; no turret above normal on a planet of world n's 13:03 save), artillery.

  for the hull's check already) and the multiplier once per quality. On the copy, Asterion's full read by part, main

## d25 batch210 (QW1, Sol #2368: belt_flow undercounts a lane where an inserter picks)
- Sol's uranium line ends at (92.5,-82.5) (a transport belt facing east), where a bulk inserter at (92.5,-81.5)
  picks. The line read (every 16 ticks) gave 276.8 + 99.6/min there. exact_tile (every 8) saw 446-458/min leave
  the lanes, and the inserter's hand counted 736-750/min (the source made about 748).
- Measured on a copy of world n (d25 14:06 save), 2.0.77, straight lines on a test surface, one tile read each tick:
  - The time between two items on a full lane: transport belt 8 ticks (200 of 200), fast 4, express 2 or 3
    (67 and 132 of 199 gaps), turbo 2. An item is first seen one tick's travel onto the tile (0.969 on a transport
    belt, 0.875 turbo).
  - A bulk inserter (rotation 0.04 a tick) at the end of a line, picking into a chest, sampled every 1, 2, 4, 8 and
    16 ticks over 30 s:
    - Transport belt, one lane (450/min, the inserter waiting for items): 225 picked. Every 1 or 2 ticks saw all
      225 on the tile; every 4, 8 and 16 saw 36. The hand count read 225 at every interval up to 8 and 224 at 16.
    - Turbo belt, one lane (the inserter the limit): 396 picked. On the tile at any tick: 194, at every 2 ticks 177,
      4: 153, 8: 141, 16: 131. The hand count read 396 up to every 8 ticks and 345 at 16 (a half swing is 12.5
      ticks: a hand that fills and drops between two samples is missed).
  - An inserter can take an item in the tick it comes onto the tile, so no sample interval sees every item taken
    there. A hand holds what it picked from its last pickup until it drops it, at least half a turn later
    (0.5 / rotation speed: 12 ticks for fast, bulk and stack inserters at normal quality, 5 at legendary; 35 for
    an inserter).
- belt_flow (line read) now finds the inserters whose pickup point is on each sampled tile (a splitter point: its
  left half, the half lanes 1,2 run on), once at the start, and reads their hands each sample. Such a point adds
  `inserters` [{inserter, picked, rate, items}], `picked`, `passed_on` (items gone from the tile and seen on what it
  feeds at that sample: the next belt, an underground entrance's own lines, a splitter's outputs) and `lanes_rate`
  (left + right, the old rate); its `rate` is passed_on + picked a minute, and its line adds "N/min through it: N seen
  next on X + N picked by the inserters picking from it (...)". `merges` sums use that rate. Lanes add `entered`
  (new on the lane after the first sample). `limit` still reads the lanes.
- The interval: half the ticks an item takes to cross a tile on the fastest belt sampled, as before (every item that
  crosses a sampled tile is on it for two samples; 16 ticks on a transport belt). Where an inserter picks from a
  sampled tile it is at most the item spacing (8, 4, 2, 2) and at most the half swing of every such inserter.
  exact_tile was already at the item spacing and now also takes the half swing; it adds `through` and
  `through_rate` (passed_on + picked where inserters pick from the tile, else left) and a line "through the tile".
- Each result's note names what each count can miss: a lane's rate misses an item taken off the tile before a
  sample sees it; picked counts those and misses what anything else takes (a character, a loader); passed_on misses
  an item taken on the next tile before a sample sees it there; entered misses what is taken before a sample sees it.
- On the copy (bot sol, `belt_flow {surface: nauvis, position: (91.5,-82.5), seconds: 30}`): main 272.4 + 106.6/min
  (every 16, 20 samples, 5 s); this runtime every 8 ticks, left 188/min + right 144/min on the lanes, "746/min through

## d25 batch212 (QX1, Sol #2372: flight_watch ammunition used per part)
- Trial190 (Asterion, aquilo -> solar-system-edge -> aquilo): #1296 watched from the departure (began 63165231),
  #1297 from now at the turnaround (63263001). Hub deltas and uptime gave no exact whole-trip uranium magazine count;
  flight_watch counted repair packs only.
- flightwatch.lua reads the platform's item production statistics (`get_output_count`, consumed; a turret's shots
  count there) of `M.AMMO` (uranium-rounds-magazine, firearm-magazine, piercing-rounds-magazine, rocket,
  explosive-rocket, railgun-ammo) at every quality: at a window's start and end, at each sample while it watches,
  and at each sample while armed and stopped.
- Read fields:
  - `ammunition` {from_tick, to_tick, ticks, total, used {item: {quality: n}}}: the window, from its start to its end
    (or now). Each `mixed.parts` entry keeps its own `ammunition` and `repair_packs_used` (mixed.lua part()).
  - `ammunition_watch`: from the tick the watch began, across its mixed splits (also the parts mixed.lua drops past 3).
  - `ammunition_chain` (also `watches`, `first`, `more`): a start with `replace: true` carries the replaced watch's
    chain on: from the first watch's start to this one's end, gaps between watches included. With no watch counting
    (the old one done and read), `replace: true` chains to the platform's newest kept watch that is done. At most
    `M.CHAIN` (8) ids are named; the count always runs from the first.
  - `ammunition_boundaries` [{what, from_tick, to_tick, ticks, total, used, line}]: `departure` (from the last armed
    sample that read it stopped to the first that read it flying: before the watch began, in no count), `arrival`
    (from the last sample that read it flying to the end: in the last window), `between` (a replaced watch's end to
    the next one's start: in the chain only), `start` (a watch begun from now while flying).
  - The line adds "ammunition used ..." (and the whole watch's and the chain's); the end's team.alerts line adds the
    window's. A watch begun before this runtime reads "ammunition used ?"; a replace of one says
    `ammunition_chain_note`.
- Tests: tests/d25_batch212.lua (fails on main: an armed watch reads nothing).
- On a copy of world n (d25 16:24 save, tick 63358761):
  - Watches started from now on Swiftlet, Anvil and Kestrel IVb ended at their arrivals with, for example, #1306
    (Swiftlet) firearm-magazine 8 from tick 63369212 to 63372844, and the arrival between 63372784 and 63372844, none
    used. A running watch on Weaver read 110 firearm magazines at tick 63433586; a direct read of the statistics in the
    same command, less the watch's start read, gave 110.
  - profile_ticks {seconds: 60}, part flightwatch.tick: 3 watching + 1 armed: main 23.6 ms (232 calls), this runtime
    46.4 ms (236) with qflow.count_by reads; 1 armed (Asterion): main 1.87 ms (60 calls, median 0.029 ms a second),
    this runtime 5.46 ms with the read as shipped (median 0.084 ms). A read alone, 100 in one command: 0.016 ms
    (qflow.count_by's 0.044 ms fetched get_output_count for each count).

## d25 batch216 (QAA1, Astra 20:09: where Asterion's foundation went; QAA2, Astra 20:59: ghosts name takes a tile)
- Flight 205's return: Asterion's hub foundation fell 154 -> 153 -> 148 between ticks 63979515 and 64022118. Watch
  #1304 recorded no entity hits, losses or repairs; no ghosts were open at 64024909; supply read 0 foundation made or
  used.
- Engine facts (2.0.77), measured on a copy of world n's 20:02 save (tick 64007786, Asterion flying
  solar-system-edge -> aquilo). Asteroids were made by script at its bare front edge, and level-script handlers
  recorded every event and each tick's hub foundation, foundation tiles and tile ghosts:
  - An asteroid that enters the foundation destroys every foundation tile under its collision box at once:
    - small (box 1x1): 2 tiles;
    - medium (2x2): 3 tiles;
    - big (4x4): 5 tiles, and 5 more each tile it went on (40 in 8 rows from tick 64018232 to 64018380).
  - The asteroid takes no damage from the tiles; the small one slowed from 0.050 to 0.039 tiles a tick.
  - LuaSpacePlatform.damaged_tiles stays empty: tiles go whole.
  - No event fires for the destruction: no tile event, no on_entity_died or on_entity_damaged, and no platform event.
    2.0.77 has no tile-destruction event.
  - On the same tick the game puts a tile ghost on each destroyed tile: ghost_name space-platform-foundation, force
    player, last_user nil, quality normal.
  - The hub builds the ghosts from its own foundation, one tile a build, with the hub's count 1 lower each:
    - 153 -> 113 for 40 tiles;
    - the first build 63 to 168 ticks after the ghosts appeared.
  - Each build raises on_space_platform_built_tile: tile and item space-platform-foundation, the quality, and tiles
    with old_tile empty-space and the tile's whole-number position.
  - The platform's item production statistics read foundation made 0 and used 0 throughout.
- flightwatch.lua: each window (and each `mixed.parts` entry) has `foundation`:
  - destroyed, rebuilt, destroyed_between_finds, rebuilt_from_before, open;
  - placed, placed_built, open_placed, removed;
  - taken {quality: n}, taken_total, hub_foundation {start, end};
  - first and last destroyed ticks, rows [{tick, what, count, at, from_tick}], rows_more, skipped_finds,
    builds_heard;
  - the line adds "foundation: N tiles destroyed (ticks a to b), N rebuilt by the platform, N foundation taken from
    the hub by its tile builds, N destroyed not rebuilt yet; hub foundation a -> b".
- How the watch finds the ghosts:
  - The watch makes one find of the platform's tile ghosts at a sample: every `M.FLOOR_TICKS` (300) while the
    platform's builds are heard, else each sample.
  - The find is limited to the chunks that held foundation when the watch began (one tile count a chunk, once a
    watch), widened by each build heard.
  - It reads at most `M.FLOOR_SCAN` (512); a find that meets more reads none of them and counts in skipped_finds.
  - A foundation ghost new since the last find counts as placed when the ghost log names a placer, else destroyed.
    A placer is:
    - a record kept with this ghost's unit number;
    - the game's last user (a player);
    - or an older record placed after the last find.
  - A record placed earlier is of a ghost once built there: the hull's own pasted tiles.
  - Ghosts aboard when the watch begins count as placed only with their own record or a player's.
  - A seen ghost gone since is rebuilt (foundation there now) or removed.
- How the platform's builds are read:
  - The platform's builds come from on_space_platform_built_tile (`M.on_built_tile`) at their tick and quality.
  - A build where no find saw a ghost counts as destroyed and built between two finds, or as placed when its record
    is newer than the last find or it lay outside the chunks searched.
  - Without the event (an older control.lua), each sample's find reads the builds, and the line says so.
- The platform read (`platforms {platform}`) gains `foundation_lost`:
  - the event's builds on that platform since the record began (`M.floor_read`; storage `floorlog`), as rebuilt
    (ghosts no one placed) and placed_built;
  - taken by quality, and the last 8 rows;
  - the foundation ghosts aboard now, with and without a placer;
  - builds_heard.
- ghostlog.lua:
  - A tile ghost's record keeps its unit number (`u`). `owner`/`owner_at` skip a record kept with another ghost's
    unit number, and return the record's tick and whether it was kept with the ghost's own unit number.
  - `forget_tile` drops a tile's record once its tile is built.
  - Before this, a destroyed hull tile's new ghost read as placed by whoever pasted the hull; removeghosts.lua reads
    the same owner.
- control.lua forwards `on_space_platform_built_tile`. This is a mod update: control.lua takes effect when world n
  restarts with the new mod folder. A runtime deploy alone gives the sample-read counts.
- Tests: tests/d25_batch216.lua (tests/d25batch216.test.ts). It fails on main: a watch has no `foundation`.
- On the copy, the branch runtime with the new control.lua, watch #1307 on Asterion:
  - Astra placed 2 foundation ghosts (place_ghosts) at tick 64020720, and a medium asteroid struck at the front edge.
  - The read gave destroyed 3 at 64020771 (from 64020720), placed 2 and placed_built 2 at 64020784/85, and rebuilt
    3 at 64020787, 64020815 and 64020816.
  - Taken: normal 5; hub foundation 78 -> 73. `foundation_lost` agreed.
  - With the old control.lua (watch #1306, a find each sample), a big asteroid gave destroyed 28 (ticks 64020051 to
    64020171) and rebuilt 28 read by the finds; hub foundation 108 -> 78, 30 taken, the 2 more from ghosts open
    before the watch began.
- Cost on the copy (world n's 20:02 save, Asterion, the largest platform: 402 chunks on its surface, 40 holding
  foundation, 22015 tiles):
  - One find a second, 30 of them in a level-script handler:
    - within the 40 hull chunks: 0.67 ms each;
    - over the whole surface: 1.02 ms each.
  - In loops of 20, the same finds took 0.25 and 0.33 ms, and a count 0.43 ms.
  - Finding the hull's chunks: 4.6 ms, once a watch.
  - profile_ticks {seconds: 60}, part flightwatch.tick, watch #1309 on Asterion. The same runtime ran with the watch's
    foundation reading off and on in turn (`w.fl` set aside):

    | Pair | off (median / mean ms) | on (median / mean ms) |
    |---|---|---|
    | 1 | 0.736 / 0.928 | 0.685 / 0.891 |
    | 2 | 0.661 / 0.824 | 0.701 / 1.319 |

  - With a find every sample (before FLOOR_TICKS): off median 0.579 ms, on median 1.476 ms.
  - Main's runtime with a watch on Asterion: median 0.584 ms.
  - A big asteroid's 20 rebuilds in 40 s:
    - part flightwatch.built_tile 4.47 ms (0.22 ms a build);
    - event on_space_platform_built_tile 13.7 ms (0.69 ms a build, the forwarded event whole).
- QAA2 (Astra 20:59): `ghosts {name}` takes a tile name.
  - The game's `ghost_name` filter knows entity names only. Before this change, `name: "space-platform-foundation"`
    was refused "Unknown entity name: space-platform-foundation", while an unfiltered read listed the ghosts
    (tile: true, item, hub_holds).
  - A name that is a tile prototype (and no entity) now finds the tile ghosts and keeps those of that name.
  - A name that is neither is refused: "name: no entity or tile is named X".
  - On the copy, after a strike: 3 foundation ghosts listed.
  - Tested in tests/d25_batch216.lua (its QAA2 part fails on main with the game's refusal).

## d25 batch213 (QY1, operator 17:47: an agent whose quota rest ends is resumed in its pane)
- Shift76: Muse rested on its weekly limit until Sun 17:00. From 17:00 its CLI showed "Usage limit reached ... Send a

  stopped at its prompt never reads. tools/supervise.sh typed nothing: herdr reads Muse's pane as "working" from its
  launch on (revision 1, 14:31 to 17:46). The operator typed a message into the pane at 17:44.
- tools/pane_resume.py, run by tools/idle_nudge.py at each poll. When a rest's `until` passes (runs/RUN/AGENT/
  resting.json, any reason), it acts once in the agent's pane (panes.txt):
  - muse, claude, codex: one message, "Operator (automatic): your quota rest ended at Sun 17:00, when your usage limit
    was due to reset. Continue the shift from notes.md and your inbox (./fh tells)." Sent with `herdr agent prompt`,
    or `herdr pane send-text` and `send-keys enter` where herdr refuses the pane as an agent (Muse).
  - grok, with its limit dialog up ("You hit your weekly limit.", 1 Buy more credits, 2 Try Again): `down` when Buy
    more credits is highlighted, then `enter` only when the screen's colours show Try Again highlighted (bold) and Buy
    more credits not. Otherwise nothing is pressed and the next nudge tries again. Without the dialog: a message.
  - agy: nothing typed. The loop sleeps until the reset and ends the rest itself (agy-quota.py --woke). A resting.json
    still there a minute after `until` is logged once.
  Then it logs the resume and ends the rest (resting.json to resting-last.json; the runtime hears done, as
  tools/quota_rest.py --done does). A rest the agent already ended with a request of its own is cleared, nothing typed.
- Never into a pane mid-turn: nothing is typed while the screen's last 25 lines show a turn running ("esc to
  interrupt" for Muse, Claude Code and Codex; Grok's "[stop]"), while herdr reads the pane working (claude, codex,
  grok; Muse's status is ignored, see above), or within 2 min of a request of its own in the journal. It waits for the
  next poll and logs the wait once.
- A minute after it types: a request of its own since, or a turn running, is logged as resumed. The CLI's limit text
  after the message (or Grok's dialog still up) is logged once, and it types again at the next nudge (--every-min
  after the last try) until the CLI moves or the deadline passes.
- Logs: rows {"resume": true, "action": typed | waiting | still_at_limit | resumed | cleared | loop | ...} in
  runs/RUN/nudges.jsonl, and "resume NAME: ..." lines in idle-nudge.log. --dry-run reads the panes and types nothing.
- Limit texts matched: Muse "Usage limit reached" (shift76's screen); Claude Code "You've hit your limit · resets ..."
  (its API error rows); Codex "Usage limit reached. You've reached your usage limit" (the 0.164.0 binary); Grok "You
  hit your weekly limit." and the dialog's "Resubmit the last prompt once you have usage again" (1.0.70, the d24 capture).
- Test: tools/test_pane_resume.py, with fake panes and fixed times. It replays shift76's Muse screen and also covers
  mid-turn panes, Grok's dialog (Enter never on Buy more credits), Claude, Codex, agy, a dry run and the deadline. It
  fails on main (no tools/pane_resume.py). Under POG_TEST=1, HerdrPanes refuses (docs/TESTS-LIVE.md).

## d25 batch214 (QZ1, Sol #2379: uptime rows in pages; QZ2, Astra #2380: limits dry_run missed)
- QZ1. Sol's 600 s Asterion watch of 20 machines gave `machine_rows` as text above 16 (uptime.ROWS: 64 rows of 15
  fields took 23 ms to encode on a copy), so the coal and sulfur shortage counters of each machine could not be compared.
  - `uptime {read: true, page?, page_size?, positions?, id?, details?}` (uptime.lua M.read) reads a watch and never
    starts or replaces one (M.starts is false with read). Rows are M.machine_row's (now apart from M.result) or
    M.lab_row's for the page's machines only, with `index` and `short_counts` {ingredient: {samples, least, need,
    first_tick, last_tick}}; `details: true` keeps each row's `line` and adds `lines`. `positions` picks machines (the
    nearest centre within M.MATCH 2 tiles a side; `not_found`), `id` `uptime@START_TICK` any agent's (`agent` names
    the owner; only the owner's read marks a done one read). A done watch counts to `ended_tick` (set when it ends) or
    `until_tick`, so a late read gives its final numbers. The default `uptime {}` is unchanged.
  - Checked with no world (M.check_read): read true; not with seconds, area, items, position, surface, platform,

## d25 batch215 (QZ3, Sol #2388: uptime ids collided across agents)
- Cause: a watch's id was `KIND@START_TICK` (measures.lua). Sol's 13-machine and Astra's 41-machine uptime watches
  began on tick 63906911 (both aligned to trial 205), so both were `uptime@63906911`, and batch214's read by id gave
  the reader's own first.
- Ids: `measures.id(kind, job, index)` gives `KIND@START_TICK/AGENT` (the owner's name, board.who), kept on the watch
  (`job.id`) once the name is known; a watch begun before this runtime gets it on its first read. Every measures kind
  uses it: uptime, turret_tally, belt_flow, collector_tally, asteroid_watch, signal_watch (status work, the idle
  count's `measuring`, the sleep line, sleep_check, flags). signal_watch's own replies and uptime's start reply give
  it (`api.watch_id`). With no owner name known, `KIND@START_TICK`, not kept.
- uptime read: `agent` (a name; `@` and `pog-` dropped, any case) reads that agent's watch; `id`
  `uptime@START_TICK/AGENT` reads that one; `uptime@START_TICK` reads the one watch begun on that tick, and two or more
  are refused with each id and its machine count named, the reader's own among them. An id or agent with no match is
  refused with the kept watches named. `id` and `agent` without `read: true` are refused (the call, submit and
  dry_run: uptime.check_read). id: up to 96 characters; agent: 1..64.
- Not affected: flight_watch (`flight#N`) and delivery_watch (`#N`) number their watches from one counter each
  (state().flightwatch.seq, delivwatch.seq) shared by every agent; launch watches and ghost tallies give no id.
- Cost: idle_tick asked measures.running every tick for every agent, and it built `kind .. '@' .. job.start` for each
  agent with a running watch. On the copy that took 7.0 µs a call; reading the kept id takes 0.02 µs, and making it the
  first time 0.41 µs. With Sol and Astra running watches on the copy, that is about 14 µs a tick less.
- On the copy (world n's 19:46 save, tick 63953710): the runtime on world n read Sol's 13 machines for
  `uptime@63906911`; this runtime refused it naming `uptime@63906911/astra (41 machines), uptime@63906911/sol (13

## d26 batch225 (QR, Sol #2413: a finished uptime watch unreadable once its agent began another)
- Cause: the uptime store held one watch an agent; a new start overwrote it, done or not. Astra's 41-machine
  uptime@65848202/astra could not be read once Astra began uptime@65920807.
- uptime.lua `M.keep`: a new watch keeps the agent's previous one as a done watch. One still running is finished at
  that tick as `close` does (its final made, `closed_by` "finished Ns early: a new watch began"). Its entity refs are
  dropped and it is never sampled (the tick walks the store's watches only). Its final keeps groups, flows, research
  and silo figures; its lines and rows are left out, since a page read makes them again from its machines.
- Bounds: at most `KEPT` 4 kept watches, their machines (their segments' included) together at most `KEPT_MACHINES`
  96; past that the oldest goes, the newest always kept. Each drop is logged on the new watch's `kept_dropped` (the
  last `DROPPED` 8: id, machines, dropped_tick, by, why). A watch begun on the same tick holds nothing and is not kept.
- Reads: `uptime {read: true, id}` (any agent) reads a kept watch in pages, with `kept_watch` {kept_tick, ended_tick,
  closed_by, by}; its segments read by their ids. `uptime {}` and the paged read of the current watch list `kept`
  [{id, started_tick, ended_tick, seconds, samples, machines, segments, closed_by, kept_tick}], `kept_dropped` and
  `kept_note`. The start reply gives `kept`, `dropped` (this start's drops), a `replaced` that names the kept id, and
  the line names both. A read of a dropped id says when, by which start and why, and lists what is kept.
- mixed.lua: a split marks the old watch `splitting` around its restart, so the restart carries the kept watches on
  and keeps no copy of it; `close` keeps it as a segment as before.
- Storage (the copy, world n's 14:06 save, astra's watch of Nauvis (0,52)-(100,100): 41 machines, 71 samples): the kept watch
  is 30,234 bytes as a serpent line (machines 28,245, its slimmed final 1,481); with its final whole it was 52,181
  (lines 19,047, group_lines 2,874). A kept 58-machine watch (85 samples): 47,116. At the bounds an agent keeps about
  66-76 KB.
- Tests: tests/d26_batch225.lua (in lua.test.ts), failing on main; tests/d25_batch215.lua now expects uptime@1000 to
  name two watches (Astra's earlier one is kept).

  margin use movement + drift (at rest none, as before). The result adds `moving` {reads, of_reads, from_tick,
  to_tick, speed_max_km_s, drift_max (tiles a second)}; the line adds "the platform moved at N of M reads (ticks A-B,

  per planet with no destination still in flight (the other unlanded rows were pods sent in the last 35 s).
- The game's rule (the copy of world n's 07:31 save, 2.0.77; test platforms at Nauvis and a silo with both switches
  off unless named):
  - A rocket holding a starter pack launches on its own the tick it is ready (the next tick when it is ready already),
    whatever the silo's automatic requests and send to orbit automatically, while one of our platforms waits for a pack
    at that planet (waiting_for_starter_pack). It goes to the waiting one with the lowest index: 53 over 54 and 55, 56
    over 57, 57 over 58, 60 over 62. Indices are never reused (a deleted platform's index stayed free), so that is the
    one made first.
  - A launch ordered in the tick the pack goes in comes first: a platform named gets it (61 over 60), orbit loses it
    (the pod is gone after its ascent, no delivery, the platform still waits), no destination sends it back down to
    the planet's landing pad. load_silo with launch loads and launches in one tick; a launch call after a transfer
    finds the rocket gone.
  - With none waiting the pack stays aboard; automatic requests switched on then move it to the trash slots. With one
    waiting, automatic requests switched on keep it aboard and it launches to that platform when ready (the platform
    reads starter_pack_requested first). Silos with automatic requests and packs in their network claim waiting
    platforms on their own (the copy's Nauvis silos started three test platforms).
  - A starter pack pod: on_rocket_launch_ordered with destination space_platform (the platform), then
    on_cargo_pod_finished_ascending about 1650 ticks later; in that tick the platform turns paused with its hub built
    and on_cargo_pod_delivered_cargo fires (the destination now reads invalid); the pod is invalid the next tick. No
    on_cargo_pod_finished_descending.
  - game.get_entity_by_unit_number finds no cargo pod in 2.0.77 (every pod on every surface, any state, read nil).
- podlog.lua: an up pod with destination space_platform names that platform ("vulcanus to Aethera (its starter
  pack)", `starter_pack`), one to orbit reads "to orbit". A delivery with no landing closes the journey as landed then
  (a starter pack: "landed in platform X (its starter pack: the platform starts, its hub built)"); a row kept before
  this with `delivered` and no landing (#20903) reads landed at that tick. Each open journey keeps its pod; once a
  second (SWEEP 60, only while one is open) a journey whose pod is invalid closes: "pod gone by tick T, Ns after it
  was sent, no landing recorded", with "(a pod sent to orbit is removed there with its cargo)" or, for a starter pack
  whose platform has no hub, "X reads <state>"; one whose platform has its hub reads landed. A journey opened before
  this runtime (no pod kept) takes its pod from its next pod event, else ends as before after OPEN_TICKS.
- starterpack.lua: the tick each platform was made (platform_create, the chronicle's once-a-second look; platforms
  made before from the chronicle's kept platform_created events, else "made before tick N"), the platforms waiting at
  a planet in the game's order, with how long each has waited. Lines:
  - platform_create: `starter_queue` when 2 or more of ours wait at that planet (names, ages, which one a pack goes to).
  - a transfer of a pack into a rocket, load_silo, the silo read and settings (configure, launch): `starter_pack`
    "the rocket holds space-platform-starter-pack*1, which launches on its own once the rocket is ready, whatever the
    silo's switches, to Aethera (waiting ...), the first made of ours waiting for one at vulcanus; also waiting: ...",
    or with none waiting "it stays aboard (automatic requests on: the trash slots)".
  - launch with a pack aboard: `starter_pack` "<pack> starts Loom", "goes to X's hub as cargo" or "is lost in orbit".
  - platforms: a waiting platform has no surface, so the compact read left it out; it now has a line (and a full row
    `starter_pack`): where it waits, how long, and which of ours waiting there gets the next pack.
- Step 3, the refusal at 66352254 ("...that no platform stopped above asks this planet for... the game moves it into
  the silo's trash slots"): wrong while a platform of ours waits there. silo.trash_risk keeps a pack out of the lost
  cargo then (`starter_pack` on the risk, the line says where it goes), so launch {auto_requests: true} and load_silo's
  restore of automatic requests go ahead, and cargo_to_trash leaves the pack out. With none waiting it is refused as
  before.
- Cost (profile_ticks 60 s on the copy, the save's runtime then this one, 5-6 journeys open): podlog.tick ran 7 times
  for 0.29 ms in all before, 68 times for 1.56 ms after (at most 0.12 ms in a game second): the sweep adds about
  0.02 ms a second.
- Checked through fh on the copy: Loom's compact line and full row, platform_create's starter_queue, the silo read and
  launch {auto_requests: true} with a pack in a rising rocket (switched on, settings.starter_pack names T229s), the
  pod's ledger row ("nauvis to T229s (its starter pack) ... landed in platform T229s ..."), row #20903, and Sol's
  transfer of a pack into silo (14.5,140.5) naming Loom.
- Docs: agent/ref/space-age.md (platform_create).
- Tests: tests/d26_batch229.lua (in lua.test.ts).
## d26 batch230 (SF, Sol #2425: fresh stock snapshots at 5 s)
- Cause: supply keeps a read 10 s (supply.lua M.reuse, REUSE_TICKS 600). Sol's recorder read
  `supply {surface: "platform-16", item: "explosives", belt_positions: true}` (Asterion) every 5 s, so every other
  frame was the read before: 7 unique of 13 at 66415490..66419090.
- The supply read's cost, on a private copy of world n's 07:31 save (each read uncached; a measuring copy with the
  reuse off):
  - Asterion (platform-16; 7460 buildings in the census, 7716 entities found): 34-40 ms a call (the first 84), reply
    8.9 KB. Profile parts a read: supply.scan 23.7 ms (supply.find 4.6, supply.belts 8.3, supply.inserters 1.0,
    supply.crafters 0.4, sorting the found entities by type ~9), the rest of the read (belt lines and positions, machines,
    lines) ~8.6, board.team 1.7,
    platalerts.lines 0.7, encode 0.45.
  - Nauvis, the same item: 184-204 ms a call, reply 6.2 KB. supply.scan 179 ms (supply.find 33, supply.stock 55,
    supply.chests 19, supply.requesters 11, supply.inserters 9, supply.belts 9, supply.robots 5, supply.crafters 4).
  - So a fresh supply read every 5 s (a `fresh: true`) would cost 35 ms each on Asterion: the lean stock read instead.
- `supply {item, stock: true}` (whole surface): the item's count there by place, read now and never reused: `stock`
  true, `read` "fresh", `read_tick`, `as_of`, `total`, `where` (the same text as supply's `where`) and `places`
  (`{label: count}` for the places holding it: belts, requester chests, ..., machine outputs, users' inputs, inserter
  hands, robots, fuel slots, on the ground, characters), `counted`, `next_tick`.
  - The counts are the supply scan's own (opts.stock leaves out spots, spoilage, logistic networks, chests' orphan
    requests, belt tiles and inserter targets), so the same total and places as `where`. On the copy at one tick:
    stock and supply both `2732: belts 2650, machine outputs 24, users' inputs 42, inserter hands 16`, and again at
    66384739 (2731). Normal quality, as `where`; on the ground from the ground watch's last pass, as `where`. In-orbit
    hubs and placed vehicles are not added (supply's text adds them after `where`'s total).
  - One read an agent a 5 s (300 ticks) for the same surface and item: sooner is refused, `stock: one read a 5 s for
    the same surface and item; yours of explosives on platform-16 was at tick N; the next from tick N+300 (in 5.0 s)`.
    A refused call takes no read. Another agent or item reads now.
  - Size: a platform of at most 10000 buildings and a planet of at most 2500, by the census's count of the surface
    (census.lua M.surface_buildings: the snapshot types, ours); a planet the census has not counted yet is refused, a
    platform not counted is read. Refusal: `stock reads a platform of at most 10000 buildings, a planet of at most
    2500; the census counts 49944 on nauvis. supply {item, surface} reads it (reused within 10 s)`.
  - Not with near, radius, belt_positions, belt_tiles, all_stopped, makers, consumers, from, requesters or split; not
    for a fluid. compact leaves a stock reply as it is.
  - On a platform the stock read finds each group of types apart (a find per group): on Asterion the finds cost what
    one does and the 9 ms of sorting one find's entities by type is left out. On a planet a find per group cost
    1.6-2.2 times one find (Vulcanus 39-43 ms against 25), so planets keep the one find.
- Cost of a stock read on the copy (a call, reply blocks included; five agents at one paused tick):
  - Asterion 16-20 ms (the supply read at the same tick: 34.9 ms, 9.0 KB). Parts a read: supply.scan 14.1 ms
    (supply.find 7.2, supply.belts 5.8, supply.crafters 0.33, supply.inserters 0.30), board.team 2.5,
    platalerts.lines 0.9, encode 0.27. Reply: the stock fields 0.7 KB, 0.9-1.4 KB with clock and team lines.
  - platform-4 (1509 buildings): 5.1-5.8 ms. Aquilo (587): 6.4-6.5 ms (supply 15.9). Fulgora (3836): 21-25 ms
    (supply 32). Gleba (4265): 19-20 ms (supply 22). Nauvis (49944): about 60 ms of reads (find 34, belts 18,
    robots 3, hands 2, chests 2; probe), refused. Fit: platforms about 2.3 ms + 1.9 us a building, planets 3.9 ms +
    4.5 us: the caps are about 21 ms and 15 ms.
  - At 5 s on Asterion: 17 ms every 5 s, against the supply read's 35 ms every 10 s the recorder costs now.
- Every supply reply (the plain read and `requesters`) now says `read`: "fresh" (read now) or "reused" (the same read
  within 10 s), and `read_tick`: the tick it was read (compact keeps both). For existing callers nothing else changed:
  the reuse (10 s, the same key) and `as_of`'s text are as before.
- Test: tests/d26_batch230.lua (in lua.test.ts), failing on main.
